semin-durr:9-9.t: The words of the Exalted: {إِنَّهُمْ سَآءَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ}: [ساء] may be taken in its basic usage, as a fully conjugable transitive verb whose mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. "what they used to do grieved them", or "their deeds [grieved them]"; or it may be treated like بئس, so that it is converted to the pattern فَعُل with ḍamma, ceases to be conjugable and comes to express blame, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, as has been established more than once.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَئِمَّةَ الكفر}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «أئمة» with two hamzas, the second of them softened "between-between" (bayna bayna), with no alif between them. The Kufans and Ibn Dhakwān from Ibn ʿĀmir pronounce both of them fully (taḥqīq) without inserting an alif between them, and Hishām likewise, except that he inserted an alif between them. This is what is well known among the seven readers; some of it is open to discussion, which will come, if Allah the Exalted wills. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] reported from Nāfiʿ and those with him that they change the second into a pure yāʾ, and that a lengthening (madd) between them, i.e. between the hamza and the yāʾ, has been transmitted from Nāfiʿ.
As for the reading with full pronunciation (taḥqīq) and with "between-between", a group of grammarians judged it weak, such as Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and his followers; and among the readers too there are those who judged the taḥqīq weak, even though they transmitted it and taught it to their students. Some of them rejected the "between-between" softening and did not teach it to the people of softening, but read with a light yāʾ bearing kasra; they stated this explicitly in their books.
As for the reading with yāʾ, it is the one that al-Fārisī and this group approved, because pronouncing two hamzas in one word is heavy, and the "between-between" hamza has the weight of the full one. Al-Zamakhsharī declared the reading with a pure yāʾ to be a solecism (laḥn), and [said] that pronouncing both hamzas fully is not accepted by the Basrans. He said: "If you ask: how is «أئمة» pronounced? I say: with a hamza followed by a 'between-between' hamza, i.e. between the articulation point of the hamza and that of the yāʾ. Pronouncing both hamzas fully is a well-known reading, even if it is not accepted by the Basrans. As for pronouncing the yāʾ explicitly, it cannot be, and whoever reads so commits a solecism and a distortion." The Shaykh said: "That is his habit of accusing the readers of solecism. How can it be a solecism, when the head of the Basran grammarians, Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, read with it, as did the reader of the people of Mecca, Ibn Kathīr, and the reader of the people of Medina, Nāfiʿ?" I say: nothing is to be held against al-Zamakhsharī, for he only said that it is not accepted by the Basrans, and it does not follow from this that he himself does not accept it; at most he reported it from others. As for the explicit yāʾ, he is excused in it, because, as I have already told you, what became well known among the readers is the "between-between" softening, not the pure substitution, so much so that al-Shāṭibī made that [substitution] the doctrine of the grammarians, not of the readers. So al-Zamakhsharī simply chose the doctrine of the readers, not that of the grammarians, regarding this word.
Abū al-Baqāʾ rejected the reading with "between-between" softening, saying: "It is not permissible here to make it 'between-between', as the hamza of «أئذا» is made, because the kasra here is transferred, whereas there it is original. Had the second hamza [here] been softened according to the rule, it would have been changed into an alif because of the fatḥa before it; but it was left so that it might take the vowel of the mīm in the original form." I say: his saying "transferred" is of no avail, because the transfer here is obligatory, so it is like the original. And his saying "had it been softened according to the rule…" to the end, is of no avail either, because consideration of the assimilation (idghām) precedes consideration of the softening of the hamza.
That has a place [of discussion] for which this place is too narrow.
The pattern of أَئِمَّة is أَفْعِلة, because it is the plural of إمام, like حمار and أَحْمِرة. Its original form is أَأْمِمة; two mīms came together and their assimilation was intended, so the vowel of the first mīm was transferred to the vowelless letter before it, namely the second hamza. That led to the meeting of two hamzas, the second of them with kasra. The Basran grammarians make it obligatory to change the second into yāʾ, while others pronounce it fully or soften it "between-between". Whoever inserted the alif did so for lightness, in order to separate the two hamzas; and it is best, in that case, that this be done with full pronunciation, as Hishām read. As for what the Shaykh related from Nāfiʿ of lengthening, together with his report from him that he pronounces the yāʾ explicitly, it is for the sake of extra lightness.
His words: {لاَ أَيْمَانَ}: Ibn ʿĀmir read «لا إيمان» with kasra on the hamza; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of آمَن يُؤْمن إيماناً. Is it from al-amān (safety)? In that case there are two views on its meaning. The first: that they are not granted safety themselves, i.e. they are not given a guarantee of safety after their breaking [of oaths] and their slandering, and there is no way to that. The second: a statement that they do not fulfil any covenant they conclude with anyone. Or [is it] from belief (taṣdīq), i.e. they have no Islam? Makkī chose the first interpretation, because it brings a new point not mentioned before, since describing them with unbelief and lack of faith has already preceded and is known.
The rest read with fatḥa; it is the plural of يمين (oath). This suits the [mention of] breaking [oaths], and there is consensus on the fatḥa in the second [occurrence]. The meaning of negating oaths of the unbelievers is that they do not fulfil them, even if they issue from them and are established. This is like the words of the other [poet]:
2473 - وإنْ حَلَفَتْ لا تَنْقُضُ الدهرَ عهدَها ... فليس لمخضوبِ البَنانِ يمينُ
(Even if she swears she will never break her covenant, the one with dyed fingertips has no [binding] oath.)
Al-Shāfiʿī held this view. Abū Ḥanīfa took it in its literal sense: that the oath of an unbeliever is not a legally valid oath, while according to al-Shāfiʿī it is a legally valid oath.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ}: accusative as an adverb of time; its origin is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of مَرَّ يَمُرُّ. Its verification has preceded.
His words: {فالله أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَوْهُ}: the Majestic Name is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are several views on the khabar (predicate). First: it is «أحقُّ», and «أن تَخْشَوه» on this view is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from the Majestic Name, the thing it is preferred over being omitted; [i.e.] fearing Allah is more deserving than fearing them. Second: «أحقُّ» is a fronted khabar and «أَن تَخْشَوه» a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being the khabar of the Majestic Name. Third: «أحقُّ» is a mubtadaʾ and «أن تَخْشَوه» its khabar, the clause again being the khabar of the Majestic Name; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Beginning with an indefinite noun is acceptable because it is an elative of preference (afʿal al-tafḍīl), and Sībawayh permitted a definite noun to be the khabar of an indefinite one in such as: اقصدْ رجلاً خيرٌ منه أبوه. Fourth: «أنْ تَخْشَوه» is in the position of the accusative, or the genitive, after dropping the preposition, the implied form being: أحقُّ بأن تَخْشَوه.
His words: {إِن كُنتُمْ مُّؤُمِنِينَ}: a condition whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, or placed before it, according to the disagreement.

semin-durr:14-14.t: The words of the Exalted: {وَيَشْفِ}: the majority read with the yāʾ of the absent [third person], referring back to the name of Allah the Exalted. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «نَشْفِ» with nūn, which is a fine iltifāt (shift of person). And He said «قوم مؤمنين» as a testimony of faith for those addressed; so it belongs to the category of iltifāt and of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, since He did not say «صدوركم».

semin-durr:15-15.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَيُذْهِبْ}: the majority read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the hāʾ, from أَذْهب, and «غَيْظ» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). A group read «ويَذْهَبْ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the hāʾ, making it the imperfect of ذهب, with «غيظ» as its fāʿil (agent). Zayd ibn ʿAlī read likewise, except that he put the verb in the nominative as a new start and did not conjoin it to the jussive before it, just as they read «ويتوبُ» in the nominative according to the majority. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Aʿraj, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid, ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī, Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, and Yaʿqūb read «ويتوبَ» in the accusative.
As for the reading of the majority, it is a new statement (istiʾnāf), and so it happened, for many people embraced Islam. Al-Zajjāj and Abū al-Fatḥ said: "This is a thing that exists whether they are fought or not fought; there is no reason to include repentance in the apodosis of the condition contained in «قاتِلوهم»." By "the condition" they both mean what is understood from the imperative clause.
As for the reading of Zayd and those mentioned with him, repentance is included in the answer to the imperative by way of meaning. There is obscurity in explaining this. Some said: when He commanded them to fight, that was hard on some of them; so when they went ahead with fighting, that act took the place of repentance from that dislike. I say: so the meaning becomes: if you fight them He will punish them and relent towards you for that dislike of fighting them. Others said in explaining it: attaining victory and much wealth is a pleasure sought by unlawful means; when they obtained it by lawful means, that became a motive for them to repent of what had gone before, so repentance became dependent on fighting.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya also said in explaining it: "In my view it is accounted for if one holds that by repentance here is meant [that] killing the unbelievers and striving in the way of Allah is a repentance for you, O believers, and a completion of your faith; on this view repentance enters into the condition of fighting." The Shaykh said: "What he supposed, that repentance falls under the answer to the imperative, is with reference to the believers who were commanded to fight the unbelievers. What appears [correct] is that it is with reference to the unbelievers, the meaning being: towards whomever He wills of the unbelievers, because fighting the unbelievers and the Muslims' overcoming them may be a cause of the Islam of many. Do you not see how, at the conquest of Mecca, many people embraced Islam because of it, and the Islam of some of them became very good, such as Ibn Abī Sarḥ and others?" I say: so this is a fourth explanation, and the meaning becomes: if you fight them, Allah will relent towards whomever He wills of the unbelievers, i.e. whomever of them He wills will embrace Islam.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذُواْ}: two views are possible for this clause. First: it falls within the domain of the "ṣalāh" [Translator's note: so written in the source, «الصلاة»; presumably «الصلة», the ṣila (relative clause), is meant] because it is conjoined to it, i.e. "those who made a covenant (عاهدوا) and did not take" [Translator's note: so in the source, «عاهدوا»; the verse has «جَاهَدُواْ»]. Second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «جاهدوا», i.e. they strove while not taking an intimate (walīja).
«وَلِيجة» is an object. And {مِن دُونِ الله} is either a second object, if taking (al-ittikhādh) means "making into", or attached to the taking if it is in its basic sense. Al-walīja is a فَعِيلة from al-wulūj, which is entering. Al-walīja is the one who enters with you into the inner part of your affairs. Abū ʿUbayda said: "Everything you put into something of which it is not part is a walīja; and a man among a people who is not one of them is called a walīja." It is used in a single form for singular, dual and plural. It may be pluralised as وَلائج and وُلُج, like صحيفة, صحائف and صُحُف. They recited, by ʿUbāda ibn Ṣafwān al-Ghanawī:
2474 - وَلائِجُهُمْ في كل مبدى ومَحْضَرٍ ... إلى كلِّ مَنْ يرجى ومَنْ يَتَخَوَّفُ
(Their intimates, in every desert and settled place, [reach out] to everyone who is hoped for and everyone who is feared.)
Al-Ḥasan read «بما يَعْملون» with the absent [third person], by iltifāt (shift of person), and Yaʿqūb read so in the transmission of Sallām.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مَا كَانَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ أَن يَعْمُرُواْ مَسَاجِدَ الله}: «أن يَعْمروا» is the noun (ism) of kāna. Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «مسجد الله» in the singular. It bears two possibilities: that a particular mosque is meant, namely the Sacred Mosque, because of His words {وَعِمَارَةَ المسجد الحرام} [al-Tawba: 19]; or that it is a generic noun (ism jins) under which all mosques are included, the Sacred Mosque being included first and foremost. The rest read «مساجد» in the plural, and it too admits both matters. The reason for the plural is either that every spot of the Sacred Mosque is called a mosque, or that it is the qibla of all mosques, so that it was valid for that reason to apply the plural word to it.
His words: {شَاهِدِينَ}: the majority read it with yāʾ, accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يَعْمُروا». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «شاهدون» with wāw, nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause also being a ḥāl. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «يُعْمِروا» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm, from the four-letter أَعْمَرَ, the meaning being: that they help in its upkeep.
His words: {على أَنْفُسِهِمْ}: the majority read «أنفسهم», the plural of نَفْس. It was also read «أَنْفَسهم» with fatḥa on the fāʾ; its justification is that by al-anfas — the noblest and most exalted, from nafāsa (preciousness) — is meant the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It was said: because there is no clan among the clans of the Arabs but that he has kinship by birth among them. This meaning is also transmitted in the explanation of the majority reading, but it is clearer with this reading.
His words: {وَفِي النار هُمْ خَالِدُونَ}: this is a resumptive (mustaʾnafa) clause, and «في النار» is attached to the khabar; it was fronted out of concern for it and for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. and they are abiding in the Fire; the adverbial has occurred between the conjunction and the maʿṭūf (conjoined)." I say: this is questionable, in that it gives the impression that this clause is conjoined to what precedes it as a single word is conjoined to its like by implication, which is not so; rather it is resumptive. And if it is resumptive, one does not say of it that the adverbial separated the conjunction from the conjoined; that only applies to two conjoined single words or what is interpreted as such. The verification of this has preceded at His words: {رَبَّنَآ آتِنَا فِي الدنيا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الآخرة حَسَنَةً} [al-Baqara: 201] and at His words: {وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ الناس أَن تَحْكُمُواْ بالعدل} [al-Nisāʾ: 58].
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «خالدين» with yāʾ, accusative as a ḥāl of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the preposition phrase before it, because the preposition phrase has become the khabar, as when you say: «في الدار زيد قاعداً». Thus Zayd ibn ʿAlī put «شاهدين» in the nominative and «خالدون» in the accusative, the reverse of the majority reading in both.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِنَّمَا يَعْمُرُ مَسَاجِدَ الله}: the majority of readers, of the Seven and others, read the plural. Al-Jaḥdarī, and Ḥammād ibn Abī Salama from Ibn Kathīr, read the singular. The justification is taken from what has preceded. What appears here is that the plural is literal here, because what is meant is all the believers who frequent all the mosques of the regions of the earth.
His words: {سِقَايَةَ الحاج وَعِمَارَةَ}: the majority read both as maṣdars (verbal nouns) on the pattern فِعالة, like الصِّيانة, الوِقاية and التِّجارة. The yāʾ was not changed into hamza because it is protected by the tāʾ of the feminine, unlike رِداء; and [unlike] عَباءة, because the tāʾ of the feminine is accidental in it. In that case a muḍāf must be omitted, either from the first or from the second, so that the two things equated correspond. The implied form is: "Have you made the people of the watering of the pilgrims and the upkeep of the Sacred Mosque like him who believed?", or "Have you made the watering and the upkeep like the faith of him who believed?", or "like the work of him who believed?".
Ibn al-Zubayr, al-Bāqir and Abū Wajra read «سُقاة» and «عَمَرَة»: [سُقاة] with ḍamma on the sīn and the tāʾ of the feminine after the alif, and عَمَرة with fatḥa on the ʿayn and the mīm, without alif. Both are plurals of ساقٍ and عامر, as one says قاضٍ and قُضَاة, رام and رُماة, بارّ and بَرَرة, فاجِر and فَجَرة. The original form is سُقَيَة; the yāʾ was changed into alif because it is vowelled and preceded by fatḥa. There is no need to suppose the omission of a muḍāf, even if it is needed in the majority reading.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read likewise, except that he put «المسجد الحرام» in the accusative with «عَمَرَة» and dropped the tanwīn because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, as in his [the poet's] words:
2475 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا ذاكرَ اللَّهَ إلا قليلا
(… nor remembering Allah except a little.)
and His words: {قُل هُوَ الله أَحَدُ الله الصمد} [al-Ikhlāṣ: 1-2].
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «سُقاية» with ḍamma on the sīn, and «عمرة», both being plurals too. There is an obvious difficulty in pluralising «ساقٍ» on the pattern فُعالة. What ought to be said, and not departed [from], is that this is made the plural of سِقْي, al-siqy being the thing watered, like الرِّعْي and الطِّحْن; and فِعْل is pluralised on فُعال — they said ظِئْر and ظُؤار. By rights the tāʾ of the feminine should not enter it, as it did not enter «ظُؤَار», but he made the plural feminine, as it is made feminine in their saying حِجارة and فُحولة. In that case a muḍāf must be supposed, i.e. "Have you made the owners of the watered things like him who believed?"
His words: {لاَ يَسْتَوُونَ}: in it [there are] two views; the more apparent of them is that it is resumptive: the Exalted informs that the two parties are not equal. The second is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the two objects of al-jaʿl (making), the implied form being: "I made them equal to one another while they differ." [Translator's note: so in the source, «سوَّيْتُهم بينهم»; the sense is "you made them equal".]

semin-durr:21-21.t:
The readers' disagreement on «يبشرهم» and its justification has preceded in Āl ʿImrān, as has the disagreement on {وَرِضْوَانٌ} [Āl ʿImrān: 15]. Al-Aʿmash read «رضوان» with ḍamma on the rāʾ and the ḍād. Abū Ḥātim rejected it and said: "It is not permissible." This is no blame on al-Aʿmash, since he transmitted it, and that is found in the language of the Arabs: they said السُّلُطان with ḍamma on the sīn and the lām.
His words: {لَّهُمْ فِيهَا نَعِيمٌ}: this clause may be a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات», or an adjective of «رحمة», because they allowed this hāʾ to refer back to the mercy and to refer back to the gardens. Makkī allowed it to refer back to the glad tidings understood from His words «يُبَشِّرهم», as though it were said: "they have in those glad tidings"; on this view the clause is an adjective of that implied maṣdar if you suppose it indefinite, and a ḥāl (circumstantial) if you suppose it definite. «نعيم» may be the fāʿil (agent) of the preposition phrase before it, which is preferable because it then belongs to the category of description by a single word; or it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the preposition phrase before it as its khabar (predicate). The verification of this has preceded more than once. «خالدين» is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «لهم».

semin-durr:24-24.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِن كَانَ آبَاؤُكُمْ}: «آباؤكم» and what is conjoined to it is the noun (ism) of kāna, and «أحبَّ» is its khabar (predicate), so it is accusative. Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf, the one who affected eloquence, used to read it in the nominative; Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar declared it a solecism, and so he exiled him. The Shaykh said: "He declared it a solecism only in respect of its contradicting the transmitting readers; otherwise it is permissible in Arabic: a noun is implied in «كان», namely the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and what follows is in the nominative as mubtadaʾ and khabar, the clause then being the khabar of «كان»." I say: so it would be like the words of the poet:
2476 - إذا مِتُّ كان الناسُ صِنْفان ... شامتٌ وآخرُ مُثْنٍ بالذي كنتُ أَصْنَعُ
(When I die, people will be of two kinds: one gloating, and another praising what I used to do.)
This is according to one of the two interpretations of the verse. The other is that «صنفان» is an accusative khabar, and he used it according to the dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith and those who agree with them.
The story the Shaykh alluded to, of Yaḥyā declaring al-Ḥajjāj's reading a solecism, is that al-Ḥajjāj used to claim great eloquence. One day he said to Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, whom he held in high esteem: "Do you find me making mistakes in speech?" [Translator's note: the source has «هي تجدني», presumably for «هل تجدني».] He said: "The Emir is above that." He said: "I adjure you to tell me" — and they used to hold the adjurations of emirs in great regard. He said: "Yes." He said: "In what?" He said: "In the Qur'an." He said: "Woe to you! That is uglier for me. In which verse?" He said: "I heard you read: قل إن كان آباؤكم until you reached «أحبُّ» and you put it in the nominative." He said: "Then you will not hear me make a mistake after it," and he exiled him to Khurasan. He stayed there for a while, and at that time Yazīd ibn al-Muhallab ibn Abī Ṣufra was there. An army came upon them, and he wrote a letter to al-Ḥajjāj in which was: "The enemy came to us, and we left them at the foot (al-ḥaḍīḍ), and we climbed to the summit (ʿurʿura) of the mountain." Al-Ḥajjāj said: "What has Ibn al-Muhallab to do with such language?" He was told: "Yaḥyā is there." He said: "Then that [explains it]."
The majority read «عشيرتكم» in the singular, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim «عشيراتكم» as a sound plural. The justification of the plural is that each of those addressed has a clan, so the plural is fitting. Al-Akhfash claimed that «عشيرة» is not pluralised with alif and tāʾ, but only as a broken plural, عشائر. This reading is a proof against him; it is also the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Abū Rajāʾ. Al-Ḥasan read «عشائركم»; it was said that it is more common than عشيراتكم.
Al-ʿashīra is the nearest kinsfolk. It was said: they are a man's people through whom he becomes numerous, i.e. they become for him like the complete number; that is because al-ʿashara (ten) is the complete number, so al-ʿashīra became a name for a man's relatives through whom he becomes numerous, whether they reach ten or more. It was also said: it is the group gathered by lineage, pact or affection, like the bond of companionship (al-ʿishra).

semin-durr:25-25.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ}: there are several views on it. First: it is conjoined to the position of His words «في مواطنَ»: an adverb of time, without the mediation of «في», conjoined to an adverb of place governed in the genitive by it. There is nothing strange in coordinating an adverb of time with one of place or the reverse; you say: «سرت أمامك يوم الجمعة», except that it is better to leave out the conjunction in such a case. Second: Ibn ʿAṭiyya claimed that it may be conjoined to the wording of «مواطن» by supposing "and on (وفي)", the preposition having been omitted. There is no need for this. Third: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how did He conjoin time to place, namely «يوم حنين» to «مواطن»? I say: its meaning is 'and the place of the day of Ḥunayn', or 'in the days of many places and the day of Ḥunayn'." Fourth: that by the places (al-mawāṭin) times are meant, in which case only a time has been conjoined to a time. Al-Zamakhsharī said after what I quoted from him: "And by al-mawāṭin the time may be meant, as in مقتل الحسين (the killing/time of the killing of al-Ḥusayn); moreover, «يومَ حنين» must be governed in the accusative by an implied verb, not by this overt one. What necessitates that is that His words «إذا أعجبتكم» are a badal (substitute) of «يوم حنين»; had you made its governor this overt [verb], it would not be valid, because their numbers did not please them in all those places, nor were they numerous in all of them. So it remains that its governor is a verb particular to it." I say: I do not know what led him to suppose one of the two muḍāfs, or to interpret the place as the time, so that time is conjoined to time or place to place, when it is valid to conjoin one of the two adverbials to the other.
As for his words "moreover, it must be…" to the end, they are good words. Their explanation is that the verb is restricted by the adverb of place; if we make «إذ» a badal of «يوم», it is governed by it, because the badal stands in the place of what it substitutes for. It would then follow that He helped them, when their numbers pleased them, in many places, while the assumption is that in some of these places they were not of this description. However, an objection may arise, for the Exalted did not say "in all the places" so that what he said would follow; and it is possible that by "many" He meant "all", as by "few" non-existence is meant.
His words: {بِمَا رَحُبَتْ}: «ما» is maṣdariyya, i.e. its spaciousness and its breadth. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read in both places «رَحْبَت» with sukūn on the middle radical; it is the dialect of Tamīm, who strip the middle radical of فَعُل [of its vowel], saying in شَرُف: شَرْف.
Al-ruḥb with ḍamma is breadth, and with fatḥa [al-raḥb] is the wide thing. One says: رَحُب المكان يَرْحُب رُحْباً ورَحَابة, and it is intransitive. As for its being transitive in their saying «رَحُبَتْكم الدار», it is by implication of another meaning (taḍmīn), because it means وَسِعَتْكم (it was wide enough for you).
Ḥunayn is the name of a valley, which is why He made it fully declinable. Some made it the name of the area and treated it as a diptote, in his words:
2477 - نَصَرُوا نبيَّهُم وشَدُّوا أَزْرَه ... بحنينَ يومَ تواكُلِ الأبطال
(They helped their Prophet and strengthened his back at Ḥunayn, on the day when the heroes left [the fighting] to one another.)
This is like what another said about «حراء», the name of the well-known mountain, taking into account the femininity of the area, in his words:
2478 - ألسنا أكبرَ الثَّقَلَيْنِ رَحْلاً ... وأَعْظَمَهم ببطنَ حِراءَ نارا
(Are we not the greatest of men and jinn in encampment, and the greatest of them in fire [of hospitality] in the hollow of Ḥirāʾ?)
Al-mawāṭin is the plural of مَوْطِن with kasra on the middle radical; likewise its noun of maṣdar and its noun of time, because of the weakness of its first radical, like المَوْعد. He said:
2479 - وكم مَوْطنٍ لولايَ طِحْتَ كما هوى ... بأجرامه مِنْ قُلَّة النِّيْقِ مُنْهوي
(How many a situation in which, but for me, you would have perished, just as one falls with his body from the top of a mountain peak!)

semin-durr:28-28.t: The words of the Exalted: {إِنَّمَا المشركون نَجَسٌ}: by way of hyperbole, they were made impurity itself; or by omission of a muḍāf. Abū Ḥaywa read «نِجْسٌ» with kasra on the nūn and sukūn on the jīm. Its justification is that it is originally an active participle on the pattern فَعِل, like كَتِف and كَبِد, then lightened by making its middle radical vowelless after making its first radical follow it [in vowel]. In that case a qualified noun must be omitted, this adjective standing in its place, i.e. "an impure party" or "an impure kind". Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «أنجاس» in the plural; it may be the plural of the majority reading or the plural of Abū Ḥaywa's reading.

semin-durr:29-29.t: The words of the Exalted: {مِنَ الذين أُوتُواْ}: an explication (bayān) of the relative noun before it. Al-jizya is a فِعْلَة expressing manner, like الرِّكْبَة, because it is from al-jazāʾ (recompense) for the safety they were given. «عن يدٍ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they give it subdued and humbled. Likewise «وهم صاغرون».

semin-durr:30-30.t:
The words of the Exalted: {عُزَيْرٌ ابن الله}: ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read «عُزَيْرٌ» with tanwīn, and the rest without tanwīn. As for the first reading, it may be an Arabic noun functioning as mubtadaʾ (subject), with «ابنُ» as its khabar (predicate), its tanwīn being according to the base. It may also be a foreign noun which is light in pronunciation, like Nūḥ and Lūṭ, so it was made fully declinable because of the lightness of its pronunciation. This is the view of Abū ʿUbayd, meaning that it is the diminutive of «عَزَر», so its ruling is that of its non-diminutive form. This view was rebutted against Abū ʿUbayd on the grounds that it is not a diminutive; it is only a foreign word that came in the form of a diminutive in the language of the Arabs, so it is like Sulaymān, which came on the pattern of ʿUthaymān and ʿUbaydān.
As for the second reading, the dropping of the tanwīn admits three views. First: it was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, in the manner of the reading {قُلْ هُوَ الله أَحَدُ الله الصمد} [al-Ṣamad: 1-2]; it is a fully declinable noun, nominative as mubtadaʾ, and «ابن» is its khabar. Second: its tanwīn was dropped because «ابن» occurs as its naʿt (adjective); it is nominative as mubtadaʾ, «ابن» is its adjective and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "ʿUzayr son of Allah is our prophet", or "our imam", or "our messenger". It has preceded that whenever ibn occurs as an adjective between two proper names, with nothing separating it from what it qualifies, its alif is dropped in writing and its tanwīn [of the first name] in pronunciation, and it is retained only by poetic necessity; the verses cited for that preceded at the end of al-Māʾida. «عزير» may also be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "our prophet is ʿUzayr", with «ابن» as its adjective, or badal (substitute), or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Third: it was dropped only because it is a diptote, owing to definiteness and foreignness. It was written in the muṣḥaf only with the alif retained, which supports whoever makes it a khabar.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«عزير ابن» is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, like His words {المسيح ابن الله}. «عُزَيْر» is a foreign name like ʿAzrāʾīl and ʿAyzār; because of its foreignness and definiteness it is a diptote, and whoever made it fully declinable made it Arabic. As for the saying of those who said that the dropping of the tanwīn is because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, as in the reading {قُلْ هُوَ الله أَحَدٌ الله} [al-Ṣamad: 1-2], or because «ابن» occurs as an adjective and the khabar is omitted, namely 'our object of worship', that is contrivance when there is an easier way out."
His words: {يُضَاهِئُونَ}: the generality read «يضاهُون» with ḍamma on the hāʾ followed by wāw [Translator's note: the source prints «يضاهِئُون» here, which contradicts the description that follows; the majority reading is «يُضَاهُونَ»], and ʿĀṣim with a hāʾ bearing kasra, followed by a hamza bearing ḍamma, followed by wāw. It was said: both have one meaning, namely resemblance, and there are two dialects in it: ضاهَأْتُ and ضاهَيْت, with hamza and with yāʾ; the hamza is the dialect of Thaqīf. It was said: the yāʾ is derived from the hamza, as they said قرأ and قَرَيْت, توضَّأت and توضَّيْت, أَخْطَأْت and أَخْطَيْت. And it was said: rather, يضاهِئُون with hamza is taken from يضاهِيُوْن; when the hāʾ was given ḍamma [Translator's note: so in the source], it was changed into hamza. This is wrong, because such a yāʾ does not remain in this position so that it could be changed into hamza; rather its morphology leads to the dropping of the yāʾ, as in «يُرامُون» from al-ramy and «يُماشُون» from al-mashy. Some claimed that it is taken from their saying "امرأة ضَهْيَا" with the short ending, which is a woman who has no breasts, or who does not menstruate; she was so called because of her resemblance to men.
One says: امرأة ضَهْيَا with the short ending, ضَهْيَاء with the long ending, like حمراء, and ضَهْياءَة with the long ending and the tāʾ of the feminine: three dialects. Combining two feminine markers in this word is anomalous. Al-Jarmī related the third dialect from Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī. It was said: the view of whoever claimed that al-muḍāhaʾa with hamza is taken from امرأة ضَهْياء in its three dialects is wrong, because the two roots differ: the hamza in امرأة ضَهْياء is augmentative in the three dialects, while in al-muḍāhaʾa it is radical.
If it is said: why was it not claimed that the hamza of ضهياء is radical and its yāʾ augmentative? The answer is that فَعْيَل with fatḥa on the yāʾ is not established. If it is said: then why was it not claimed that its pattern is فَعْلَل, like جعفر? The answer is that the augmentative status of the hamza in ضَهْياء with the long ending is established, so let it be established in the other dialect too; this is a morphological rule.
The speech involves the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "their saying resembles the saying of those who…"; the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, so it turned into a nominative pronoun after having been a genitive pronoun.
The majority pause at «أفواههم» and begin with «يضاهئون». It was also said: the bāʾ is attached to the verb after it; on this view there is no need to omit this muḍāf. Abū al-Baqāʾ considered ʿĀṣim's reading weak, which is not good, because it is mutawātir (mass-transmitted).

semin-durr:31-31.t: The words of the Exalted: {والمسيح ابن مَرْيَمَ}: conjoined to «رُهْبانَهم», the second object being omitted, since the implied form is: "The Jews took their rabbis as lords, and the Christians their monks and the Messiah son of Maryam as lords." Because ambiguity is safe here, the pronoun in «اتخذوا» was mixed, though it is divided between the Jews and the Christians. This is what Abū al-Baqāʾ meant by his words: "i.e. and they took the Messiah as a lord; the verb and one of the two objects were omitted." He also allowed it to be accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and they worshipped the Messiah son of Maryam".

semin-durr:33-33.t: The words of the Exalted: {ويأبى الله}: {إِلاَّ أَن يُتِمَّ} is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The emptied exception (al-istithnāʾ al-mufarragh) entered an affirmative sentence only because it has the meaning of negation. Al-Akhfash the Younger said: "The meaning of يَأْبَى is 'prevents'." Al-Farrāʾ said: "«إلا» entered because there is a touch of denial in the speech." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He treated «أبى» like «لم يُرِدْ» (did not want). Do you not see how {يُرِيدُونَ أَن يُطْفِئُواْ} was matched by His words «ويأبى الله», and [how] it was put in the place of: 'and Allah wants nothing but to perfect His light'?" Al-Zajjāj said: "The thing excepted from is omitted, its implied form being: and He refuses, i.e. dislikes, everything except that He perfect His light." Abū al-Baqāʾ combined the doctrine of al-Zajjāj with that of the others, making them one doctrine; he said: "يأبى means 'dislikes', and 'dislikes' means 'prevents'; that is why He made an exception, because of the meaning of negation in it. The implied form is: He refuses everything except the perfection of His light."

semin-durr:34-34.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَيَصُدُّونَ}: it may be transitive, i.e. they turn people away, or intransitive; so said the Shaykh. This is questionable, because it is only transitive; its object is merely omitted, whether intended or not, as in His words {كُلُواْ واشربوا} [al-Baqara: 60].
His words: {والذين يَكْنِزُونَ}: the majority read it with the wāw. There are two interpretations of it. First: it [the wāw] is resumptive, and «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) that has taken on the meaning of a condition, which is why the fāʾ entered its khabar (predicate). Second: it is one of the descriptions of the many among the rabbis and monks; this is the view of ʿUthmān and Muʿāwiya. «الذين» may also be accusative by an implied verb explained by «فَبَشِّرْهم», which is preferable [because of the imperative].
Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «الذين» without wāw. It admits the two preceding views, but its being one of the descriptions of the many among the rabbis and monks is more apparent than resumption, the reverse of the reading with the wāw.
Al-kanz is gathering and joining together; from it is "ناقة كِناز", i.e. a she-camel of compact build. It is not restricted to gold and silver, but is said of other things, even if it is mostly used of them. He said:
2480 - لا دَرَّ دَرِّي إنْ أَطْعَمْتُ جائِعَهُمْ ... قِرْفَ الحَتِيِّ وعندي البُرُّ مَكْنوزُ
(May my milk run dry if I feed their hungry the husks of dried meal while I have wheat stored away.)
Another said:
2481 - على شديدٍ لحُمُه كِنازِ ... باتَ يُنَزِّيني على أَوْفازِ
(On a strong [mount] with compact flesh, which spent the night making me leap up, unsettled.)
His words: {وَلاَ يُنفِقُونَهَا}: two things preceded and the pronoun refers back [to] a singular. It was said: it belongs to the category of what is omitted because the speech indicates it, the implied form being: "and those who hoard gold and do not spend it". It was said: it refers back to the hoarded things, the part of them that is mentioned indicating this, because what is hoarded is more general than the two currencies and other things; when He mentioned the part, it indicated the whole, so the pronoun refers back as a plural in this respect. Its parallel is the words of the other [poet]:
2482 - ولو حَلَفَتْ بين الصَّفا أمُّ عامرٍ ... ومَرْوَتِها بالله بَرَّتْ يمينها
(If Umm ʿĀmir swore by Allah between al-Ṣafā and its Marwa, her oath would be kept.)
i.e. and the Marwa of Mecca; the pronoun refers back to it [Mecca] since its part, al-Ṣafā, was mentioned. So Ibn Mālik used it as evidence. There is another possibility in it, namely that the pronoun refers back to al-Ṣafā and was made feminine according to the sense, since it has the meaning of "the spot" or "the hillock". It was said: the pronoun refers back to the gold, because its feminine treatment is more common, and [a pronoun] has also been omitted after the silver. It was said: it refers back to the spending indicated by the verb, as in His words {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8]. It was said: it refers back to the zakāt, i.e. and they do not spend the zakāt of the wealth. And it was said: it refers back to the treasures indicated by the verb.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
The words of the Exalted: {يَوْمَ يحمى}: accusative by His words «بعذاب أليم». It was said: by something omitted which «عذاب» indicates, i.e. they will be punished on the day it is heated, or: remember the day it is heated. It was said: it is accusative by «أليم». It was said: the original is «عذاب يوم», this عذاب being a badal (substitute) of the first عذاب; when the muḍāf was omitted, the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place. And it was said: it is accusative by an implied verb of saying, the explanation of which will come.
«يُحمى» may be from حَمَيْتُ or أَحْمَيْتُ, three-letter and four-letter. One says: حَمَيْتُ الحديدة and أَحْمَيْتها, i.e. I kindled [fire] over it so that it would become hot. The omitted fāʿil (agent) is the fire, its implied form being: "the day the fire is heated over it"; when the fāʿil was omitted, the feminine marker went with it, as when you say «رُفِعَت القضيةُ إلى الأمير» and then say «رُفع إلى الأمير». It was also said: the meaning is: the fuel is heated.
Al-Ḥasan read «تُحْمَى» with the upper-dotted tāʾ, i.e. the fire, which supports the first interpretation. Abū Ḥaywa read «يُكوى» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, because the femininity of the fāʿil is figurative. The majority [read] «جباهُهم» with clear pronunciation (iẓhār), and Abū ʿAmr in some of his transmission routes read it with assimilation (idghām), just as he assimilated {سَلَكَكُمْ} [al-Muddaththir: 42] and {مَّنَاسِكَكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 200]. Like جباههم is «وجوههم», in which clear pronunciation is the well-known [reading].
His words: {هذا مَا كَنَزْتُمْ لأَنْفُسِكُمْ}: governed by an omitted verb of saying, i.e. that will be said to them on the day it is heated. His words {مَا كُنتُمْ تَكْنِزُونَ}: i.e. the recompense of what you used to [hoard], because what is hoarded is not tasted. «ما» may mean "that which", the returning pronoun being omitted, or it may be maṣdariyya. It was also read «تَكْنُزون» with ḍamma on the middle radical of the imperfect; they are two dialects: one says كَنَزَ يَكْنِز and كَنَزَ يَكْنُز.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِنَّ عِدَّةَ}: al-ʿidda is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning number. «عند الله» is in the accusative by it, i.e. in His ruling. «اثنا عشر» is the khabar (predicate) of inna. Hubayra from Ḥafṣ read — and it is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar — «اثنا عْشَرَ» with sukūn on the ʿayn while retaining the alif before it. It was found objectionable in that it combines two vowelless letters not according to their [permitted] conditions, like their saying «التقت حَلْقتا البِطان» with the alif of «حَلْقتا» retained. Ṭalḥa read with sukūn on the shīn, as though he treated عشر in the masculine like عشرة in the feminine.
«شَهْراً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and it is emphatic, because that was already understood from the first [word]; it is like your saying «عندي من الدنانير عشرون ديناراً». The plural differs in His words «عدَّة الشهور» and in His words {الحج أَشْهُرٌ} [al-Baqara: 197], because this is a plural of multitude and that is a plural of paucity.
His words: {فِي كِتَابِ الله}: it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «اثنا عشر». It may [also, as was said,] be a badal (substitute) of the adverbial before it; but this is not permissible, or is weak, because it entails giving a predicate about the relative [i.e. the maṣdar ʿidda] before its ṣila is complete, since this preposition phrase is attached to it by way of substitution. And even supposing that this is valid technically, how can it be valid in meaning? Nor may {فِي كِتَابِ الله} be attached to «عدة», lest it entail separating the maṣdar from what it governs by its khabar. The analogy of whoever allowed its substitution for the adverbial is that he should allow this; and al-Ḥawfī explicitly allowed it.
His words: {يَوْمَ خَلَقَ}: it may be attached to «كتاب», on the view that the maṣdar is meant by it and not a concrete thing. It may be attached to the [notion of] existence (al-istiqrār) in the preposition phrase {فِي كِتَابِ الله}, the book then being a concrete thing, not a maṣdar. Al-Ḥawfī allowed it to be attached to «عدة», which is rejected by what has preceded.
His words: {مِنْهَآ أَرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ}: three views are possible for this clause. First: it is an adjective of «اثنا عشر». Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the [notion of] existence. Third: it is resumptive. The pronoun in «منها» refers back to {اثنا عَشَرَ شَهْراً}, because it is the nearest thing mentioned, not to «الشهور». The pronoun in «فيهنَّ» also refers back to «الاثنا عشر». Al-Farrāʾ and Qatāda said: it refers back to the four sacred [months], and this is better for two reasons. First: it is the nearest thing mentioned. Second: it is established that treating a plural of paucity of non-rational beings like a group of females is better than treating it with the singular feminine pronoun, and the plural of multitude the reverse: «الأجذاع انكسَرْن» and «الجذوع انكسرت»; the reverse is also permissible.
His words: {كَآفَّةً}: accusative as a ḥāl, either of the fāʿil (agent) or of the object. It has preceded that «كافَّة» is used only in the accusative as a ḥāl, that al- does not enter it, and that it is neither dualised nor pluralised; likewise the second «كافة».

semin-durr:37-37.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِنَّمَا النسياء}: there are two views on «النسِيْء». First: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern فَعِيل from أَنْسَأ, i.e. "he postponed", like النذير from أَنْذَر and النكير from أَنْكر. This is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words, for he said: "Al-nasīʾ is postponing the sanctity of a month to another month." In that case predicating «وزيادة» of it is clear and needs no supposition. Al-Ṭabarī said: "Al-nasīʾ with hamza means increase." I say: because it is a postponement in time, increase follows from it.
Second: it is a فَعِيل in the sense of مَفْعول (passive participle), from نَسَأه, i.e. he postponed it, so it is منسوء; then مفعول was converted into فعيل, just as مفعول was converted into فعيل [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably a reference to parallel words such as قتيل from مقتول]. Abū Ḥātim and al-Jawharī inclined to this. Al-Fārisī rejected this view on the grounds that the meaning would be: "the postponed [thing] is only an increase", the postponed thing being the month, and the month cannot be an increase in unbelief. Some answered this by supposing the omission of a muḍāf, either from the first, i.e. "the postponing of what is postponed is only an increase in unbelief", or from the second, i.e. "what is postponed is only a thing of increase".
The majority read «النَّسيء» with a hamza after the yāʾ. Warsh from Nāfiʿ read «النَّسِيّ», changing the hamza into yāʾ and assimilating the [preceding] yāʾ into it; this was also related from Abū Jaʿfar, al-Zuhrī and Ḥumayd, just as they lightened «برية» and «خطية». Al-Sulamī, Ṭalḥa, al-Ashhab and Shibl read «النَّسْء» with sukūn on the sīn. Mujāhid, al-Sulamī and Ṭalḥa also read «النَّسُوء» on the pattern فَعُول with fatḥa on the first radical, which is postponement; فَعول is rare among maṣdars, and a few small words of it have preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. The derivation of this root has preceded in al-Baqara. Here it denotes postponing some months after others. He said:
2483 - ألَسْنا الناسئينَ على مَعَدٍّ ... شهورَ الحِلِّ نجعلُها حَراما
(Are we not the ones who postpone the months for Maʿadd, making the lawful months sacred?)
Another said:
2484 - نَسَؤُوا الشّهور بها وكانوا أهلَها ... مِنْ قبلِكم والعزُّ لم يتحوَّلِ
(They postponed the months in it, and they were its people before you, while might had not shifted.)
His words: {يُضَلُّ بِهِ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «يُضَلُّ» in the passive, and the rest in the active [يَضِلُّ], with the relative noun as its fāʿil (agent). Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Qatāda, Yaʿqūb and ʿAmr ibn Maymūn read «يُضِلُّ», active, from أضل. There are two views on the fāʿil. First: the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, i.e. Allah leads astray those who disbelieved. Second: the fāʿil is «الذين كفروا», and on this view the object is omitted, i.e. those who disbelieved lead astray their followers. Abū Rajāʾ read «يَضَلُّ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ḍād; it is from ضَلِلْت with kasra on the lām, أضَلُّ with fatḥa on it; the original form is أَضْلَلُ, and the fatḥa of the lām was transferred to the ḍād for the sake of assimilation. Al-Nakhaʿī, and al-Ḥasan in the transmission of Maḥbūb, read «نُضِلُّ» with ḍamma on the nūn of majesty, «الذين» being the object; this strengthens [the view] that the fāʿil is the pronoun of Allah in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd.
His words: {يُحِلُّونَهُ}: two views. First: the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) of the going astray. Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His words: {لِّيُوَاطِئُواْ}: there are two views on this lām. [First:] it is attached to «يُحَرِّفونه» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «يُحَرِّمُونَهُ»]. This is what the doctrine of the Basrans requires, for they give government to the second of two competing [governors]. Second: it is attached to «يُحِلُّونه»; this is what the doctrine of the Kufans requires, for they give government to the first because it comes first. The saying of whoever said that it is attached to both verbs together means only in meaning, not in wording.
Abū Jaʿfar read «ليوطِيُوا» with kasra on the ṭāʾ and ḍamma on a pure yāʾ. The correct [form] is that it ought to be read with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ and the yāʾ dropped, because when he changed the hamza into yāʾ, the ḍamma on it was found heavy and was dropped; then two vowelless letters met, so the yāʾ was dropped and the ṭāʾ given ḍamma to match the wāw.
Al-muwāṭaʾa is agreement and coming together. One says: تواطَؤُوا على كذا, i.e. they came together on it, as if each one treads (yaṭaʾu) where the other treads. From it is His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ الليل هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْأً} [al-Muzzammil: 6], also read وِطاءً; it will come, if Allah wills.
Al-Zuhrī read «ليواطِيُّوا» with a doubled yāʾ. That is how they described his reading, and it is problematic, so much so that someone said: "If he did not mean by it a strong articulation of the yāʾ and freeing it from the hamza, without doubling, I do not know its justification." It is as he said.
His words: «زُيِّنَ»: the majority read «زُيِّن» in the passive, the omitted fāʿil being Satan. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it in the active, [the fāʿil] being Satan too, and «سوء» its object.

semin-durr:38-38.t:
The words of the Exalted: {اثاقلتم}: its original form is تثاقلتم. When assimilation was intended, the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the tāʾ is meant] was made vowelless and a connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in, as preceded at {فادارأتم} [al-Baqara: 72], whose original form is تدارأتم. Al-Aʿmash read «تثاقلتم» in this original form. «ما» in His words «مالكم» is interrogative, with a sense of disapproval in it. It was said: its [i.e. of «قيل»] omitted fāʿil (agent) is the Messenger.
«اثَّاقلتم» is past in wording and imperfect in meaning, i.e. they are being sluggish; it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it governs the adverbial, i.e. "what is the matter with you, being sluggish at the time of the saying?" Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "اثَّاقلتم is a past verb in the sense of the imperfect, i.e. what is the matter with you that you are sluggish; it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. what [good] is there for you in sluggishness; or in the position of the genitive according to the opinion of al-Khalīl. It was also said: it is in the position of a ḥāl." The Shaykh said: "This is not good, because it entails the omission of «أَنْ», since a maṣdar is only formed from a maṣdar particle and the verb, and omitting «أَنْ» in such a case is very rare, or a poetic necessity. And if the implied form is 'in sluggishness', it cannot govern «إذا», because what is governed by the relative maṣdar does not precede it; so what governs «إذا» in the accusative, and what 'in sluggishness' is attached to, is what «لكم», occurring as the khabar (predicate) of «ما», is attached to."
It was also read «أَثَّاقَلْتم» with the interrogative whose meaning is disapproval. In that case it may not govern «إذا», because what follows an interrogative particle does not govern what precedes it; so the governor of this adverbial is either the [notion of] existence implied in «لكم», or something implied that the wording indicates, the implied form being: "what do you do when it is said to you?". Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this. What appears [best] is to suppose: "what is the matter with you that you are sluggish when it is said", so that it is indicated both by the wording and by the meaning.
His words: {إِلَى الأرض}: it implies the meaning of inclining and clinging. His words «من الآخرة»: the statements of the grammatical analysts and commentators concur that «مِنْ» means "instead of", as in His words {لَجَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ مَّلاَئِكَةً} [al-Zukhruf: 60], i.e. instead of you. Like it are the words of the other [poet]:
2485 - جاريةٌ لم تَأْكُلِ المُرَقَّقا ... ولم تَذُقْ من البُقول الفُسْتُقا
(A girl who has not eaten thin bread, nor tasted pistachios instead of vegetables.)
and the words of the other:
2486 - فليت لنا مِنْ ماءِ زمزمَ شَرْبةً ... مُبَرَّدَةً باتَتْ على طَهَيانِ
(Would that we had, instead of the water of Zamzam, a cooled draught that spent the night on [Mount] Ṭahayān.)
However, most grammarians do not affirm this meaning for it and interpret whatever suggests it; the implied form here is: "you have held fast [away] from the Hereafter, content with the life", and likewise the rest of them. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«من الآخرة» is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. in place of the Hereafter"; so he supposed the attachment to be specific, though he may have intended to explain the meaning.
His words: {فِي الآخرة}: attached to something omitted in terms of meaning, its implied form being: "the enjoyment of the life of this world, counted in the Hereafter, is only…"; «محسوباً» is thus a ḥāl of «متاع». Al-Ḥawfī said: "It is attached to «قليل», which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject)." He said: "It is permissible for the adverbial to precede its governor that is joined with «إلا», because adverbials are governed by mere traces of verbs. Had you said «ما زيدٌ عمراً إلا يَضْرب», it would not be permissible."

semin-durr:40-40.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِلاَّ تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ}: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of this condition is omitted because His words «فقد نصره» indicate it; the implied form is: "If you do not help him, He will help him." Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned two views on it, one of them being what has preceded. The second, he said: "He made help obligatory for him and made him helped at that time, so he will not be forsaken after it." The Shaykh said: "From this the apodosis of the condition does not appear, because making help obligatory for him is something that preceded, and the past does not follow upon the future; so what appears [correct] is the first view."
His words: {ثَانِيَ اثنين}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «أخرجه». The meaning of the annexation in this kind of construction has preceded at His words {ثَالِثُ ثَلاَثَةٍ} [al-Māʾida: 73]. A group read «ثاني اثنين» with sukūn on the yāʾ. Abū al-Fatḥ said: "Abū ʿAmr reported it." Its justification is that he made the yāʾ vowelless, likening it to the alif; some restrict this to poetic necessity.
His words: {إِذْ هُمَا فِي الغار}: a badal (substitute) of the first «إذ», so what governs it is «فقد نَصَره». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Whoever denies that what governs the badal is what governs the thing substituted for supposes another governor, i.e. He helped him «إذ هما في الغار»."
«الغار» is a hollow in a mountain; it is pluralised as غِيران, like تاج and تِيْجان, قاع and قِيعان. Al-ghār is also a sweet-smelling plant, al-ghār is also a group, and al-ghārān are the belly and the private parts. The alif of al-ghār is from wāw.
His words: {إِذْ يَقُولُ}: a second badal of the first «إذ». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«إذ هما في الغار» and «إذ يقول» are two adverbials of «ثاني اثنين»." The pronoun in «عليه» refers back to Abū Bakr, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ always had tranquillity upon him. The discussion of {السكينة} [al-Baqara: 248] has preceded. The pronoun in «أيَّده» is for the Prophet ﷺ. Mujāhid read «وأَيَدَه» without doubling. «لم تَرَوْها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنود».
His words: {وَكَلِمَةُ الله هِيَ العليا}: the majority read «كلمة» in the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). «هي» may be a second mubtadaʾ, with «العُلْيا» its khabar (predicate) and the clause the khabar of the first; or «هي» may be a separating pronoun (faṣl) and «العليا» the khabar. It was also read «وكلمةَ الله» in the accusative, coordinated with the two objects of جَعَلَ, i.e. "and He made the word of Allah the highest". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak for three reasons. First: putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, since the proper way is to say وكَلِمَتُه. Second: it implies that the word of Allah was the lowest and then became the highest, which is not so. Third: emphasising such a thing with «هي» is far-fetched, since analogy requires «إياها»." I say: as for the first, there is no weakness in it, because the Qur'an is full of this kind, and it is among the best [usages], because there is magnification and exaltation in it. As for the second, what he mentioned does not follow, namely that the thing made into [something] was in the specific opposite state; rather, the "making" indicates the passing of that thing from some state to this state. As for the third, «هي» is not emphasis at all; «هي» is only a separating pronoun as it stands. How could it be emphasis, when the grammarians have stated explicitly that a pronoun does not emphasise an overt noun?

semin-durr:41-41.t: {خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً} is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «انفروا».

semin-durr:42-42.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لَوْ كَانَ عَرَضاً}: the noun (ism) of kāna is a pronoun referring back to what the context indicates, i.e. "had what you called them to been…". ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Aʿraj read «بَعِدَت» with kasra on the middle radical. ʿĪsā also read «الشِّقَّة» with kasra on the shīn. Abū Ḥātim said: "Both are the dialect of Tamīm."
Al-shuqqa is the land which is traversed (yushaqqu) with difficulty; it is derived from al-shiqq or al-mashaqqa (hardship).
His words: {بالله}: attached to «سَيَحْلِفُون». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«بالله» is attached to «سَيَحْلِفُون», or it is part of their speech, the [verb of] saying being intended in both views; i.e. they will swear — meaning those who stayed behind, when you return, making excuses — saying: 'By Allah, had we been able…'; or: and they will swear by Allah, saying: 'Had we been able…'. And His words «لَخَرَجْنا» fill the place of both the answer of the oath and [that of] «لو»." The Shaykh said: "His saying that «لخَرَجْنا» fills the place of both the answer of the oath and «لو» is not good. Rather, the grammarians have two doctrines on such a case. One: «لَخَرَجْنا» is the answer of the oath, and the answer of «لو» is omitted, according to the rule for the combination of oath and condition, since the oath precedes the condition; this is the choice of Abū al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUṣfūr. The other: «لَخَرَجْنا» is the answer of «لو», and «لو» with its answer is the answer of the oath; this is the choice of Ibn Mālik. As for «لَخَرَجْنا» filling the place of both, I know of no one who held that. His words may be interpreted as meaning that, since the answer of «لو» was omitted and the answer of the oath indicated it, it was treated as if it filled the place of both the answer of the oath and the answer of لو."
Al-Aʿmash and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «لوُ اسْتَطَعْنا» with ḍamma on the wāw, as though they fled from the kasra on the wāw, even though it is the base; they likened the wāw of «لو» to the wāw of the pronoun, just as they likened the wāw of the pronoun to the wāw of «لو» when they gave it kasra, as in {اشتروا الضلالة} [al-Baqara: 16], because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. Al-Ḥasan read «اشْتَرَوَا الضلالة» and «لوَ استطعنا» with fatḥa on the wāw, for lightness.
His words: {يُهْلِكُونَ}: there are three views on this clause. First: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «سَيَحْلِفُون», i.e. they will swear, destroying themselves. Second: it is a badal (substitute) of the clause before it, «سَيَحْلِفون». Third: it is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «لَخَرَجْنا». Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these three views, saying: "«يُهْلِكون» is either a badal of «سيحلفون» or a ḥāl in the sense of 'destroying'. The meaning is that they cast themselves into destruction by their false swearing. It may be a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «خَرَجْنا», i.e. we would have gone out even if we destroyed ourselves. It came in the third-person form because He is giving information about them. Do you not see that if it were said: 'they will swear by Allah, had they been able they would have gone out', it would be sound? One says: حَلَفَ بالله ليفعلن and لأفعلن; the third person follows the rule of reporting, and the first person follows that of quotation."
The Shaykh said: "As for «يُهْلِكون» being a badal of «سَيَحْلِفون», it is far-fetched, because destroying is neither synonymous with swearing nor a kind of it, and a verb is substituted for a verb only if it is synonymous with it or a kind of it." I say: the badal is valid in the sense of a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because swearing is a cause of destruction and so includes it; the effect was substituted for its cause because the cause includes it. It has many parallels, among them his words:
2487 - إنَّ عليَّ اللَّهَ أن تُبايعا ... تُؤْخَذَ كَرْهاً أو تجيءَ طائعاً
(I owe it to Allah that you shall give allegiance: be taken by force or come willingly.)
«تُؤْخَذ» is a badal of «تبايع», a badal of inclusion in the sense mentioned, and neither is a kind of the other. Then the Shaykh said: "As for its being a ḥāl of His words «لخرجنا», [what appears is that it is not permissible, because His words «لخَرَجْنا»] contain the pronoun of the speaker, so what is predicated of it can only be with the pronoun of the speaker. Were it a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «لخَرَجنا», the construction would be: نُهْلك أنفسنا, i.e. destroying ourselves. As for his drawing an analogy with «حَلَفَ زيد ليفعلن» and «لأفعلنَّ», it is not correct, because if he treats it according to the third-person pronoun, he does not go out of it to the pronoun of the speaker. Were you to say «حَلَفَ زيد ليفعلن وأنا قائم», with «وأنا قائم» as a ḥāl of the pronoun of «ليفعلن», it would not be permissible; and likewise its reverse, as in «حَلَفَ زيدٌ لأفعلن يقوم», meaning 'standing', would not be permissible. As for his saying 'it came in the third-person form because He is giving information about them', it is a fallacy: He is not giving information about them by His words {لَوِ استطعنا لَخَرَجْنَا}; rather He is quoting the wording of their speech. Then he said: 'Do you not see that if it were said: had they been able they would have gone out, it would be sound…' to the end: that is correct speech, but the Exalted did not say it as information about them; rather it is quotation, and the ḥāl is part of their quoted speech, so it may not differ from the one it qualifies, since they share the governor. Were you to say «قال زيد خرجت يضرب خالداً», meaning 'I went out striking Khālid', it would not be permissible; and were you to say «قالت هند: خرج زيد اضربْ خالداً», meaning 'Zayd went out striking Khālid', it would not be permissible." End of quotation.
Fourth: it is a resumptive clause; Allah informed about them with it.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ}: «لِمَ» and «لهم» are both attached to أَذِنْتَ. That is permissible because the meanings of the two lāms differ: the first is causal and the second is for conveying [to the addressee]. The alif of the interrogative ما was dropped because it is in the genitive. Fronting the first preposition phrase is obligatory because it governs something that has the right to the head of the sentence. What the permission relates to is omitted. It may be staying behind, i.e. "why did you permit them to stay behind?", which the context indicates, from their excusing themselves for lagging behind him, upon him be peace. Or it may be going out, i.e. "why did you permit them to go out?", because their going out involves harm, such as discouraging [others] and the like, as {لَوْ خَرَجُواْ فِيكُم مَّا زَادُوكُمْ إِلاَّ خَبَالاً} [al-Tawba: 47] indicates.
His words: {حتى يَتَبَيَّنَ}: «حتى» may express the limit, or it may be causal. On both suppositions it is a preposition, meaning either "until" or [that of] the lām, with «أَنْ» implied after it putting the verb in the accusative; and it is attached to something omitted. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its implied form is: why did you not defer them until it became clear, or so that it might become clear. His words {لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ} indicate the omitted part. «حتى» may not be attached to «أَذِنْتَ», because that would require that he gave them permission up to this limit or for the sake of clarification, and he would not be reproached for that." Al-Ḥawfī said: "«حتى» is a limit for what the interrogative implies, i.e. he ought not to have given them permission until the excuse became clear to him." I say: there is some impropriety in this wording.

semin-durr:44-44.t: The words of the Exalted: {أَن يُجَاهِدُواْ}: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: it is what the asking for permission relates to, i.e. they do not ask your permission concerning striving; rather they go ahead with it without hesitation. The second: what the asking for permission relates to is omitted, and «أن يُجاهدوا» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its implied form being: "the believers do not ask your permission to go out or to stay behind out of dislike of striving; rather, when you command them with something, they hasten to it."

semin-durr:46-46.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لأَعَدُّواْ لَهُ عُدَّةً}: the generality read «عُدّة» with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the tāʾ of the feminine; it is the provisions, the mount and everything the traveller needs.
Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān and his son Muʿāwiya read «عُدَّهُ» likewise, except that in place of the tāʾ of the feminine he put the hāʾ of the third-person pronoun, referring back to the going out. There was disagreement on how to account for it. It was said: its origin is like the majority reading with the tāʾ of the feminine, but they drop it in annexation, like the tanwīn. Al-Farrāʾ counted among this His words, the Exalted: {وَإِقَامَ الصلاة} [al-Nūr: 37], and from it are the words of Zuhayr:
2488 - إنَّ الخَلِيْطَ أجَدُّوا البَيْنَ فانْجَرَدُوا ... وأَخْلَفُوك عِدَ الأمرِ الذي وَعدُوا
(The companions resolved on parting and went off quickly, and broke with you the promise of the matter they had promised.)
He means: عِدَّة الأمر. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "When he annexed it, he made the pronoun stand in for the tāʾ and dropped it; that is because العُدّ without tāʾ, and without supposing it, is something that comes out on the face [Translator's note: i.e. a pimple]." Abū Ḥātim said: "It is the plural of عُدَّة, like بُرّ, plural of بُرّة, and دُرّ, plural of دُرَّة; the proper form for it would be عُدَد, but that does not agree with the script of the muṣḥaf."
Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Abān, read «عِدَّهُ» with kasra on the ʿayn, annexed to the pronoun hāʾ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In my view it is a noun for what is prepared, like الذِّبْح and القِتْل." It was also read «عِدَّة» with kasra on the ʿayn and the tāʾ of the feminine, the meaning being a quantity of provisions and weapons, derived from al-ʿadad (number).
His words: {ولكن كَرِهَ الله}: the restriction (istidrāk) here requires reflection; that is why al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the position of the particle of restriction? I say: since His words {وَلَوْ أَرَادُواْ الخروج} convey the negation of their going out and of their preparing for the campaign, it was said: but Allah disliked [their setting out]; as if it were said: they did not go out, but they held back from going out because of [Allah's] dislike of their setting out; just as [you say: Zayd did not] treat me well, but he treated me badly." End of quotation. He means that the apparent sense of the verse requires that what follows «لكن» agrees with what precedes it, while it is established about it that it occurs only between two contraries, two contradictories, or two different things — with a disagreement over this last — so he needed the answer mentioned.
The Shaykh said: "The verse is not a parallel to this example," meaning: Zayd did not treat me well but he treated me badly, "because in the example «لكن» occurs between [two contraries, whereas in the verse «لكن» occurs between] two things that agree in meaning." I say: by "two contradictories" they mean negation and affirmation in wording, even if they meet in meaning, and that is not counted as agreement.
Al-tathbīṭ is hindering. One says: ثَبَّطْتُ زيداً, i.e. I hindered him from what he wanted; from their saying: ناقة ثَبِطَة, i.e. slow in pace. What is meant by His words «اقعدوا» is leaving [them] alone; it is a metonymy for their sluggishness, and [indicates] that they made themselves like women, or children, the chronically ill and those with excuses. Sitting [literally] is not meant, as in his words:
2489 - دَعِ المكارِم لا تَقْصِدْ لبُغْيَتها ... واقعُدْ فإنَّك أنت الطاعِمُ الكاسي
(Leave noble deeds, do not set out to seek them, and sit [at home], for you are the one who is fed and clothed.)

semin-durr:47-47.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لَوْ خَرَجُواْ فِيكُم}: i.e. in your army and in your company. It was said: «في» means "with", i.e. with you. The explanation of «الخبال» has preceded in Āl ʿImrān.
His words: {إِلاَّ خَبَالاً}: they allowed it to be a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) which is emptied (mufarragh), because «زاد» takes two objects. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "What is excepted from is not mentioned, so the exception is from the most general of the general, which is 'thing'; so it is a connected exception, because al-khabāl (corruption) is a part of the most general of the general; as though it were said: they would not have increased you in anything but corruption." They also allowed it to be a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), the meaning being: they would not have increased you in strength or might, but in corruption. This fits the view of whoever said that there was no corruption in the army of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; so said the Shaykh. This is questionable, because if there was no corruption in the army at all, how could something be excepted that did not exist and whose existence was not imagined?
His words: {خِلاَلَكُمْ}: accusative as an adverbial. Al-khilāl is the plural of خَلَل, which is the gap between two things; it is used figuratively for abstract things, so one says: "there is a flaw (khalal) in this matter".
Al-īḍāʿ is hastening. One says: أَوْضَعَ البعيرُ, i.e. it hastened in its pace. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
2490 - أرانا مُوضِعينَ لأَِمْرِ غيبٍ ... ونُسْحَرُ بالطعامِ والشراب
(I see us hastening toward a hidden matter, while we are beguiled by food and drink.)
Another said:
2491 - يا لَيْتَني فيها جَذَعْ ... أَخُبُّ فيها وأَضَعْ
(Would that I were a young man in it, trotting and hastening in it!)
The object of «أوضعوا» is omitted, i.e. they hastened their mounts, because the rider is faster than the walker. One says: وَضَعَتْ الناقةُ تَضَعُ when it hastens, and أوضعتها I [made it hasten]. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read {ما زادَكم إلا خَبالاً}, i.e. their going out would not have increased you [except in corruption]. Mujāhid and Muḥammad ibn Zayd read «ولأَوْفَضوا», which is also hastening, from His words, the Exalted: {إلى نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ} [al-Maʿārij: 43]. Ibn al-Zubayr read «وَلأَرْفَضُوا» with rāʾ, fāʾ and the dotted ḍād, from رَفَضَ, i.e. also hastened [Translator's note: so in the source; the verses cited below, and the closing remark, concern رَقَصَ (with qāf and ṣād) "to move quickly", and the reading is usually reported as «ولأرقصوا»]. Ḥassān said:
2492 - بزجاجةٍ رَقَصَتْ بما في جَوْفِها ... رَقْصِ القَلوصِ براكبٍ مستعجِلِ
(With a glass that danced with what was inside it, like the young she-camel's quick pace under a hurrying rider.)
And he said:
2493 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... والراقصاتِ إلى مِنَىً فالغَبْغَبِ
(… and by the [camels] hastening to Minā and then to al-Ghabghab.)
One says: رَفَضَ في مِشْيته رَفْضاً ورَفَضاناً.
His words: {يَبْغُونَكُمُ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «أَوْضَعوا», i.e. they would have hastened among you, seeking, i.e. seeking discord for you.
His words: {وَفِيكُمْ سَمَّاعُونَ لَهُمْ}: this clause may be a ḥāl of the object of «يَبْغُونكم» or of its fāʿil; that is permissible because the clause contains the pronouns of both. It may also be resumptive, the meaning being that among you are some who listen to them and give ear to their speech. Or what is meant may be: among you are spies of theirs who listen to news from you for them. On the first [meaning] the lām is for strengthening (taqwiya), because the governor is secondary [i.e. an intensive participle]; on the second it is causal, i.e. for their sake.
{ولا أَوْضَعُوا خلالكم} was written in the muṣḥaf with an alif after «لا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The fatḥa used to be written as an alif before the Arabic script, and the Arabic script was invented shortly before the revelation of the Qur'an; a trace of that remained in people's habits, so they wrote the form of the hamza as an alif and its fatḥa as another alif. Similar is {أَوْ لا أَذْبَحَنَّهُ} [al-Naml: 21]" — he means with regard to the addition of an alif after «لا». It is not permissible to read according to this, and whoever reads it [so] deliberately commits unbelief.

semin-durr:48-48.t: Maslama ibn Muḥārib read «وقَلَبوا» without doubling. His words «وهم كارهون» are a ḥāl (circumstantial), the link being the wāw.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مَّن يَقُولُ ائذن}: like His words {يَاصَالِحُ ائتنا} [al-Aʿrāf: 77], in that the hamza may be pronounced fully or changed into wāw because of the ḍamma before it, even though it is separated [as part of] another word. This hamza is the first radical of the word, and before it there was a connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) that dropped out in continuous speech. Abū Jaʿfar said: "When the wāw or the fāʾ enters upon «ائذن», it is spelled alif, dhāl, nūn, without yāʾ; or [when] «ثم» [enters], it is spelled alif, yāʾ, dhāl, nūn. The difference is that one may pause on «ثم» and it is separable, unlike those two." I say: he means that when the wāw or fāʾ of coordination enters this word, their connection with it becomes strong, so the connective hamza dropped in continuous speech is not taken into account and no form is written for it; so it is written «فَأْذَنْ، وَأْذَنْ», this alif being the form of the hamza that is the first radical of the word. When «ثم» enters upon it, it is written thus: {ثُمَّ ائتوا}; they took account of the connective hamza and wrote a form for it. I say: it is as though this rule he mentioned with «ثم» is specific to this word; otherwise, for other words whose first radical is hamza, the form of the connective hamza is dropped in writing, so the imperative from al-ityān with «ثم» is written thus: «ثم أْتُوا»; and the analogy with «ثمَّ ائْذَنْ» would have been «ثم ائتوا». This is questionable.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Ismāʿīl al-Makkī, in what Ibn Mujāhid related from him, read «ولا تُفْتِنِّي» with ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from the four-letter أفتنه. Abū Ḥātim said: "It is the dialect of Tamīm." It was said: أفتنه means "he brought him into it [i.e. temptation]". The poet combined the two dialects, saying:
2494 - لئن فَتَنَتْني فهي بالأمس أفتنتْ ... سعيداً فأمسى قد قلا كلَّ مسلم
(If she has tempted me, well, yesterday she tempted Saʿīd, and he came to loathe every Muslim.)
What the permission relates to is staying behind, i.e. "permit me to stay behind and lag back from [facing] the enemy, and do not tempt me by my going out with you."

semin-durr:51-51.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لَّن يُصِيبَنَآ}: ʿAmr ibn Shaqīq said: "I heard Aʿyun, the judge of al-Rayy, read «لن يُصيبَنَّا» with a doubled nūn." Abū Ḥātim said: "That is not permissible, because the nūn does not come with «لن». Had it been [the reading] of Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, it would have been permissible, because it is with «هل»; Allah the Exalted said: {هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُ مَا يَغِيظُ} [al-Ḥajj: 15]." I say: Abū Ḥātim means that the imperfect may be emphasised after an interrogative particle, and Ibn Muṣarrif reads «هل» instead of «لن»; it is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd.
An excuse was offered for this reading: it treated «لن» like the negative «لم» and «لا», after which the negated verb may be emphasised. As for «لا», the verification of the discussion on it preceded in al-Anfāl. As for «لم», that has been heard, and they recited:
2495 - يَحْسَبُه الجاهل ما لم يَعْلما ... شيخاً على كرسيِّه مُعَمَّمَا
(The ignorant, as long as he does not know, takes it for an old man on his chair wearing a turban.)
He meant «يَعْلَمَنْ», and changed the light [nūn] into alif after a fatḥa, like the tanwīn.
The judge and Ṭalḥa also read «هل يُصَيِّبُنا» with a doubled yāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its justification is that it is يُفَيْعِل, not يُفَعِّل, because it is from the wāw-roots, given their saying الصواب, صاب يصوب, and مصاوب as a plural of مصيبة; so the يُفَعِّل [form] from it would properly be يُصَوِّب — do you not see their saying صَوَّب رأيه? — unless it is from the dialect of those who say صاب السهمُ يَصيب, as in his words:
2496 - أَسْهُمِيَ الصائِبات والصُّيُبْ
(My arrows, those that hit and the hitting ones.)"
He means that its original form is صَوْيِب; the wāw and the yāʾ came together, the first of them being vowelless, so the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated into it, just as preceded for you in تحيَّز, whose original form is تَحَيْوَز. But if we take it from the dialect of those who say صاب السهم يَصيب, it is from the yāʾ-roots, and its pattern in this dialect is فَعَّل.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِلاَّ إِحْدَى}: the object of the waiting, so it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). Ibn Muḥayṣin read «إلا احدى» with the alif of «احدى» connected, treating the disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) like the connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl). It is like the words of the poet:
2497 - إنْ لم أُقاتِلْ فالبسوني بُرْقُعا
(If I do not fight, then dress me in a veil.)
and the words of the other:
2498 - يابا المغيرة رُبَّ أَمْرٍ مُعْضِلٍ ... فَرَّجْتُه بالمكر مِنِّي والدَّهَا
(O Abū al-Mughīra, many a perplexing matter I have resolved by my cunning and shrewdness.)
His words {أَن يُصِيبَكُمُ} are the object of the waiting.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
The words of the Exalted: {طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً}: two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. willingly or unwillingly. The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «كُرْهاً» with ḍamma; the verification of that has preceded in al-Nisāʾ.
The Shaykh said here: "Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Waththāb read «كُرْهاً» with ḍamma on the kāf." This gives the impression that it was not read among the Seven. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a command in the sense of a statement, like His words {فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ الرحمن مَدّاً} [Maryam: 75]. Its meaning is: it will not be accepted from you, whether you spend willingly or unwillingly. Similar are His words, the Exalted: {استغفر لَهُمْ أَوْ لاَ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ} [al-Tawba: 80], and his words — he means Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
2499 - أسِيْئي بنا أو أَحْسِني لا مَلُومَةٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Treat us badly or treat us well, [you are] not blamed …)
i.e. Allah will not forgive them whether you ask forgiveness or not, and we do not blame you whether you treat us well or badly. In its meaning are the words of the speaker:
2500 - أخوك الذي إنْ قُمْتَ بالسيفِ عامداً ... لتضربَهُ لم يَسْتَغِشَّك في الودِّ
(Your [true] brother is the one who, if you rose with the sword intending to strike him, would not suspect your affection of deceit.)"
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is a command containing a recompense [i.e. a conditional sense]; this holds in every command accompanied by a recompense. The implied form is: if you spend, it will not be accepted from you. But when the command is devoid of an answer, implication of a condition does not accompany it."
