The Shaykh said: "What impairs this account is that if the command has the sense of a condition, the answer would be [treated like] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition; on this view the construction would have to be «لن يُتقبل» with the fāʾ, because «لن» does not occur as the apodosis of a condition except with the fāʾ, and likewise what implies its meaning. Do you not see its making the answer jussive in such as: اقصد زيداً يُحْسِنْ إليك?" I say: Abū Muḥammad [Ibn ʿAṭiyya] only meant to explain the meaning; otherwise, he is not ignorant of such obvious matters. Moreover, it does not follow, because what is implied need not be given the ruling of the overt thing in every respect.
His words: {إِنَّكُمْ} and what follows function as a statement of cause.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَن تُقْبَلَ}: there are two views on it. First: it is the second object of «منع», either by supposing the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "from being accepted", or because the verb reaches it by itself, since you say: منعتُ زيداً حَقَّه and مِنْ حقه. Second: it is a badal (substitute) of «هم» in مَنْعِهم; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, as though he meant a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). There is no need for it.
There are two views on the fāʿil (agent) of «منع». The first, which is the apparent one: it is {إِلاَّ أَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُواْ}, i.e. nothing prevented them from the acceptance of their spending but their unbelief. The second: it is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, i.e. Allah did not prevent them, «إلا أنهم» then being accusative by the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "because they disbelieved".
The two brothers read «أن يُقْبَلَ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, and the rest with the upper-dotted tāʾ; both are clear, because the femininity is figurative. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read like the two brothers, except that he made النفقة singular. Al-Aʿraj read «تُقْبل» with the upper-dotted tāʾ and «نفقتُهم» in the singular. Al-Sulamī read «يَقبل» in the active, [the fāʿil] being Allah the Exalted. It was also read «نَقْبل» with the nūn of majesty, and «نفقتهم» in the singular.
His words: {إِلاَّ وَهُمْ كسالى} and {إِلاَّ وَهُمْ كَارِهُونَ}: both clauses are a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil before them.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
The words of the Exalted: {الحياة الدنيا}: there are two views on it. First: it is attached to «تعجبك», His words {إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ الله لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ بِهَا} being a parenthetical clause, the implied form being: "so let them not please you in the life [of this world]". The preposition phrase may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أموالهم». Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Suddī and Ibn Qutayba inclined to this; they said: in the speech there is fronting and postponing, and the meaning is: "so let not their wealth nor their children please you in the life of this world; Allah only intends to punish them by them in the Hereafter." The Shaykh said: "However, as for restricting the forbidden admiration that arises from their wealth and children, it is known that it can only be in the life of this world, so that remains like an additional emphasis; unlike the punishment, which may be in this world as it may be in the Hereafter. Moreover, our colleagues restrict fronting and postponing to poetic necessity." I say: how can it be said, despite the explicit statement of those I mentioned, "our colleagues restrict that to poetic necessity"? Besides, it has nothing to do with the fronting and postponing that occurs in poetic necessity; it is only a parenthesis, and of a parenthesis one does not say "fronting and postponing" in the technical sense restricted to poetic necessity. Their naming it so — I mean Ibn ʿAbbās and those with him, may Allah be pleased with them — they only intend by it the parenthesis indicated, not what the people of the craft restrict to poetic necessity.
Second: «في الحياة» is attached to the punishment, what is meant by worldly punishment being the misfortunes and calamities of this world, or the burdensome obligations imposed on them, for which they hope for no reward — Ibn Zayd said this — or the zakāts imposed on them — al-Ḥasan said this. On this view the pronoun in «بها» refers back to the wealth only, while on the first it refers back to the children and the wealth.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مَلْجَئاً أَوْ مَغَارَاتٍ}: al-maljaʾ is the fortress; it was said: the place of escape; and it was said: the place of safekeeping. It is a مَفْعَل from لجأ إليه يلجأ, i.e. he withdrew [to it]. One says: ألجأته إلى كذا, i.e. I compelled him to it, so he took refuge (iltajaʾa). Al-maljaʾ is suitable for the maṣdar, the time and the place; what is apparent here is the place. Al-maghārāt is the plural of مغارة, a مَفْعَلة from غار يغور (to sink in), so it is like al-ghār (cave) in meaning. It was said: al-maghāra is a burrow in the ground, like the tunnel of the jerboa; and al-ghār is a hollow in a mountain.
The majority read «مغارات» with fatḥa on the mīm. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf read «مُغارات» with ḍamma; it is from أغار. أغار may be intransitive — the Arabs say أغار meaning غار, i.e. he entered — or transitive: you say أَغَرْتُ زيداً, i.e. I made him enter the cave. On this view it is from the transitive أغار, with the object omitted, i.e. places in which they make themselves enter, i.e. hide themselves.
Al-muddakhal is a مُفْتَعَل from al-dukhūl (entering); it is a form of intensification in this meaning. The original is مُدْتَخل, then the dāl was assimilated into the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form, like ادَّان from al-dayn. Qatāda, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Aʿmash read «مُدَّخَّلاً» with doubling of both the dāl and the khāʾ. Its justification is that the original is مُتَدَخَّلاً, from the doubled تَدخَّل; when the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl, the word became مُدَّخَّلاً, like مُدَّيَّن from تَدَيَّن. Al-Ḥasan also, Maslama ibn Muḥārib, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Ibn Kathīr in one transmission read «مَدْخَلاً» with fatḥa on the mīm, sukūn on the dāl and a light fatḥa on the khāʾ, from دخل. Al-Ḥasan in the transmission of Maḥbūb read likewise, except that he gave the mīm ḍamma, making it from أدخل.
This is among the most brilliant of knowledge: He first mentioned the most general thing, namely a refuge of whatever kind; then He mentioned the caves in which one hides in the highest places and in the mountains; then the places in which one hides in the low places, namely the burrows, which He expressed by al-muddakhal.
Al-Zajjāj said: "It is valid for al-maghārāt to be from their saying حَبْل مُغار, i.e. firmly twisted; then that is used figuratively for a firm, settled matter. On this view the interpretation is: if they found help, or well-directed, interconnected matters that would protect them from you." He also made al-muddakhal [mean] a people whose company they would enter.
Ubayy read «مُنْدَخَلاً» with nūn after the mīm, from اندخل. He said:
2501 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا يدي في حَمِيتِ السَّمْنِ تَنْدَخِلُ
(… nor does my hand go into the skin of clarified butter.)
Abū Ḥātim denied this reading from him and said: "It is only with tāʾ." I say: he is excused, because انفعل is intransitive and does not take an object, so how could a passive participle be formed from it?
Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read «لَوَالَوا», i.e. they gave allegiance and hastened; likewise Ibn Abī ʿUbayda ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Nawfal related it from his father from his grandfather, who was a Companion — from al-muwālāt (alliance). This is among the cases in which فَعَّل and فاعَل have one meaning, as in ضَعَّفْتُه and ضاعَفْتُه. Saʿīd ibn Muslim said: "I think it is «لَوَأَلُوا», with a hamza bearing fatḥa after the wāw, from وَأَلَ, i.e. he took refuge." Al-Zamakhsharī transmitted this reading and explained it as taking refuge, as preceded.
Al-jumūḥ is bolting away swiftly; from it is فرس جَموح, when the bridle does not hold it back. He said:
2502 - جَمُوحاً مَرُوحاً وإحضارُها ... كمَعْمَعَةِ السَّعَفِ المُؤْقَدِ
(Bolting, lively, and her gallop is like the crackling of burning palm-fronds.)
Another said:
2503 - إذا جَمَحَتْ نساؤكُمُ إليه ... أَشَظَّ كأنه مَسَدٌ مُغَارُ
(When your women rush to him, he stiffens as though he were a firmly twisted rope.)
Another said:
2504 - وقد جَمَحْتُ جِماحاً في دمائِهمُ ... حتى رأيتُ ذوي أحسابِهم جَهَزوا
(I rushed headlong into their blood until I saw their men of noble lineage finished off.)
Anas ibn Mālik and al-Aʿmash read «يَجْمِزُون». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "[It means] they trot in their walking." It was said: يَجْمِزُون, يَجْمَحون and يشتدُّون have one meaning. In the ḥadīth: "When the stones struck him painfully, he ran off (jamaza)." Ruʾba said:
2505 - إمَّا تَرَيْني اليومَ أمَّ حَمْزِ ... قارَبْتُ بين عَنَقي وجَمْزي
(If you see me today, O Umm Ḥamz, [you see that] I have brought my stride and my trot close together.)
This is its origin in the language.
His words: {إِلَيْهِ}: the pronoun refers back to the refuge or to the muddakhal, because the coordination is with «أو»; it may also refer back to «المَغَارات» by interpreting it as a masculine.
His words: {مَّن يَلْمِزُكَ}: the generality read «يلمِزك» with kasra on the mīm, from لَمَزه يَلْمِزه, i.e. he found fault with him; its origin is signalling with the eye and the like. Al-Azharī said: "Its origin is pushing: لَمَزْته means I pushed him." Al-Layth said: "It is winking in the face; from it is هُمَزَةٌ لُمَزَة, i.e. one who does these two acts much."
Yaʿqūb, Ḥammād ibn Salama from Ibn Kathīr, al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read it with ḍamma on it [the mīm], and it was also related from Abū ʿAmr; they are two dialects in the imperfect. Al-Aʿmash read «يُلْمِزُك», from the four-letter ألمز. Ḥammād ibn Salama related «يُلامِزُك», on the form of mufāʿala from one party, like سافرَ and عاقَب.
The discussion of «إذا» of surprise has preceded many times. As for what governs it: Abū al-Baqāʾ said «يَسْخَطون», because he said that it is an adverb of place; this is questionable, as preceded in its parallel.

semin-durr:59-59.t: The words of the Exalted: {وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ رَضُوْاْ}: what is apparent is that the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, its implied form being: "it would have been better for them". It was said: its apodosis is «وقالوا», the wāw being redundant (zāʾida); this is the doctrine of the Kufans. His words «سيُؤْتينا» and «إنَّا إلى الله راغبون»: these two clauses are like an explanation of their saying "Allah is sufficient for us"; that is why they were not [Translator's note: the source has «يم», a misprint for «لم»] conjoined, because they are like one thing; the strength of the connection prevented coordination.

semin-durr:60-60.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَرِيضَةً}: there are two views on its accusative. First: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the sense, because the meaning of «إنما الصدقات للفقراء» amounts to: Allah has prescribed that. Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الفقراء»; al-Kirmānī and Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, meaning: of the pronoun latent in the preposition phrase because it occurs as a khabar (predicate), i.e. the alms are for them, being an obligation, i.e. obligatory. In that case «فريضة» may be in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūla), the tāʾ having entered only because it is treated like nouns, like النَّطيحة; or it may be a maṣdar occurring in the place of a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why did He turn from the lām to «في» in the last four? I say: to indicate that they are more firmly established in deserving to receive alms than those mentioned before, because «في» is for containment; so He drew attention to the fact that they are worthy of having alms placed in them and of being made a likely place and a receptacle for it." Then he said: "The repetition of «في» in His words {وَفِي سَبِيلِ الله وابن السبيل} gives these two an extra preference over the slaves and the debtors."
It was transmitted from Sībawayh that «فريضة» is accusative by its implied verb, i.e. Allah prescribed that as an obligation. It was transmitted from al-Farrāʾ that it is accusative by way of "cutting off" (al-qaṭʿ).
It was also read «فريضةٌ» in the nominative, on [the implied form]: "that is an obligation".
The origin of al-ghurm is the binding of something burdensome; from it, passionate love was called gharām, and it is used to express destruction in His words, the Exalted: {إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً} [al-Furqān: 65]. Paying a fine (gharāma) of wealth involves great hardship.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَّكُمْ}: «أُذُن» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "say: he is an ear of good". The majority read «خيرٍ» in the genitive by annexation. Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «أُذنٌ» with tanwīn and «خيرٌ» in the nominative. There are two views on it. First: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «أُذُن». Second: it is a khabar after a khabar. «خير» may be an adjective without [the sense of] preference, i.e. "an ear possessing good for you", or it may express preference in its basic sense, i.e. "more good for you". The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» allowed «أذن» to be a mubtadaʾ and «خير» its khabar; beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible here because it is qualified by implication, i.e. "an ear that does not take you to task is better for you than an ear that takes you to task".
One says: رَجُلٌ أُذُنٌ, i.e. [a man who] listens to everything that is said. There are two interpretations of it. First: he was named by the organ because it is the instrument of hearing, which is the principal thing intended of him, like their calling the scout "an eye". It was said: what is meant by the ear here is the organ, in which case it involves the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "possessor of an ear". Second: أُذُن is an adjective on the pattern فُعُل, like أُنُف and شُلُل; one says أَذِن يَأْذَن, so he is أُذُن. He said:
2506 - وقد صِرْتَ أُذْناً للوُشاة سَميعةً ... ينالُون مِنْ عِرْضي ولو شئتَ ما نالوا
(You have become an ear for the slanderers, listening keenly; they attack my honour, and had you wished, they would not have.)
His words: {وَرَحْمَةٌ}: the majority read «ورحمة» in the nominative, coordinated with «أذن ورحمة» among those who read «رحمة» in the nominative [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is that it is coordinated with «أذن»]. Some said: it is conjoined to «يؤمن», because «يؤمن» is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «أذن», the implied form being: "an ear that believes, and a mercy". Ḥamza and al-Aʿmash read «ورحمةٍ» in the genitive, coordinated with «خير», which is in the genitive through the annexation of «أذن» to it; on this reading the clause is parenthetical between the two conjoined words, the implied form being: "an ear of good and of mercy". Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ورحمةً» in the accusative, as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), what it explains being omitted, i.e. "he listens to you out of mercy towards you"; it was omitted because His words {قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ} indicate it.
The bāʾ and the lām in «يؤمن بالله» and «ويؤمن للمؤمنين» are both transitivising; the discussion of them has preceded at the beginning of this topic. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He intended belief in Allah, which is the opposite of unbelief, so He made it transitive with the bāʾ; and He intended listening to the believers and accepting what they say, so He made it transitive with the lām. Do you not see His words {وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَادِقِينَ} [Yūsuf: 17]? How far it is from the bāʾ! Similar are {فَمَآ آمَنَ لموسى} [Yūnus: 83], {أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ واتبعك الأرذلون} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 111] and {آمَنتُمْ لَهُ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 49]." Ibn Qutayba said: "Both are redundant (zāʾida), and the meaning is: he believes Allah and believes the believers." This is a rejected view; what shows that they are not redundant is the difference between the redundant particles: had an independent meaning not been intended, He would not have differentiated between the two particles. Al-Mubarrad said: "It is attached to a maṣdar implied from the verb, as though He said: and his faith for the believers." It was said: one says آمنتُ لك meaning "I believed you", and from it is {وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا}. In my view this lām implies «ما», so the meaning is: and he believes the believers in what they tell him. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The lām in «للمؤمنين» is redundant; it entered to distinguish between «يؤمن» meaning 'believes [someone]' and يؤمن meaning 'establishes faith'."

semin-durr:62-62.t:
The words of the Exalted: {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ}: He made the pronoun in «يُرْضوه» singular, even though the rule in coordination with the wāw is agreement, for several reasons. First: the pleasure of Allah and of His Messenger is one thing — whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed [Allah], {إِنَّ الذين يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ الله} [al-Fatḥ: 10] — so He made the two pronouns one pronoun to draw attention to that. Second: the pronoun refers back to the two in the singular form by interpreting [it as] "what has been mentioned", like the words of Ruʾba:
2507 - فيها خطوطٌ مِنْ سوادٍ وبَلَقْ ... كأنه في الجلد تَوْلِيْعُ البَهَقْ
(In it are streaks of black and piebald white, as though it were, on the skin, the blotching of leucoderma.)
i.e. as though that which has been mentioned. The explanation of this has preceded for you at the beginning of al-Baqara. Third: al-Mubarrad said: "In the speech there is fronting and postponing, its implied form being: and Allah is more deserving that they please Him, and His Messenger." I say: this is according to the opinion of those who claim the omission from the second. Fourth, which is the doctrine of Sībawayh: He omitted the khabar (predicate) of the first and retained the khabar of the second. This is better than its reverse, which is the view of al-Mubarrad, because it avoids separating the mubtadaʾ (subject) from its khabar [Translator's note: the source has «المبتدأ أو خبره», a misprint for «المبتدأ وخبره»], and also because it involves predicating a thing of what is nearest to it; moreover, it is the only possible [analysis] in the words of the poet:
2508 - نحن بما عندنا وأنت بما ... عندكَ راضٍ والرأيُ مختلفُ
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, and opinion differs.)
i.e. "we are content (rāḍūn)"; «راضون» was omitted because the khabar of the second indicates it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The doctrine of Sībawayh is that they are two clauses, the first having been omitted because the second indicates it." The Shaykh said: "If the pronoun in «أنهما» refers back to each of the two clauses, how can he say 'the first was omitted', when the first was not omitted, only its khabar? And if it refers back to the khabar, namely {أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ}, it is a clause only if one holds that «أن يُرْضُوه» is a mubtadaʾ with «أحقُّ» as its khabar placed before it; and this view is not necessary, since the khabar may be a single word, the implied form being: أحقُّ بأَنْ تُرْضوه." I say: Abū Muḥammad [Ibn ʿAṭiyya] only intended the first analysis, which is the well-known one among the grammatical analysts: they make «أحق» a fronted khabar and «أن يرضوه» a postponed mubtadaʾ, [i.e.] "and Allah and His Messenger — pleasing Him is more deserving". The detailed treatment of this preceded recently at His words {فالله أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَوْهُ} [al-Tawba: 13].
{إِن كَانُواْ مُؤْمِنِينَ} is a condition whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted or placed before it.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَلَمْ يعلموا}: the majority read «يَعْلموا» with the yāʾ of the absent [third person], referring back to the hypocrites. Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj read «تَعْلموا» with the tāʾ of address. It was said: it is an iltifāt (shift of person) from absence to address, if the hypocrites are meant. It was said: the address is to the Prophet, upon him be peace, and the plural form was used to honour him, as in his words:
2509 - وإن شِئْتِ حرَّمْتُ النساءَ سواكم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And if you wish, I will forbid myself all women other than you [pl.] …)
And it was said: the address is to the believers. With these three suppositions the meaning of the interrogative differs: on the first, the interrogative is for rebuke and reproach; on the second, it expresses wonder at their state; on the third, it is for affirmation (taqrīr).
Knowing (al-ʿilm) here may be in its basic sense, so that «أَنْ» fills the place of two objects according to Sībawayh, and the place of one of them, the other being omitted, according to al-Akhfash; or it may be in the sense of recognising, so that «أنَّ» fills the place of one object. «مَنْ» is conditional, and {فَأَنَّ لَهُ نَارَ} is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «أنَّ» was given fatḥa after the fāʾ for what is known from al-Anʿām. The conditional clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the first «أنَّ».
This is a clear account, yet a group turned away from this clear one to other views. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«فأنَّ له» may be conjoined to «أنه», on the view that the apodosis of «مَنْ» is omitted, its implied form being: Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger will perish, and that for him…" Al-Jarmī and al-Mubarrad said: the second «أنَّ» is repeated for emphasis, as though the implied form were: "then for him is the Fire of Hell", and «أنَّ» was repeated for emphasis. Abū al-Baqāʾ likened it to His words, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ عَمِلُواْ السواء} [al-Naḥl: 119], then He said: {إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِن بَعْدِهَا}. He said: "On this view the fāʾ is [the fāʾ of] the apodosis of the condition."
The Shaykh rebutted al-Zamakhsharī's view on the grounds that they stated explicitly that when the apodosis of a condition is omitted, the verb of the condition must be past, or imperfect joined with «لم»; while on his view the apodosis is omitted and the verb of the condition is an imperfect not joined with «لم». "Moreover, we find the speech complete without what he supposed."
It was transmitted from Sībawayh that he said: "The second is a badal (substitute) of the first." This is not authentic from Sībawayh, for it is weak or impossible. Abū al-Baqāʾ judged it weak for two reasons. "First: the fāʾ prevents that, and declaring it redundant is weak. Second: making it a badal entails the loss of the apodosis of «مَنْ» from the speech." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is objected to on the grounds that nothing is substituted for a thing until it is complete, and the first [أنّ] here has not yet received its khabar, since the apodosis of the condition has not yet come, and that clause is the khabar. Moreover, the fāʾ resists the badal; [moreover,] it has another meaning than the badal, so the badal is awkward."
Some said: "It must be on the supposition of the lām, i.e. 'then because for him is the Fire of Hell'; on this view something must be implied to complete the apodosis of the condition, its implied form being: then his opposition is because for him is the Fire of Hell."
All these are needless contrivances. The best is what preceded, what he [Translator's note: so in the source, «فالأولى ما تقدم ما ذكره»; the antecedent of "he" is unclear] mentioned: namely, that {فَأَنَّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ} is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar is omitted; and you ought to suppose it placed before it, as al-Zamakhsharī and others did, i.e. "then it is true that for him is the Fire of Hell". Someone else supposed it placed after it, i.e. "then that for him is the Fire of Hell is necessary"; so al-Akhfash supposed it. They rebutted him on the grounds that one does not begin with it; but this is not binding on him, for he permits beginning with «أنَّ» with fatḥa without fronting a khabar, while others do not permit beginning with it except on condition that «أمَّا» precedes, as in «أمَّا أنك ذاهبٌ فعندي», or on condition that the khabar precedes, as in «عندي أنَّك مُنْطَلق». It was also said: «فأنَّ له» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then what is necessary is that for him…". This clause after the fāʾ, together with the fāʾ, is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition.
Abū ʿAmr, in what Abū ʿUbayda related, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī ʿAbla [Translator's note: the source has «وابن لأبي عبلة», a misprint] read «فإنَّ» with kasra; it is a good, strong reading. It has preceded that some of the Seven read [with it] in al-Anʿām, and its justification preceded there.
Al-muḥādda is opposition, obstinacy, transgressing the limit and enmity. It was said: it is derived from al-ḥadd, the edge of the iron weapon with which one fights. It was said: from al-ḥadd meaning side, as though he is on a side other than his companion's side, like their saying شاقَّه, i.e. he was on a side (shiqq) other than his companion's side, and عاداه, i.e. he was on a bank (ʿudwa) other than his bank.
Some preferred the reading with kasra because it does not require supposing anything implied; and his words:
2510 - فَمَنْ يكُ سائلاً عني فإني ... وجِرْوَةَ لا تُعارُ ولا تُباعُ
(Whoever asks about me: I and Jirwa [my mare] — she is neither lent nor sold.)
were only transmitted with kasra. This is not binding, for it came according to one of the two permissible [forms]. «خالداً» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

semin-durr:64-64.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَن تُنَزَّلَ}: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed in the accusative by «يحذر», for «يَحْذَر» is transitive by itself, because of His words, the Exalted: {وَيُحَذِّرْكُمُ الله نَفْسَهُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 30]; were it not transitive to one object originally, the doubling would not have given it a second object. What Sībawayh recited also indicates it:
2511 - حَذِرٌ أُموراً لا تَضيرُ وآمِنٌ ... ما ليسَ مُنْجيَه من الأَقْدارِ
(Wary of things that do no harm, and feeling safe from what will not save him from the decrees of fate.)
There is discussion about the verse: it was said to be fabricated, which is false; I set out its story carefully in «Sharḥ al-Tashīl». Al-Mubarrad said: "حَذِر is not transitive," saying: "because it is one of the states of the soul, like فَزِع." This does not follow, for among the states of the soul we have what is transitive, such as خاف and خشِي. So «تُنَزَّل», according to al-Mubarrad, is by the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "of [the] sending down". His words «تُنَبِّئهم» are in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «سورة».

semin-durr:65-65.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أبالله}: attached to His words «تستهزئون», and «تستهزئون» is the khabar (predicate) of kāna. It is evidence for the fronting of the khabar of kāna before it, because fronting what is governed indicates [the possibility of] fronting the governor; what is governed by the khabar has been placed before «كان», so fronting it [the khabar] should be permissible a fortiori. There is a point of discussion here: Ibn Mālik impugned this evidence with His words, the Exalted: {فَأَمَّا اليتيم فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ وَأَمَّا السآئل فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ} [al-Ḍuḥā: 9-10]. He said: "اليتيم and السائل have been placed before the prohibitive «لا», and what governs them is what comes after it; yet what follows the prohibitive «لا» may not be placed before it, since it is made jussive by it. So what is governed has been fronted where the governor may not be fronted." He mentioned that in connection with their adducing, for the permissibility of fronting the khabar of laysa, His words: {أَلاَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفاً عَنْهُمْ} [Hūd: 8].
Al-iʿtidhār is disavowing a sin. Its origin is from تعذَّرت المنازل, i.e. the dwellings became effaced and their traces were wiped out. Ibn Aḥmar said:
2512 - قد كنتَ تعرف آياتٍ فقد جعلَتْ ... أطلالُ إلفِك بالوَعْساء تعتذِرُ
(You used to know [its] signs, but the ruins of your beloved's abode in the sandy ground have begun to be effaced.)
So the one who apologises tries to wipe out his sin. It was said: its origin is from al-ʿadhr, which is cutting; from it is al-ʿudhra (virginity), because it is severed by defloration. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "They say: اعتذرت [المياه, i.e. the waters were cut off; and it is as though the one who apologises tries] to cut off blame from himself."

semin-durr:66-66.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِن نَّعْفُ}: ʿĀṣim read «نَعْفُ» with the nūn of majesty, and «نُعَذِّب» likewise, with «طائفةً» in the accusative as an object; it is the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Zayd ibn ʿAlī. The rest read «يُعفَ» in both places [Translator's note: so in the source; the second verb is «تُعَذَّبْ»] with the lower-dotted yāʾ, in the passive, with «طائفةٌ» in the nominative as standing in place of the fāʿil (agent). What stands in place of the fāʿil in the first verb is the preposition phrase after it. Al-Jaḥdarī read «إن يَعْفُ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ in both, in the active, [the fāʿil] being the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, with «طائفة» in the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Mujāhid read «تَعْفُ» with the upper-dotted tāʾ in both, in the active, [the fāʿil] being the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, with «طائفةً» in the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. Mujāhid [also] read «تُعفَ» with the upper-dotted tāʾ in both, in the passive, with «طائفة» in the nominative because it stands in place of the fāʿil. [Translator's note: so in the source; Mujāhid is credited with two different readings.]
There are two views on what stands in place of the fāʿil in the first verb. First: it is the pronoun of the sins, i.e. "if these sins are pardoned". Second: it is the preposition phrase, the verb having been made feminine only according to the sense. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The proper way is the masculine, because what it is predicated of is the adverbial, as you say «سِيْرَ بالدابة» and do not say «سِيْرت بالدابة»; but he went by the meaning, as though it were said: 'if a party is shown mercy', so he made it feminine for that reason. It is unusual."

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying, the Exalted: {يَأْمُرُونَ}: This clause has no grammatical position, because it is explicative of His saying {بَعْضُهُمْ مِّن بَعْضٍ}; and likewise what is conjoined to «يَأْمرون».

semin-durr:68-68.t: His saying, the Exalted: {خَالِدِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first object of the promise, and it is a anticipated (muqaddara) ḥāl, because this state did not coincide with the promise. As for His saying «هي حَسْبُهم», this clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. And His saying «هي حسبهم»: this resumptive clause has no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source repeats this last remark.]

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قَوْمِ نُوحٍ}: a badal (substitute) for the relative noun before it. It may be a badal of the whole for the whole, if what is meant by «الذين» is only what is mentioned after it; and it may be a partial badal of the whole, if what is meant by it is more general than that.
And «المُؤْتَفكات» means "those overturned". One says: أَفَكْتُه فانتفك, that is, "I overturned it and it was overturned". The root indicates turning and changing about, and from it comes {يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 9], that is, "is turned away". The pronoun in «أَتَتْهم» may refer back to those mentioned earlier, and some restricted it to «المؤتفكات».

semin-durr:71-71.t: His saying, the Exalted: { [بَعْضُهُمْ] أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ}: whereas He said of the hypocrites {مِّن بَعْضٍ} [al-Tawba: 67], since there is no wilāya (mutual allegiance) among the hypocrites. As for His saying «يَأْمُرون», it is as in its counterpart above. The sīn in «سيرحمهم الله» is for the future, since what is meant is a particular mercy, namely what He has kept in store for them in the Hereafter. al-Zamakhsharī claimed that it indicates the certainty of the mercy and the reinforcement of the threat and the warning, as in: سأنتقم منك ("I shall take vengeance on you").

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {خَالِدِينَ}: an anticipated ḥāl, as stated above. And «العَدْن» means residing. One says: عَدَنَ بالمكان يَعْدِن عَدْناً, that is, "he settled and became established"; from it comes «المَعْدِن» (the mine), for the place where jewels are fixed. One also says عَدَن عُدُوناً, so it has two verbal nouns. This is the original sense of this word in the language; in exegesis they have mentioned many meanings for it. al-Aʿshā said, in the sense of residing:
2516 - وإن يَسْتضيفوا إلى حِلْمِهِ ... يُضافُوا إلى راجِحٍ قد عَدَنْ
(If they seek hospitality with his forbearance, they will be hosted by one steadfast, who has settled.)
that is, "he has become fixed and settled"; and from it «عَدَن» is the name of a city in Yemen, because of the many who reside in it.
His saying: {وَرِضْوَانٌ مِّنَ الله أَكْبَرُ}: the indefiniteness (of «رضوان») conveys a causal sense, that is: the least bit of good pleasure is greater than all that preceded of the gardens and their dwellings. [Translator's note: the source says «التكثير» ("making plentiful"); this is likely a slip for «التنكير» (indefiniteness), which is how it is rendered here.]

semin-durr:73-73.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ}: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If it is asked: how is the wāw good here, when the fāʾ would be more fitting in this place? There are three answers. The first: the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), and the estimate is: 'Do that while they deserve Hell', and that state is the state of their disbelief and hypocrisy. The second: the wāw is brought as a signal that an omitted verb is intended, its implied form being: 'and know that their abode is Hell'. The third: the speech has been carried according to the meaning, the meaning being that there has been gathered for them the punishment of this world, through jihad and harshness, and the punishment of the Hereafter, by making Hell their abode." But none of all this is needed; rather, this is a resumptive clause.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ أَنْ أَغْنَاهُمُ}: There are two possibilities in it. The first: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), that is: "they disliked and found fault with nothing except Allah's enriching them". It is of the type of their saying: ما لي عندك ذنبٌ إلا أَنْ أَحْسَنْت إليك ("I have no offence with you except that I did you good"), that is: "if there is any offence, it is this"; so it is mockery of them, as in the saying:
2517 - ولا عيبَ فينا غيرُ عِرْقٍ لمعشرٍ ... كرامٍ وأنَّا لا نَخُطُّ على النمل
(There is no fault in us except a lineage of noble folk, and that we do not write upon ants.)
and the saying of another:
2518 - ما نقِموا من بني أميةَ إلا ... أنهمْ يَحْلُمون إنْ غَضِبوا
وأنهم سادةُ الملوكِ ولا ... يَصْلحُ إلا عليهم العَرَبُ
(They resented nothing in the Banū Umayya except that they are forbearing when angered, and that they are the masters of kings, and the Arabs are fit to be ruled only by them.)
The second: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and on this the direct object is omitted, its implied form being: "and they did not resent faith in them except because of Allah's enriching them". The discussion of نَقِم has already preceded.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّنْ عَاهَدَ الله}: it contains the sense of an oath, therefore it was answered with His saying «لنصَّدَّقَنَّ»; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted because this answer indicates it, and you already know the rule on that. The lām is the preparatory lām (lām al-tawṭiʾa). Combining the oath with the preparatory lām is not precluded. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "There are two possibilities in it. One: its implied form is 'so he said: if He gives us...'. The second: that «عاهد» is in the sense of «قال» ('he said'), for a covenant is a statement." But there is no need for what he mentioned.
His saying: {لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ وَلَنَكُونَنَّ}: the majority read both with the heavy nūn, and al-Aʿmash with the light one.

semin-durr:77-77.t: The majority read «يَكذبون» with the light form (without shadda), and Abū Rajāʾ with the heavy form (with shadda).

semin-durr:78-78.t: The majority read «يَعْلموا» with the yāʾ (third person). ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Ḥasan and al-Sulamī read it with the address (tāʾ, second person), as an iltifāt (shift of address) directed to the believers rather than the hypocrites.

semin-durr:80-80.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), like your saying: «ضربتُه عشرين ضربةً» ("I struck him twenty strikes"); it is for the number of his times. As for His saying {استغفر لَهُمْ أَوْ لاَ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ}, the discussion of this has already preceded shortly after His saying {قُلْ أَنفِقُواْ طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً لَّن يُتَقَبَّلَ مِنكُمْ} [al-Tawba: 53], and that it is the counterpart of the saying:
2519 - أَسِيْئي بنا أو أَحْسِني لا مَلومةٌ ... لدينا ولا مَقْلِيَّةٌ إنْ تَقَلَّتِ
(Treat us ill or treat us well: you are not blamed with us, nor hated, if you hate.)

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كالذين مِن قَبْلِكُمْ}: There are several possibilities in it. The first: this kāf is in the position of the nominative, its implied form being "they are like those who…", so it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). The second: that it is in the position of the accusative. al-Zajjāj said: "The meaning is: He promised you a promise like that of those before you; so it is attached to «وَعَدَ»." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is shaky." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It may be attached to «يَسْتهزئون»", and in this there is great remoteness.
His saying: {كَانُواْ أَشَدَّ} is an explanation of their likeness to them and an illustration of their action. al-Farrāʾ made its position accusative by an implied verb, saying: "The comparison is from the side of the action, that is: you did as those before you did", so the kāf is in the position of the accusative. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and in the speech a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) is omitted, its implied form being 'a promise like the promise of those who…'." al-Zamakhsharī mentioned the nominative possibility given above and the possibility I put first from al-Farrāʾ, and likened it to the saying of al-Namir ibn Tawlab:
2513 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كاليوم مَطْلوباً ولا طَلَبا
(…like today, [I have never seen] one sought, nor one seeking.)
with the implied "I have not seen".
His saying: {كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ الَّذِينَ}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "an enjoyment like the enjoyment of those who…".
His saying: {كالذي خاضوا}: the kāf is like the one before it. There are several possibilities regarding «الذي». The first: that the meaning is "and you plunged a plunging like the plunging of those who plunged", the nūn being dropped for lightness, or the singular put in the place of the plural. The verification of this was given at the beginning of al-Baqara. So the described maṣdar and the muḍāf to the relative noun are omitted, and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) of the relative is implied as "خاضوه", the original being "خاضوا فيه", because it is made transitive by «في»; then latitude was allowed in it, the preposition was dropped, the pronoun became attached to the verb, and so its omission became permissible. Without this gradation the omission would not be permissible, for you know from what has passed that whenever the ʿāʾid is governed by a preposition, the condition for permitting its omission is that the relative noun be governed by the like of that preposition, and that the thing to which it is attached be the same, along with other conditions I mentioned earlier.
The second: that «الذي» is an adjective of a singular that conveys a plural, that is: "and you plunged a plunging like the plunging of the company who plunged", or "the group who plunged". The discussion of the ʿāʾid is as before.
The third: that «الذي» is a description of the maṣdar, and the estimate is: "and you plunged a plunging like the plunging that they plunged". On this the ʿāʾid is accusative without the mediation of a preposition. This possibility ought to be the preferred one, since there is no objection in it.
The fourth: that «الذي» occurs as a maṣdar-forming particle, and the estimate is "and you plunged a plunging like their plunging"; and likewise:
2514 - فَثَبَّتَ اللَّهُ ما آتاك مِنْ حسنٍ ... في المُرْسلين ونَصْراً كالذي نُصِروا
(May Allah make firm what He gave you of goodness among the messengers, and a victory like the one they were given.)
that is, "like their victory". And the saying of another:
2515 - يا أمَّ عمروٍ جزاكِ اللَّهُ مغفرةً ... رُدِّي عليَّ فؤادي كالذي كانا
(O Umm ʿAmr, may Allah reward you with forgiveness: return my heart to me as it was.)
that is, "like its being". It has already been mentioned that this is the school of al-Farrāʾ and Yūnus, and the Basrans' interpretation of this has also preceded. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the benefit of His saying {فاستمتعوا بِخَلاقِهِمْ كَمَا} when His saying {كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ} suffices without it, as «كالذي خاضوا» dispenses with saying 'and they plunged, so you plunged like those who plunged'? I say: its benefit is to censure the first group for enjoying what they were given and for their contentment with it instead of looking to the outcome and seeking success in the Hereafter, and to make the matter of enjoyment seem base and the one content with it abhorrent, and then to liken the state of those addressed to theirs. As for «وخُضْتُمْ كالذي خاضوا», it is conjoined to what precedes it, and is predicated of that, being independent through its predication to it of that introduction." He means that it dispenses with the construction being: "and they plunged, so you plunged like those who plunged".
In His saying {كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ الَّذِينَ} there is the placing of the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, for a subtle point: the original was «فاستمتعتم فخَلاقكم كما استمتعوا بخلاقِهم», but He brought them out in the form of the overt noun to disparage them, like His saying {لاَ تَعْبُدِ الشيطان إِنَّ الشيطان كَانَ للرحمن عَصِيّاً} [Maryam: 44], and like His saying before this {المنافقون والمنافقات بَعْضُهُمْ مِّن بَعْضٍ} and then {إِنَّ المنافقين هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ} [al-Tawba: 67]. Just as placing the overt noun in the place of the pronoun indicates magnification and exaltation, by it one also indicates the opposite, which is disparagement.

semin-durr:79-79.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يَلْمِزُونَ}: There are several possibilities in it. The first: that it is nominative through an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are those who…". The second: that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «من المؤمنين» a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المطَّوِّعين», and «في الصدقات» attached to «يَلْمِزون». And {وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَجِدُونَ} is conjoined to «المطَّوِّعين», that is: they find fault with the wealthy and the poor.
Makkī said: "«والذين» is genitive, conjoined to «المؤمنين»; and its being conjoined to «المطَّوِّعين» is not good, because the noun is not yet complete, since «فيسخرون» is conjoined to «يَلْمِزُون»." So al-Naḥḥās mentioned it in his «Iʿrāb», and in my view it is a slip on his part. I say: the matter is as he stated, for «المطَّوِّعين» is complete without needing anything else.
His saying {فَيَسْخَرُونَ} is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is the clause of His saying {سَخِرَ الله مِنْهُمْ}. This is the clearest iʿrāb said here. It was also said: {وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَجِدُونَ} is conjoined to «الذين يَلْمزون»; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it. This is not permissible, because it would necessitate predicating of them His saying {سَخِرَ الله مِنْهُمْ}, and this could only be if those who do not find were hypocrites; but if they were believers, how could Allah mock them? It was also said: {وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَجِدُونَ} is conjoined to the believers; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. The Shaykh said: "It is very remote." I say: the reason for its remoteness is that it suggests that those who do not find are not believers, because the basis of conjunction is to indicate difference; so it is as if it were said: "they find fault with the volunteers from these two classes: the believers and those who do not find", which would make those who do not find volunteers who are not believers.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «في الصدقات» is attached to «يَلْمِزون» and not to «المطَّوِّعين», lest a stranger intervene between them. This refutation is open to question, since His saying «من المؤمنين» is a ḥāl, and a ḥāl is not a stranger. What does show the refutation is that «يطَّوَّع» is made transitive only by «بـ», not by «في», and «في» being in the sense of «بـ» is contrary to the basic rule.
It was also said: {فَيَسْخَرُونَ} is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the fāʾ enters because of the sense of condition the mubtadaʾ contains. In this possibility there is remoteness, in that it comes close to the khabar being identical in meaning with the mubtadaʾ, for whoever finds fault with someone and winks at him knows that he is mocking him; so it would be like their saying: «سيد الجارية مالكها» ("the master of the girl is her owner").
The third: that its position is accusative by ishtighāl (an occupying verb), with an implied verb which {سَخِرَ الله مِنْهُمْ} explains by way of meaning, like: "He censured those who find fault; Allah mocked them." The fourth: that it is accusative as an expression of vilification (shatm). The fifth: that it is genitive as a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in «سِرَّهم ونجواهم».
It was also read «يُلْمزون» with a ḍamma on the mīm, and it has already been mentioned that it is a dialect form.
His saying {سَخِرَ الله} may be a plain statement, and it may be a supplication. The majority read «جُهدهم» with a ḍamma on the jīm. Ibn Hurmuz and a group read «جَهْدهم» with a fatḥa. It was said they are two dialect forms with one meaning. It was also said: the fatḥa form is hardship and the ḍamma form is capacity, as al-Qutabī said. It was also said: the ḍamma form is a small thing one lives on, and the fatḥa form is work.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ}: attached to «فرح». It is suitable for the maṣdar of «قعد», for its time and for its place; what is meant here is the maṣdar, that is: by their sitting and their staying in Medina.
His saying: {خِلاَفَ}: There are three possibilities in it. The first: that it is accusative as a maṣdar with an implied verb which «مَقْعدهم» indicates, because it is in the sense of «تخلَّفوا», that is: "they stayed behind in opposition to the Messenger of Allah". The second: that «خلاف» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and its governor is either «فرح» or «مَقْعد», that is: they rejoiced because of their opposing the Messenger of Allah, in that he went on to jihad and they stayed behind from it; or by their sitting because of opposing him. To this al-Ṭabarī, al-Zajjāj and Muʾarrij went, and it is supported by the reading of whoever read «خُلْف» with a ḍamma on the khāʾ and a sukūn on the lām. The third: that it is accusative as a circumstance of place/time (ẓarf), that is: after the Messenger of Allah. One says: «أقام زيد خلاف القوم», that is, "he stayed behind after their departure", and «خلاف» is used as a ẓarf. The poet said:
2520 - عَقَبَ الربيعُ خِلافَهُمْ فكأنما ... بَسَطَ الشَّواطِبُ بينهن حصيرا
(The spring followed after them, as though the palm-leaf splitters had spread a mat among them.)
and another said:
2521 - فقلْ للذي يَبْقى خِلاَفَ الذي مضى ... تَهَيَّأْ لأخرى مِثلها وكأنْ قَدِ
(So say to the one who remains after the one who has gone: prepare for another like it, as if it had already come.)
To this Abū ʿUbayda, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Akhfash went, and it is supported by the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Ḥaywa and ʿAmr ibn Maymūn «خَلْفَ» with a fatḥa on the khāʾ and a sukūn on the lām.

semin-durr:83-83.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِن رَّجَعَكَ}: «رجع» is used transitively, as in this noble verse, and its maṣdar is «الرَّجْع», as in {والسمآء ذَاتِ الرجع} [al-Ṭāriq: 11]; and it is used intransitively, like {وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجِعُونَ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 35] in the reading of whoever built it with the agent as subject, and its maṣdar is «الرجوع», like «الدخول».
His saying: {أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ}: this has already preceded. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is a ẓarf." The Shaykh said: "He means a ẓarf of time, and it is remote", because the apparent sense is that it is accusative as a maṣdar; and in the exegesis it is "the first expedition the Messenger of Allah went out on", so the meaning is "the first time of going out". al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «مرة» is an indefinite noun put in the place of «المرات» ('times') from the superlative, then why is the superlative noun annexed to it mentioned, when it indicates one of the times? I say: the more frequent of the two usages is «هند أكبرُ النساء وهي أكبرُهن» ('Hind is the eldest of the women, and she is the eldest of them'); then your saying «هي كبرى امرأة» you will hardly come across, but rather «هي أكبر امرأة وأول مرة وآخر مرة»."
His saying: {مَعَ الخالفين}: this ẓarf may be attached to «اقعدوا», and it may be attached to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl from the agent of «اقعدوا». «الخالِف» is the one who stays behind after the people. It was also said: «الخالف» is the corrupt, from «خَلَفَ», that is, "became corrupt", and from it «خُلوف فم الصائم» (the odour of the fasting person's mouth). What is meant by them is the women, the children and the incapable men, and therefore its plural form is permissible by predominance (taghlīb). Qatāda said: "The Khālifūn are the women", which is rejected because of the plural form. ʿIkrima and Mālik ibn Dīnār read «مع الخَلِفين», shortened from «الخالِفين», like his saying:
2523 - مثل النَّقَا لَبَّده بَرْدُ الظِّلَلْ
(Like a sand dune packed down by the coolness of the shade.)
and his saying:
2524 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
عَرِدا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . بَرِدا
(…firm… cold.)
he means «الظلال» (shades), and «عارِداً» and «بارداً».

semin-durr:84-84.t: His saying, the Exalted: {مِّنْهُم}: an adjective of «أحد», and likewise the clause of His saying «مات». «منهم» may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مات», that is: "he died while being one of them, characterised by the attribute of hypocrisy", like their saying «أنت مني» ("you are from me"), meaning "on my way". And «أبداً» is a ẓarf governed by the prohibition.

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ}: It was said: this is a reinforcement of the preceding verse. al-Fārisī said: "It is not a reinforcement, because that one concerns one group and this one another, and the wording of the two differs. Here it is «ولا» with the wāw, for the fitness of conjoining a prohibition to a prohibition before it in His saying «ولا تُصَلِّ، ولا تَقُمْ، ولا تُعْجبك», so the wāw is fitting; while there it is with the fāʾ, for the fitness of following on from His saying «ولا يُنْفِقون إلا وهم كارهون», that is, 'for spending', so they are impressed by the abundance of wealth and children, and He forbade him to be impressed with the fāʾ of sequence. Here it is «وأولادهم» without «لا», because it is a prohibition of being impressed by the two together, while there it has the addition of «لا», because it is a prohibition regarding each one by one; so the two combined indicate the prohibition regarding them both together and separately. Here it is «أنْ يُعَذِّبهم» and there «ليُعَذِّبهم»; so He brought the lām there to signal predominance, and the object of the intending is omitted, that is: 'Allah only intends to test them with wealth and children'; and He brought «أن» here because the target of the intending is the punishing, that is: 'Allah only intends to punish them'. So the object to which the intending is attached differs in the two verses. This is the apparent sense, though it is possible that the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and that «أَنْ» is on the omission of a causal lām. There it is «في الحياة الدنيا», and here «الحياة» is dropped, to alert to the baseness of this world and that it does not deserve to be called life, especially as it is mentioned after the mention of the death of the hypocrites, so it was fitting that it not be called life."

semin-durr:86-86.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذَآ أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ}: «إذا» by its original placement does not require repetition, even if some people understood that from it here. This has already preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara, and I recited on it:
2525 - إذا وجدْتُ أوارَ الحُبِّ في كَبِدي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When I find the heat of love in my liver… [verse incomplete in the source])
and that this is understood only from contextual indications, not from what «إذا» was placed to convey.
His saying: {أَنْ آمِنُواْ}: there are two possibilities. The first: that it is explicative (tafsīriyya), because what precedes it is in the sense of speech, though not its letters. The second: that it is a maṣdar-forming particle with an omitted preposition, that is: «بأنْ آمنوا». In His saying «اسْتَأْذَنَكَ» there is an iltifāt (shift) from the third person to the second person, because the word «رسوله» preceded; had it followed the basic pattern it would have been said «استأذنه».

semin-durr:87-87.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَعَ الخوالف}: «الخَوَالِفُ» is the plural of «خالفة», from a description of women, and this is a description of censure, as in the saying of Zuhayr:
2526 - وما أَدْري وسوف إخالُ أَدْري ... أقومٌ آلُ حِصْنٍ أم نساءُ
فإنْ تكنِ النساءُ مُخَبَّآتٍ ... فَحُقَّ لكل مُحْصَنَةٍ هِداءُ
(I do not know, and I shall presently think I know: are the family of Ḥiṣn men or women? If women are to be kept hidden away, then every guarded woman deserves to be given a gift of a bride.)
and another said:
2527 - كُتِبَ القَتْلُ والقتالُ علينا ... وعلى الغانيات جَرُّ الذيولِ
(Killing and fighting have been decreed upon us, and upon the beautiful women the trailing of skirts.)
al-Naḥḥās said: "«الخوالِف» may be from a description of men, in the sense that it is the plural of «خالفة». One says «رجل خالِفَة», that is, 'there is no good in him'; so on this it would be a plural for males according to its wording." Some said: it is the plural of «خالف»; one says «رجلٌ خالفٌ», that is, "no good in him". But this is rejected, for «فواعل» is not a plural of «فاعل» as a description of a rational being, except what is irregular such as «فوارس» and «نواكس» and «هوالك».

semin-durr:88-88.t:
And «الخَيْرات» is the plural of «خَيْرة» on the pattern faʿla with a sukūn on the ʿayn; it is the best-liked of everything, and its use came to predominate for women, and from it comes His saying, the Exalted: {خَيْرَاتٌ حِسَانٌ}, and the poet's saying:
2528 - ولقد طَعَنْتُ مَجامِع الرَّبَلاتِ ... رَبَلاتِ هندٍ خَيْرةِ الملَكاتِ
(I have pierced the places where the plump flesh gathers, the plump flesh of Hind, the best of the queens.)

semin-durr:90-90.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {المعذرون}: It has been read in many ways. Among them is the reading of the majority: a fatḥa on the ʿayn and shadda on the dhāl. This reading admits two possibilities: that its pattern is faʿʿala, with doubling, and the meaning of the doubling in it is taking pains (takalluf); the meaning being that he imagined that he has an excuse, while he has no excuse. The second: that its pattern is iftaʿala, the original being «اعتذرَ»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl by converting the tāʾ of iftiʿāl into a dhāl, and its vowel was moved to the silent letter before it, which is the ʿayn. The reading of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr «المعتذرون» on the original form indicates this. To this al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ, Abū ʿUbayda, Abū Ḥātim and al-Zajjāj went.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Aʿraj, Abū Ṣāliḥ and ʿĪsā ibn Hilāl read, and it is also the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Yaʿqūb and al-Kisāʾī, «المُعْذِرون» with a sukūn on the ʿayn and a kasra on the dhāl, light, from «أَعْذَر يُعْذِر» like «أكرم يكرم».
Maslama read «المُعَّذَّرون» with shadda on the ʿayn and the dhāl, from «تعذَّر» in the sense of «اعتذر». Abū Ḥātim said: "He meant «المتعذرون», but the tāʾ is not assimilated into the ʿayn because of the distance of their points of articulation, so it is a mistake by him or against him."
His saying: {لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُمْ}: attached to «جاء»; the agent is omitted and the prepositional phrase is put in its place because it is known, that is: "so that the Messenger may give them leave". The majority read «كَذَبوا» light, that is, "they lied in their faith". al-Ḥasan in the well-known report from him, Ubayy and Ismāʿīl read «كذَّبوا» with shadda, that is, "they did not believe what the Messenger brought from his Lord, nor did they comply with His command".

semin-durr:91-91.t:
Abū Ḥaywa read «نصحوا اللَّهَ» without a lām, and it has already been mentioned that «نَصَح» is made transitive by itself and by the lām.
His saying {مِن سَبِيلٍ}: an agent of the prepositional phrase, because it relies on a negation; it may also be a mubtadaʾ with the preceding prepositional phrase as its khabar. On both views «مِنْ» is redundant in it, that is: «ما على المحسنين سبيل».
Some said: in this verse there is a kind of badīʿ (rhetorical embellishment) called «التمليح» (tamlīḥ), which is: that you allude, in the gist of your speech, to a famous story, a current proverb or a rare verse without mentioning it; and from it is the saying:
2529 - اليومَ خمرٌ ويبدو بعده خَبَرٌ ... والدهرُ مِنْ بين إنعامٍ وإبْآسِ
(Today is wine, and after it news will appear; time moves between bestowing favour and bringing misery.)
He alludes to the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays when the news of the killing of his father reached him: «اليومَ خمرٌ وغداً أمره» ("Today is wine, and tomorrow is its matter"). And the saying of another:
2530 - فواللَّهِ ما أدري أأحلامُ نائمٍ ... أَلَمَّت بنا أم كان في الركب يوشَعُ
(By Allah, I do not know whether it was a sleeper's dreams that visited us, or whether Joshua was in the riding party.)
It alludes to the story of Joshua, peace be upon him, and his making the sun stop. And the saying of another:
2531 - لعَمْروٌ مع الرَّمْضاءِ والنارُ تَلْتَظِي ... أرقُّ وأحفى منكَ في ساعة الكَرْبِ
(ʿAmr, even with the scorching ground and the blazing fire, is gentler and more solicitous than you in the hour of distress.)
It alludes to the famous verse:
2532 - المستجيرُ بعمروٍ عند كُرْبته ... كالمستجير مِنَ الرَّمْضاءِ بالنار
(One who seeks the protection of ʿAmr in his distress is like one who flees the scorching ground into the fire.)
It is as if this saying, «ما على المحسنين من سبيل», had something of its meaning become widespread among the people, so He alluded to it without mentioning its wording. When the Shaykh mentioned tamlīḥ he did not qualify it with "without mentioning it", yet it is indispensable, because if he mentions it by its wording it is iqtibās (quotation) and taḍmīn (incorporation).

semin-durr:92-92.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ عَلَى الذين}: There are several possibilities in it. The first: that it is conjoined to «الضعفاء», that is: "there is no blame on the weak, nor on those who, when they came to you…", so they enter into the khabar of «ليس», the predicate being reported about them, attached to its subject «حَرَج». The second: that it is conjoined to «المحسنين», so they enter into what is predicated of His saying «من سبيل»; for «مِنْ سبيل» may be a mubtadaʾ, and may be the subject of the Hijazi «ما», and «مِنْ» is redundant in both cases. The third: that {وَلاَ عَلَى الذين} is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "nor, on those who, when they came to you, up to the end of the ṣila, is there any blame or way", and it is omitted because the speech indicates it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said it, and there is no need for it, because it is an estimate that can be dispensed with, since he has estimated something that this present expression stands in for, in wording and meaning. This relative noun may be included in His saying {وَلاَ عَلَى الذين لاَ يَجِدُونَ مَا يُنفِقُونَ}, and they were mentioned by way of denying blame from them; and they may not be included, if these were people who found what to spend but did not find a mount.
Maʿqil ibn Hārūn read «لنَحْملهم» with the nūn of majesty. There is a difficulty in it, since what the construction required was: "I said, I do not find that on which Allah may carry you."
His saying «قلت»: there are four possibilities in it. The first: that it is the apodosis of the conditional «إذا», and «إذا» with its apodosis is in the position of a ṣila, the ṣila being a conditional clause. On this, His saying «تَوَلَّوا» is an answer to an implied question, as if someone had said: "What was their state when they were answered with this answer?" and it was answered with His saying «تولَّوا». The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the kāf of «أَتَوْك», that is: "when they came to you while you were saying: I do not find that on which to carry you"; and «قد» is implied according to those who require that in a past verb occurring as ḥāl, like His saying {أَوْ جَآءُوكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 90] in one of its possibilities, as its verification has preceded. To this al-Zamakhsharī inclined. The third: that it is conjoined to the condition, so it is in the position of the genitive through the annexation of the ẓarf to it by way of coordination, with the conjunction omitted, the implied form being «وقلت». You have already had discussion of this question and of what people cited as evidence on it. To this al-Jurjānī went, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya followed him, except that he estimated the conjunction as a fāʾ, that is «فقلت». The fourth: that it is resumptive. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: is it permissible for His saying «قلت لا أجدُ» to be resumptive like it", meaning like {رَضُواْ بِأَن يَكُونُواْ مَعَ الخوالف}, as if it were said: 'When they came to you for you to carry them, they turned away', and then it was said: 'What is the matter with them, that they turned away weeping?' [and it was said], 'You said: I do not find that on which to carry you', except that it is placed between the condition and the result like a parenthesis. I say: yes, and it is good." End of quotation.
The Shaykh said: "It is neither permissible nor good in the speech of the Arabs, so how in the speech of Allah? It is an understanding of a non-Arab." I say: I do not know the reason for his prohibiting it and not finding it good, given its clarity and obviousness in wording and meaning. That is because their turning away stands as it is, so the tears are not consequent merely on their coming to him, peace be upon him, for him to carry them, but on his saying to them {لاَ أَجِدُ مَآ أَحْمِلُكُمْ}; and if that is so, his saying that to them is a cause of their weeping, so it is good to make His saying {قُلْتَ: لاَ أَجِدُ مَآ أَحْمِلُكُمْ} an answer to whoever asks about the reason for their turning away while their eyes overflow with tears, which is the meaning Abū l-Qāsim intended. On these three possibilities which I put forward for «قلت», its apodosis is His saying «تولَّوا», and His saying «لتحملَهم» is the reason for «أَتَوْك». And His saying «لا أجد» is the one that takes one object, because it is from «الوُجْد». And «ما» may be a relative or a described (indefinite) noun.
His saying: {وَّأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «تَوَلَّوا». al-Zamakhsharī said: «تفيضُ من الدمع» is like your saying «تفيض دمعاً» ("overflowing tears"). This has been treated fully in al-Māʾida at His saying {ترى أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدمع} [al-Tawba: 83] [Translator's note: the source says al-Māʾida but cites al-Tawba 9:83; kept as written], where he made «من الدمع» a tamyīz (specification) and «مِنْ» redundant, and the refutation of him in that was given there, so turn to it.
His saying: {حَزَناً}: there are three possibilities for its accusative. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and its governor is «تفيض», as the Shaykh said. It cannot be said that the agent here differs, since the overflowing is attributed to the eyes and the grief proceeds from the owners of the eyes, and when the agent differs the noun must be governed by a preposition; for we say: grief is attributed to the eyes too, figuratively. One says: عين حزينةٌ وسخينة ("a sad eye", "a hot eye"), and عين مسرورةٌ وقريرة ("a delighted eye", "a cool eye") for the opposite. It may also be that its governor is «تَوَلَّوا», and then the agents of the reason and the effect are really the same. The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is: "they turned away sad", or "their eyes overflow sad", on the figurative sense mentioned. The third: that it is a maṣdar with an implied governor of its own wording, that is: "they grieve a grief", as Abū l-Baqāʾ said. And this clause he estimated as governing this maṣdar is itself in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl: either from the agent of «تَوَلَّوا» or from the agent of «تفيض».
His saying: {أَلاَّ يَجِدُواْ}: there are two possibilities in it. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and its governor is «حَزَناً» if we parse it as an object of purpose or a ḥāl; but if we parse it as a maṣdar, then no, because a maṣdar does not govern when it is a reinforcement of its governor. On the view that «حَزَناً» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, «أن لا يَجِدوا» is the reason of the reason, meaning that he gave the overflow of tears the reason of grief, and gave the grief the reason of not finding anything to spend. This is clear, and you have already had its counterpart in His saying {جَزَآءً بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَالاً مِّنَ الله} [al-Māʾida: 38]. The second: that it is attached to «تفيض». The Shaykh said: "Abū l-Baqāʾ said: 'It may be attached to «تفيض»'." Then the Shaykh said: "That is not permissible on his parsing of «حزناً» as an object of purpose governed by «تفيض», since a governor does not call for two objects of purpose except by conjunction or substitution."

semin-durr:93-93.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {رَضُواْ}: there are two possibilities in it. The first: that it is resumptive, as if someone had said: "What is the matter with them, that they asked leave to sit when they are able to fight?" and it was answered with His saying «رَضُوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالِفِ». To this al-Zamakhsharī inclined. The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with «قد» implied in His saying [«رَضُوا»].
His saying: {وَطُبَعَ}: conjoined to «رضُوا», to alert that the cause of their staying behind is their contentment with their sitting and Allah's sealing of their hearts.
His saying {إِنَّمَا السبيل على}: He brought «على» although it can be connected with «إلى», for a difference they mentioned: «على» indicates superiority and the weakness of the defence of the one it is applied to, as in «لي سبيل عليك» and «لا سبيلَ لي عليك», unlike «إلى». So when you say «لا سبيل عليك», it is different from your saying «لا سبيلَ إليك». And among the cases where «إلى» comes with it is his saying:
2533 - ألا ليت شِعْري هل إلى أمِّ سالمٍ ... سبيلٌ فأمَّا الصبرُ عنها فلا صبرا
(Would that I knew whether there is a way to Umm Sālim; as for patience away from her, there is none.)
and his saying:
2534 - هل من سبيلٍ إلى خَمْرٍ فأشربَها ... أم من سبيل إلى نَصْرِ بن حَجَّاجِ
(Is there a way to wine, that I may drink it, or a way to Naṣr ibn Ḥajjāj?)

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قَدْ نَبَّأَنَا الله مِنْ أَخْبَارِكُمْ}: there are two possibilities in it. The first: that «نبَّأ» is the one governing two objects, the first being the «نا» and the second His saying «مِنْ أخباركم». On this «مِنْ» has two possibilities. One: that it is not redundant, and the estimate is: "Allah has informed us of some reports of your reports", or "a portion of your reports", so it is in reality an adjective of the omitted object. The other: that «مِنْ» is redundant according to al-Akhfash, because he sets no condition for it; the estimate being: "Allah has informed us of your reports".
The second of the two possibilities from the first pair: that it governs three objects, like «أعلم»; so the first and second are as stated, and the third is omitted for brevity because it is known, the estimate being: "Allah has informed us, of your reports, that it is a lie", or the like. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It may govern three, and the other two are omitted, the estimate being 'reports of your reports, established'; «من أخباركم» alerts to the omitted element, and «مِنْ» is not redundant, since if it were redundant it would be the second object and the third object omitted, which is an error because whenever the second object is mentioned in this chapter, mentioning the third is required. It was also said: «مِنْ» is in the sense of «عن»." I say: his statement that omitting the third is an error — if he means omission by suppression (ḥadhf iqtiṣār), it is conceded; if he means omission for brevity (ḥadhf ikhtiṣār), it is denied. The positions of the scholars on this question have already come to you.

semin-durr:95-95.t: His saying, the Exalted: {جَزَاءً}: it may be accusative as a maṣdar with an implied verb of its own wording, that is: «يُجْزَوْنَ جزاء»; and it may be accusative by the content of the preceding clause, because their taking refuge in Hell is in the sense of requital. It may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi.

semin-durr:97-97.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الأعراب}: a plural form, and it is not the plural of «عرب», as Sībawayh said; this is so as not to make the plural more specific than the singular, since «العرب» is this particular people whether they dwell in the desert or in the towns, whereas «الأعراب» is applied only to those who dwell in the desert. You have had this at the beginning of this work at His saying, the Exalted, {رَبِّ العالمين} [al-Fātiḥa: 1]. For this difference, the relative adjective is formed from «الأعراب» on its wording, so one says «أعرابيّ», and it is pluralised as «أعاريب».
His saying: {وَأَجْدَرُ}, that is, more fitting and more apt. One says: هو جديرٌ وأجدر وحقيق وأحقّ وقمين وأَوْلى وخليق بكذا, all in one meaning. al-Layth said: "جَدَر يَجْدُر جَدارةً, so he is جديرٌ", and it is feminised, dualised and pluralised. The poet said:
2535 - بِخَيْلٍ عليها جِنَّةٌ عَبْقَرِيَّةٌ ... جديرون يوماً أن يَنَالوا وَيَسْتَعْلوا
(With horsemen upon whom is a ʿabqarī jinn-like spirit, worthy one day of attaining and rising high.)
al-Rāghib drew attention to the origin of the derivation of this root, that it is from «الجِدار» (the wall), saying: "«الجديرُ» is the limit, because the matter ends at it as a thing ends at the wall." What appears is that its derivation is from «الجَدْر», which is the root of the tree, so it is as if it were firm, like the firmness of the root, in your saying «جدير بكذا».
His saying: {أَلاَّ يَعْلَمُواْ}, that is, «بأن لا يعلموا»; the preposition was omitted, so the well-known disagreement arose between al-Khalīl and al-Kisāʾī on the one side, and Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ on the other.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن يَتَّخِذُ مَا يُنفِقُ مَغْرَماً}: «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ, and it is either a relative noun or a described (indefinite) noun. «مَغْرَماً» is a second object, because «اتخذ» here is in the sense of «صَيَّر» ("made"). «المَغْرَمُ» is loss, derived from «الغَرام», which is destruction, because it is an evil; and from it {إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً} [al-Furqān: 65]. It was also said: its origin is clinging, and from it comes «الغَريمُ» (the creditor), for his clinging to the one from whom he demands.
His saying: {وَيَتَرَبَّصُ}: conjoined to «يَتَّخِذ», so it is either part of the ṣila or an adjective. «التربُّصُ» is waiting. «الدوائر» is the plural of «دائرة», which is what surrounds a person of calamity and misfortune, conceived from the circle which surrounds a thing without escape from it. Its original is «داوِرَة» because it is from «دار يدور», that is, "surrounded". The meaning of «تربُّص الدوائر» is waiting for calamities. He said:
2536 - تَرَبَّصْ بها رَيْبَ المَنون لعلها ... تُطَلَّقُ يوماً أو يموتُ حليلُها
(Wait out with her the vicissitudes of fate; perhaps she will be divorced one day, or her husband will die.)
His saying: {عَلَيْهِمْ دَآئِرَةُ السوء}: this clause is parenthetical between the clauses of this account, and is a supplication against the Bedouins mentioned earlier. Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read here «السُّوء», and likewise the second in al-Fatḥ, with a ḍamma; the rest read with a fatḥa. As for the first in al-Fatḥ, which is «ظنَّ السَّوْء», the seven agreed on its fatḥa. As for the fatḥa form, it was said that it is a maṣdar. al-Farrāʾ said: "One says سُؤْتُه سُوْءاً ومَساءةً وسَوائِية ومَسَائِية, and with the ḍamma it is the noun." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is harm, and it is a maṣdar in reality." I say: he means that in origin it is like the fatḥa form in being a maṣdar, and then it was applied to every harm and evil. Makkī said: "Whoever puts a fatḥa on the sīn, its meaning is corruption and badness, and whoever puts a ḍamma, its meaning is defeat, affliction and harm." The apparent sense is that the two are nouns for what was mentioned, and it is possible that they are in origin a maṣdar and then applied to what was mentioned. Others said: the ḍamma form is punishment and harm, and the fatḥa form is censure; do you not see that they agreed on the fatḥa in {ظَنَّ السوء} [al-Fatḥ: 6] and in His saying {مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ امرأ سَوْءٍ} [Maryam: 28], and mention of punishment is not fitting in these two places.
al-Zamakhsharī said, and did well: "The ḍamma form is punishment, and the fatḥa form is censure of the 'circle', as in your saying «رجلُ سَوْء» as the opposite of «رجل عدل», because whoever the circle turns upon censures it." He means that it is of the type of annexing a described noun to its adjective, so it was in origin described by the maṣdar for emphasis and then annexed to its description, as in His saying, the Exalted, {مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ امرأ سَوْءٍ} [Maryam: 28]. The Shaykh said: "It has been reported with the ḍamma", and recited:
2537 - وكنت كذئبِ السُّوء لمَّا رأى دماً ... بصاحبه يوماً أحال على الدَّم
(You were like the evil wolf which, seeing blood on its companion one day, turned upon the blood.)
Concerning «الدائرة» there are two views, the clearer of which is that it is an adjective on the pattern fāʿila like «قائمة». al-Fārisī said: "It may be a maṣdar like «العافية»."
His saying: {بِكُمُ الدوائر}: there are two possibilities in it. The clearer is that the bāʾ is attached to the verb before it. The second: that it is a ḥāl from «الدوائر», as Abū l-Baqāʾ said, which is not clear; and on this it is attached to an omitted element, as has been established several times.

semin-durr:99-99.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قُرُبَاتٍ}: a second object of «يتخذ», as stated for «مَغْرَما». The seven readers did not differ over the ḍamma on the rāʾ of «قُرُبات», although they differ over the rāʾ of «قربة», as will come. It may be a plural of «قُرُبة» with a ḍamma, as in the reading of Warsh from Nāfiʿ, and it may be a plural of the form with a sukūn, the ḍamma being given only as assimilation to «غرفات»; and notice of this rule and its conditions has preceded at His saying, the Exalted, {فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ} [verse 17] at the beginning of al-Baqara.
His saying: {عِندَ الله}: there are three possibilities for this ẓarf. The clearest: that it is attached to «يَتَّخذ». The second: that it is a ẓarf of «قربات», as Abū l-Baqāʾ said, which is not so. The third: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of «قربات».
His saying: {وَصَلَوَاتِ الرسول}: two possibilities. The clearer: that it is conjoined to «قربات», which is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words, for he said: "The meaning is that what he spends is a cause of obtaining nearness with Allah «وصلوات الرسول», because he used to pray for those who give charity with good, as in his saying, 'O Allah, bless the family of Abū Awfā.'" The second, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed and Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned no other: that it is conjoined to «ما ينفق», that is: "and he takes, through righteous deeds and the blessings of the Messenger, a means of nearness."
His saying: {ألا إِنَّهَا قُرْبَةٌ}: the pronoun in «إنها» was said to refer to «صلوات», and it was also said to refer to the expenditures understood from «يُنفقون».
Warsh read «قُرُبَة» with a ḍamma on the rāʾ, and the rest with a sukūn; it was said they are two dialect forms. It was also said: the original is the sukūn and the ḍamma is assimilation, and there has already been a disagreement among the morphologists on this: is it permissible to make fuʿl heavy to fuʿul? Some made «عُسُراً» and «يُسُراً» with a ḍamma on the sīn branches of the sukūn forms. It was also said: the original is «قُرُبة» with a ḍamma, and the sukūn is for lightness, which accords more with the usage of the Arabs, since their basis is fleeing from heaviness to lightness.
In the resumption of this clause and its being headed by the two particles of alerting and verification, which signal the firmness and establishment of the matter, there is a testimony from Allah to the soundness of what he believed about his spending. al-Zamakhsharī said the sense of this, and said: "And likewise «سيُدْخلهم», and what is in the sīn of the verification of the promise."

semin-durr:100-100.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والسابقون}: two possibilities. The clearer: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and for its khabar there are three possibilities. One, which is the apparent one: that it is the supplicatory clause of His saying «رضي الله عنهم». The second: that the khabar is His saying «الأوَّلون», the meaning being: "the foremost, that is in emigration, [they] are the first of the people of this religion", or "the foremost to Paradise are the first of the people of emigration". The third: that the khabar is His saying {مِنَ المهاجرين والأنصار}, the meaning in it being the notification that the foremost of this community are from the Emigrants and the Helpers; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned that, and in the last two possibilities there is affectation.
The second of the two possibilities for «السابقين»: that it is conjoined to {مَن يُؤْمِنُ بالله}, that is: "and among them are the foremost". In it there is remoteness.
The majority have genitive «الأنصار», conjoined to the Emigrants, meaning that the foremost are from these two classes. A large group of distinguished figures read — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Qatāda, al-Ḥasan, Sallām, Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd, ʿĪsā al-Kūfī, Ṭalḥa and Yaʿqūb — «والأنصارُ» in the nominative. There are two possibilities in it. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «رضيَ الله عنهم». The other: conjoined to «السابقون». What there is in it has preceded, so it takes its ruling.
His saying: {بِإِحْسَانٍ}: attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl from the agent of «اتَّبعوهم». ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, held that the wāw is omitted from «والذين اتبعوهم», and said that the relative noun is an adjective of what precedes it, until Zayd ibn Thābit told him that it is with the wāw. He said: "Bring me Ubayy." They brought him, and he said to him: "The confirmation of that is in the Book of Allah, at the beginning of al-Jumuʿa: {وَآخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ لَمَّا يَلْحَقُواْ بِهِمْ} [verse 3], in the middle of al-Ḥashr: {والذين جَآءُوا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ} [verse 10], and at the end of al-Anfāl: {والذين آمَنُواْ مِن بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُواْ} [verse 75]." It is reported that he heard a man reading it with the wāw and said: "Who taught you to read?" He said: "Ubayy." He summoned him, and he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught it to me, while you were selling mimosa pods at al-Baqīʿ."
