He said: "You have spoken truly; and if you wish, say: we were present while you were absent, we gave support while you gave none, we sheltered while you drove away." From there ʿUmar said: "I used to think that we had been raised to a height that no one after us would reach."
Ibn Kathīr read {تجري من تحتها} with the preposition «مِنْ», and it is written so in the Meccan codices. The rest read «تحتها» without it, and it is not written in their codices. Most of what the Qur'an has agrees with the reading of Ibn Kathīr here: {تجري مِنْ تحتها} in more than one place.

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكُمْ}: a fronted khabar. «منافقون» is the mubtadaʾ, and «مَنْ» may be a relative or a described (indefinite) noun, the ẓarf being a ṣila or an adjective.
His saying: {مِّنَ الأعراب} is to clarify the kind. His saying: {وَمِنْ أَهْلِ المدينة} may be conjoined to «مَنْ» governed by «مِنْ», so the two genitives share in predicating of the mubtadaʾ «منافقون», as if it were said: "the hypocrites are from a people around you and from the people of Medina"; on this it is a conjunction of single terms, since it conjoins a khabar to a khabar, and on this His saying «مَرَدُوا» is resumptive and has no position. It may also be that the speech is complete at His saying «منافقون», and His saying {وَمِنْ أَهْلِ المدينة} is a fronted khabar, the mubtadaʾ after it being omitted with its adjective standing in its place. Omitting the described noun and putting its adjective in its place, when it is a clause, is regular with the partitive «مِنْ», as has been verified, as in «منا ظَعَن ومنا أقام» ("among us is one who departed and among us is one who stayed"); and the estimate is: "and among the people of Medina are a people or folk who persisted"; on this it is a conjunction of clauses. On the first possibility, «مَرَدُوا» may be an adjective of «منافقون», separated from its adjective by His saying {وَمِنْ أَهْلِ المدينة}. The estimate is: "among those around you and among the people of Medina are hypocrites who have persisted." al-Zajjāj said that, and al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ followed him. The Shaykh considered it remote because of the separation by the conjoined element between the adjective and what it describes, saying: "So it becomes like «في الدار زيدٌ وفي القصرِ العاقلُ»", meaning you separate Zayd and «العاقل» with your saying «وفي القصر». al-Zamakhsharī likened the omission of the described mubtadaʾ in the second possibility, with its adjective standing in for it, to the saying:
2538 - أنا ابنُ جلا. . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I am the son of Jalā…)
The Shaykh said: "If he means in the general omission of the described noun, it is fine; but if he likened it to it in its particularity, it is not fine, because omitting the described noun with «مِنْ» is regular, while «أنا ابن جلا» is a poetic licence like the saying:
2539 - يَرْمِي بكفَّيْ كان مِنْ أَرْمَى البشَرْ ..."
(He throws with the two hands of one who was among the best archers of mankind…)
I say: the verse referred to is his saying:
2540 - أنا ابن جَلا وطَلاَّعُ الثَّنايا ... متى أَضَعِ العِمامةَ تعرفونِي
(I am the son of the one who unveils and who climbs the mountain passes; when I take off my turban you will know me.)
The grammarians have several interpretations of this verse. One is what preceded. Another: that this clause is quoted, because the man was named by it, for «جلا» contains an agent pronoun, and then he was named by it and it was quoted, as they said «شاب قَرْناها» and «ذرى حَبَّا», and his saying:
2541 - نُبِّئْتُ أخوالي بني يزيدُ ... ظُلْماً علينا لهمُ فَدِيدُ
(I was told my maternal uncles, the Banū Yazīd, [wrongfully against us they have a clamour].)
The third, which is the school of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar: that it is a verb empty of a pronoun, and it is not given tanwīn because according to him it is a diptote, being barred by the pattern of the verb in common; so if one were named with «ضرب» or «قتل» they would be barred. As for the mere pattern without transfer from a verb, it is not barred at all, like «جَمَل» and «جَبَل». [Translator's note: the source text of this paragraph seems slightly corrupt; translated as written.]
«مَرَدوا» means "they became expert and practised". The discussion of this root has preceded in al-Nisāʾ at His saying {شَيْطَاناً مَّرِيداً} [verse 117].
His saying: {لاَ تَعْلَمُهُمْ}: this clause is also in the position of the nominative, an adjective of «منافقون»; it may also be resumptive. «العلم» here may be in its basic sense and so governs two objects, that is: "you do not know them to be hypocrites", the second being omitted because the earlier mention of the hypocrites indicates it, and because hypocrisy is among the attributes of the heart which cannot be observed. Or it may be the sense of recognition (ʿirfāniyya) and so governs one object, as Abū l-Baqāʾ said. As for «نحن نعلمهم», it cannot be except in its basic sense, for a discussion I mentioned to you in al-Anfāl, even though al-Fārisī in his «Īḍāḥ» explicitly ascribed recognition to Him, the Exalted, which is objectionable for what you have learned.
His saying: {مَّرَّتَيْنِ}: the discussion of the accusative of «مرة» has preceded, that it is in two ways: either as a maṣdar or as a ẓarf, and so likewise this. This dual may mean doubling of the one (that is, two times), which is what most say, and they differ in explaining the two; or it may be that the true dual is not meant but rather multiplication, as in His saying, the Exalted, {فارجِعِ البَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ} [al-Mulk: 4], that is, many times, by the proof of His saying «ينقلبْ إليك البصرْ خاسئاً وهو حسير», that is, repelled and weary, and that does not befall it except after many repetitions; and like it «لَبَّيْك وسَعْدَيْك وحنانَيْكَ».
ʿAbbās reported from Abū ʿAmr: «سنعذِّبْهم» with a sukūn on the bāʾ, which is his habit of lightening successive vowels, as in «ينصركم» and its like, though the case of «ينصركم» is better for the sukūn, as the rāʾ is a letter of repetition, so it is as if two ḍammas succeed each other, unlike other cases. The verification of this has preceded. The Shaykh said: "In the codex of Anas: «سيعذبهم» with the yāʾ." It has already been mentioned that the codices were devoid of dots and vocalisation marks, so how could this be said?

semin-durr:102-102.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَآخَرُونَ}: conjoined to «منافقون», that is: "and among those around you are others", or "and among the people of Medina are others". It may be a mubtadaʾ with «اعترفوا» as its adjective and its khabar His saying «خلطوا».
His saying: {وَآخَرَ}: conjoined to «عملاً». al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: each of the two has been made 'mixed', so what is it mixed with? I say: each is mixed and mixed-with, because the meaning is that each of the two was mixed with the other, as in your saying «خَلَطْتُ الماء واللبن» ('I mixed the water and the milk'), meaning: I mixed each of the two with its companion. In it is something that is not in your saying «خَلَطْتُ الماءَ باللبن» ('I mixed the water with the milk'), because there you made the water the mixed and the milk the mixed-with. When you say it with the wāw, you make water and milk both mixed and mixed-with, as if you had said: I mixed the water with the milk and the milk with the water." Then he said: "It may be from their saying «بِعْتُ الشاء: شاةً ودرهماً» ('I sold the sheep: a sheep and a dirham'), in the sense of 'a sheep for a dirham'." I say: he does not mean that the wāw is in the sense of the bāʾ; this is only an explanation of meaning. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If it were with the bāʾ, it would be permissible to say: «خلطْتُ الحِنْطة والشعير» and «خلطت الحنطةَ بالشعير»."
His saying: {عسى الله}: this clause may be resumptive, and it may be in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «آخرون», in which case His saying «خلطوا» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with «قد» implied with it, that is: «قد خلطوا». So it is summarised for «آخرون» that it is conjoined to «منافقون», or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «خلطوا», or the clause of hope.

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ}: two possibilities. One: that it is attached to «خُذْ», and «مِنْ» is partitive. The other: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl from «صدقة», since in origin it is an adjective of it, and when it was fronted it became accusative as a ḥāl.
His saying: {تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ}: the tāʾ in «تُطَهِّرهم» may be the address to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and may be third person, the agent being the pronoun for the charity. On the first, the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «خذ». It may also be an adjective of «صدقةً», in which case an ʿāʾid must be omitted, its implied form being «تطهِّرهم بها»; and «بها» is omitted because what follows indicates it. On the second, the clause is an adjective of «صدقة» only. As for «وتُزَكّيهم», the tāʾ in it is for the address only, because of «بها», since the pronoun refers to the charity, so it is impossible for the pronoun of «تزكِّيهم» to refer to the charity; on this the clause is a ḥāl from the agent of «خُذْ», on our saying that «تُطَهِّرهم» is a ḥāl from it and that the tāʾ in it is the address. It may also be an adjective if we say that «تطهِّرهم» is an adjective and its ʿāʾid is omitted.
Makkī allowed «تُطَهِّرهم» to be an adjective of «صدقة» with the tāʾ as third person, and «تُزَكِّيهم» a ḥāl from the agent of «خُذْ» with the tāʾ as address. They rejected it against him, because the wāw is a conjunction, that is: "a purifying charity and one that purifies by it"; whereas had it been without the wāw it would be permissible. I say: the reason for its invalidity is clear, for the wāw makes the two partners in wording and meaning, so if «وتزكيهم» were conjoined to «تُطَهِّرهم» it would necessarily be an adjective like the one it is conjoined to, since the two cannot differ; but that is permissible if «تزكِّيهم» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ and the wāw is of ḥāl, the implied form being «وأنت تزكِّيهم». In it there is weakness because of the rarity of its counterpart in their speech.
It is summarised from that that the two clauses may be two ḥāls from the agent of «خُذْ» with the tāʾ as address; or two adjectives of «صدقة» with the tāʾ as third person, with the ʿāʾid omitted from the first; or «تطهِّرهم» a ḥāl or adjective and «تزكِّيهم» a ḥāl as Makkī allowed; or «تزكِّيهم» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ with the wāw of ḥāl.
al-Ḥasan read «تُطْهِرهم» light, from «أطهر», making it transitive by the hamza.
His saying: {إِنَّ صلاوتك}: the two Brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ read «إنَّ صلاتَكَ», and in Hūd «أصلاتك تأمُرك», in the singular; the rest read «إنَّ صلواتك» and «أصلواتُك» in the plural in both; both are clear, except that «الصلاة» here is supplication, and there it is worship.
«السَّكَنُ» is tranquillity. He said:
2542 - يا جارةَ الحيِّ ألاَّ كنتِ لي سَكَناً ... إذ ليس بعضٌ من الجيران أَسْكَنني
(O neighbour of the tribe, would that you were a source of tranquillity for me, since some of the neighbours do not give me tranquillity.)
So faʿal is in the sense of mafʿūl, like «القَبْض» in the sense of «المقبوض», and the meaning is: "they find tranquillity in it". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Therefore he did not feminise it." But the apparent sense is that here it is in the sense of fāʿil, because of His saying «لهم»; and if it were as he said, the construction would be «سكنٌ إليها», that is, "something rested in"; so it is clear that the meaning is "a source of tranquillity for them".

semin-durr:104-104.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {هُوَ يَقْبَلُ}: «هو» is a mubtadaʾ, «يَقْبَلُ» is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «أنَّ», and «أنَّ» with what is in its scope stands in the place of the two objects, or in the place of the first. It is not permissible for «هو» to be a separating pronoun (faṣl), because what follows it does not create any suspicion of being an adjective; and this has been verified earlier.
al-Ḥasan read, and the Shaykh said: in the codex of Ubayy: «ألم تعلموا» with the address (second person plural). There are several possibilities in it: one: that it is an address to those who stayed behind, who said: "What is this distinction which these were given?" The [second]: that it is an iltifāt without an implied saying, and the ones meant are the repentant. The [third]: that it is on an implied saying, that is: "Say to them, Muḥammad: Do you not know?"
His saying: {عَنْ عِبَادِهِ}: attached to «يَقْبَل». It was made transitive with «عن»; it was said: because the meaning of «مِنْ» and the meaning of «عن» are close. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Often this one and that one are used interchangeably in one place, as in «لا صدقةَ إلا عن غني ومِنْ غني» ('there is no charity except from a wealthy person') and «فعل ذلك فلانٌ مِنْ أَشَره وبَطَره، وعن أَشَره وبَطَره» ('so-and-so did that out of his arrogance and insolence')." It was also said: the word «عن» signals some distance; you say «جلس عن يمين الأمير» ('he sat to the right of the emir'), that is, with a kind of distance. The apparent sense is that «عن» here is for passing beyond (mujāwaza) in its basic sense, and the meaning is: "He passes over His servants by accepting their repentance"; so when you say «أخذت العلم عن زيد» its meaning is passing, and when you say «منه» its meaning is the beginning of the limit.
His saying: {هُوَ التواب}: it may be a faṣl and it may be a mubtadaʾ, unlike what precedes it.

semin-durr:106-106.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مُرْجَوْنَ}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «مُرْجَؤُون» with a hamza with a ḍamma followed by a silent wāw. The rest read «مُرْجَوْن» without that hamza, which is like their reading in al-Aḥzāb «تُرْجِىء» with the hamza, the rest without it. They are two dialect forms: one says أَرْجَأْتُه and أَرْجَيْتُه like أَعْطيته. It is possible that they are two original forms in themselves, and that the yāʾ is a substitute for the hamza, since the realisation of the hamza is well-known to be frequent, as in قَرَأْت and قَرَيْتُ, توضَّأْت and توضَّيْت.
His saying: {إِمَّا يُعَذِّبُهُمْ}: this clause may be in the position of the nominative as a khabar, and «مُرْجَوْن» on this would be an adjective of the mubtadaʾ; or it may be a khabar after a khabar, or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is: "they are postponed: either punished or pardoned." «إمَّا» here is for doubt with respect to the addressee, or for vagueness with respect to the fact that He left it vague to the addressees.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والذين اتخذوا}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «الذين اتخذوا» without a wāw, and the rest with the conjunctive wāw. As for the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, it is for agreement with their codices, for the wāw is omitted in the codices of Medina and Syria, while it is present in the codices of others. «الذين», on the reading of whoever omitted the wāw before it, has several possibilities. One: that it is a badal (substitute) for «آخرون» before it. In it there is some doubt, because these who took a mosque for harm cannot be said to be "deferred to the command of Allah", because it is reported in the exegesis that they were among the chief hypocrites such as Abū ʿĀmir the monk.
The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and about its khabar there are then several views. One: that it is «أفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بنيانَه», with the ʿāʾid omitted, its implied form being «بنيانَه منهم». The second: that it is «لا يزال بنيانُهم», as al-Naḥḥās and al-Ḥawfī said, and in it there is remoteness because of the length of the separation. The third: that it is «لا تقمْ فيه», as al-Kisāʾī said. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is workable with an implied element, either at the beginning of the verse or at its end, with the estimate: 'do not stand in their mosque'." The fourth: that the khabar is omitted, its implied form being «معذَّبون» or the like, as al-Mahdawī said.
The third possibility: that it is accusative by ikhtiṣāṣ (specification). This possibility will also come in the reading with the wāw.
As for the reading with the wāw, it has what has preceded, except that the badal from «آخرون» is barred because of the conjunction. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «والذين اتخذوا», what is its position in iʿrāb? I say: its position is the accusative by ikhtiṣāṣ, as in His saying, the Exalted, {والمقيمين الصلاة} [al-Nisāʾ: 162]. It was also said: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its meaning being 'among those we have described are those who took…', as in His saying {والسارق والسارقة} [al-Māʾida: 38]." I say: he means according to the school of Sībawayh, whose estimate is "in what is recited to you is the thief", omitting the khabar and keeping the mubtadaʾ, like this verse.
His saying: {ضِرَاراً}: there are three possibilities in it. One: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, that is: "to harm their brothers". Second: that it is a second object of «اتَّخذ», as Abū l-Baqāʾ said. Third: that it is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl from the agent of «اتخذوا», that is: "they took it while harming their brothers"; and it may be accusative as a maṣdar, that is: "they harm others by it a harming", and the attachments of these maṣdars are omitted, that is: «ضِراراً لإِخوانهم وكفراً بالله».
His saying: {مِن قَبْلُ}: there are two possibilities in it. One, which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned alone: that it is attached to His saying «اتخذوا», that is: "they took a mosque before these became hypocrites". The second: that it is attached to «حارب», that is: "he fought before the taking of this mosque".
His saying: {وَلَيَحْلِفَنَّ إِنْ أَرَدْنَا}: «لَيَحْلِفُنَّ» is the answer of an implied oath, that is: «والله ليحلِفُنَّ». And His saying «إن أَرَدْنا» is the answer to His saying «ليحلِفُنَّ», so the answer to the implied oath is an oath-verb answered by His saying «إنْ أَرَدْنا». «إنْ» is negative, which is why «إلا» occurs after it. «الحسنى» is an adjective of an omitted described noun, that is: «إلا الخصلة الحسنى» or «إلا الإِرادةَ الحسنى». al-Zamakhsharī said: "We intended by building this mosque nothing but the best aim, or nothing but the desire for the best, which is prayer." The Shaykh said: "It is as if in his saying «إلا الخصلة الحُسْنى» he made it an object, and in his saying «أو لإِرادة الحسنى» he made it a reason, as though he had given «أراد» the sense of «قصد», that is: 'they intended by building it nothing at all except the desire for the best'." He said: "This is an affected possibility."

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَّمَسْجِدٌ}: two possibilities. One: that it is the lām of ibtidāʾ (commencement). The second: that it is the answer to an implied oath. On both estimates «لَمَسْجِدٌ» is a mubtadaʾ, «أُسِّس» is in the position of the nominative as its adjective, and «أحقُّ» is its khabar; and the deputy agent is the pronoun of the mosque with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "its building was founded".
«مِنْ أولِ» is attached to it, and the Kufans used it as evidence that «مِنْ» can be for the beginning of a limit in time; they also used as evidence the saying:
2543 - مِنَ الصبحِ حتى تَطْلُعَ الشمسُ لا ترى ... من القوم إلا خارجيّاً مُسَوَّما
(From dawn until the sun rises you see of the people only a marked rider outstripping.)
and the saying:
2544 - تُخُيِّرْن مِنْ أزمانِ يومِ حَليمةٍ ... إلى اليوم قد جُرِّبْن كلَّ التجاربِ
(They were chosen from the times of the Day of Ḥalīma until today; they have been tried in every trial.)
The Basrans interpreted it with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "from the founding of the first day", "from the rising of dawn", "from the coming of the times of the Day". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "This is weak, because the estimated founding is not a place such that «مِنْ» would be for the beginning of its limit. What shows the permissibility of that is His saying {لِلَّهِ الأمر مِن قَبْلُ وَمِن بَعْدُ} [al-Rūm: 4], and it is frequent in the Qur'an and elsewhere." I say: the Basrans only fled from its being for the beginning of the limit in time, and there is nothing in this expression requiring that it be only for the beginning of the limit in place such that it would be refuted against them by what was mentioned; the disagreement on this question is strong, and Abū ʿAlī has a long discussion on it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "I find it good to dispense with an estimate, and for «مِنْ» to govern the word «أول» as genitive, because it is in the sense of beginning, as if he said: 'from the start of the days'; and this which I have chosen has been related to me from one of the imams of grammar."
His saying: {أَحَقُّ} is not for comparison but in the sense of «حقيق» ("worthy"), since there is no comparison between the two mosques; «أن تقوم» is «بأن تقوم», and the tāʾ is the address to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and «فيه» is attached to it.
His saying: {فِيهِ رِجَالٌ}: «فيه» may be an adjective of «مسجد» with «رجال» as agent, and it may be a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «فيه» with «رجال» as its agent too; these two are better in that describing with a single word is the basic rule, and the prepositional phrase is close to a single word. «فيه» may also be a fronted khabar and «رجال» a postponed mubtadaʾ. In this clause there are also three possibilities: one, adjective; two, ḥāl, as preceded; three, resumptive.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd read «فيهِ» with a kasra on the hāʾ and the second «فيهُ» with a ḍamma, which is the original, combining the two dialects, and also removing the suspicion of emphasis and the suspicion that «رجالاً» is nominative by «تقوم».
His saying: {يُحِبُّونَ}: an adjective of «رجال», and «أن [يتطهروا]» is the direct object. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and al-Aʿmash read «يَطَّهَّرُوا» with assimilation, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib «المتطهِّرين» with the unassimilated form, the opposite of the readings of the majority in the two words.

semin-durr:109-109.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَانَهُ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «أُسِّس» as passive, with «بنيانُه» nominative, as it stands in for the agent. The rest read «أَسَّس» as active, «بنيانه» being the direct object and the agent the pronoun of «مَنْ». ʿUmāra ibn ʿĀʾidh read the first as passive and the second as active, with «بنيانُه» nominative in the first and accusative in the second for the reason stated. Naṣr ibn ʿAlī and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read «أُسُسُ بنيانِه». Abū Ḥaywa and the two Naṣrs also read «أَساسُ بنيانِه», the plural of «أُسّ». It was reported from Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim also «أَسُّ» with a fatḥa on the hamza and a doubled sīn with ḍamma. «إساس» with a kasra was also read; these are plurals annexed to «البنيان». «أساس» with a fatḥa on the hamza and «أُسّ» with a ḍamma on the hamza and doubled sīn were also read, and they are two singulars annexed to «البنيان». The author of the book «al-Lawāmiḥ» transmitted in it «أَسَسُ» light with ḍamma on the sīn, and «بنيانِه» genitive; «أَسَسٌ» is the maṣdar of «أسَّ يؤسُّه أَسَسَاً وأسَّاً». These are ten readings.
«الأُسُّ» and «الأَساس» are the foundation on which a thing is built; one says «كان ذلك على أُسِّ الدهر» like their saying «على وجه الدهر» ("from the earliest time"); and one says «أَسَّ» with doubling, that is, "made a foundation for it", and «آسَسَ» on the pattern fāʿala.
«البُنْيان» has two views. One: that it is a maṣdar like «الغفران» and «الشكران», applied to the object like «الخَلْق» in the sense of «المخلوق». The second: that it is a plural whose singular is «بُنْيانة». The poet said:
2545 - كبُنْيانةِ القاريِّ مَوْضِعُ رَحْلِها ... وآثارُ نَسْعَيْها مِنَ الدَّقِّ أَبْلَقُ
(Like the building of the Qārī, the place of her saddle, and the marks of her girth straps from the pounding are piebald.)
They mean that it is a generic noun like «قمح» and «قمحة».
His saying: {على تقوى}: two possibilities. One: that it is attached to «أَسَّس» itself, so it is its object in meaning. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «أَسَّسَ», that is: "intending piety by his building", as Abū l-Baqāʾ estimated it.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «تقوىً» with tanwīn. Sībawayh reported this reading, and people did not approve it because its alif is for feminine, so there is no reason for tanwīn; people have explained it as the alif being for ilḥāq (the alif of annexation to a pattern). Ibn Jinnī said: "By analogy its alif is for ilḥāq like «أَرْطى»."
His saying: {خَيْرٌ}: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The comparison here is according to their own belief. «أم» is the connected one, the second «من» is conjoined to the first «مِنْ», and «أَسَّس بنيانه» is like the first.
His saying: {على شَفَا جُرُفٍ}: like His saying «على تقوى» in its two possibilities. «الشَّفا» preceded in Āl ʿImrān. Ḥamza, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «جُرْفٍ» with a sukūn on the rāʾ, the rest with a ḍamma; it was said they are two dialect forms. It was also said: the sukūn form is a branch of the ḍamma form, like «عُنْق» for «عُنُق» and «طُنْب» for «طُنُب». It was also said the reverse, like «عُسُر» and «يُسُر». «الجُرُف» is the well that has not been lined.
It was also said: it is the hollow and what the torrent sweeps away of the valleys, as Abū ʿUbayda said. It was also said: it is the place that the water eats away and so sweeps away, that is, carries off. And «رَجُلٌ جِرَاف» means a man of much sexual intercourse, as if he sweeps away in that act, as al-Rāghib said.
His saying: {هَارٍ}: an adjective of «جُرُفٍ». There are three views on it. One, the well-known: that it is metathesised, by moving its lām before its ʿayn; its original being «هاوِرٌ» or «هايِرٌ» with wāw and yāʾ, because both forms were heard in it. They said: هار يَهُور فانْهارَ, and هار يَهير. And تَهَوَّر البناء and تَهَيَّر. The lām, which is the rāʾ, was moved before the ʿayn, which is the wāw or yāʾ, so it became like «غازٍ» and «رامٍ», and was subject to the weak-letter reduction like theirs; so its pattern after metathesis is fāliʿ, and after deletion it is fālin.
The second: that its ʿayn was dropped without cause, that is, with no requirement, and on this it takes the iʿrāb endings on its lām, so one says: هذا هارٌ, ورأيت هاراً, ومررت بهارٍ; its pattern is also fāl.
The third: that there is no metathesis and no deletion, and that its original is «هَوِر» or «هَيِر» on the pattern «كَتِف»; the weak letter was vowelled with a fatḥa before it, so it was changed to alif, becoming like their saying «كبشٌ صافٌ» (that is «صَوِف») or «يومٌ راحٌ» (that is «رَوِح»). On this it is also vowelled with the iʿrāb, like the one before it, as you say هذا باب, ورأيت باباً, ومررت ببابٍ. This is the most balanced of the views, as it is spared the claim of metathesis and deletion, which are contrary to the basic rule, were it not that it is not well-known among the morphologists. The meaning of «هار» is falling, collapsing, crumbling.
His saying: {فانهار}: its agent is either the pronoun of «البنيان», in which case the hāʾ in «به» is the pronoun of the founder-builder, that is: "the building of the builder fell on the edge of a crumbling bank"; or the pronoun of «الجُرُف», that is: "the edge fell" or "the bank fell", with the hāʾ in «به» for the building. It may also be for the builder-founder; and it is better that the agent be the pronoun of the bank, because its collapse necessarily entails the edge and the building together, while their collapse, or the collapse of one of them, does not necessarily entail its collapse. The bāʾ in «به» may be the one that makes transitive, and may be the one of accompaniment. You have already had a disagreement at the beginning of this work: that the transitive bāʾ, according to some, entails accompaniment. When it is said to be of accompaniment here, it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, that is: "it collapsed accompanying him".

semin-durr:110-110.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بُنْيَانُهُمُ}: it may be a maṣdar as it is, that is: "this action issuing from them continues"; and it may be that the thing built is meant, in which case one is forced to omit a muḍāf, that is: "the building of their building", because what is built is not doubt, and the omission is estimated from the second, that is: "what they built continues to be a cause of doubt". His saying «الذي بَنَوا» is an emphasis, to ward off the suspicion of whoever might suspect that they did not really build and only planned matters, from their saying «كم أبني وتهدمُ» ("how much I build and you demolish"), and on this is his saying:
2546 - متى يبلغُ البُنيانُ يوماً تمامَه ... إذا كنت تَبْنِيه وغيرك يَهْدِم
(When will the building ever reach completion, if you build it while another demolishes?)
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن تَقَطَّعَ}: the excepted-from is omitted and the estimate is: "their building will not cease to be a doubt at any time except the time of the cutting up of their hearts", or "in every state except the state of its cutting up". Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read «تَقَطَّع» with a fatḥa on the tāʾ, the original being «تتقطع» with two tāʾs, one of which was dropped. The rest read «تُقَطَّع» with a ḍamma, passive, imperfect of «قَطَّع» with doubling. Ubayy read «تَقْطَع» light, from «قطع». al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Qatāda and Yaʿqūb read «إلى أن» with the preposition «إلى», and Abū Ḥaywa likewise. This is a reading clear in meaning, except that Abū Ḥaywa read «تُقَطِّع» with a ḍamma on the tāʾ, a fatḥa on the qāf and a doubled kasra on the ṭāʾ, the agent being the pronoun of the Messenger; «قلوبَهم» is accusative as the object, and the meaning is that he kills them and gets full hold of them. It was also said: the agent is the pronoun of the doubt, that is: "until the doubt cuts their hearts." In the codex of ʿAbd Allāh it is «ولو قُطِّعَتْ», and his companions read it so, which differs from the script of the people's codices.

semin-durr:111-111.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ}: attached to «اشترى». The bāʾ enters here upon the thing given up, in accordance with its basic usage, and Abū l-Baqāʾ called it the bāʾ of exchange, like their saying bāʾ al-ʿiwaḍ. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb read «بالجنة».
His saying «يُقاتِلُون»: it may be resumptive and may be a ḥāl. al-Zamakhsharī said: «يقاتلون» has the sense of a command, like His saying, the Exalted, {وَتُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ الله بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَأَنفُسِكُمْ} [al-Ṣaff: 11]. I say: on this the resumptive reading is necessary, because a request cannot be a ḥāl. The disagreement over «فيَقتلون ويُقتلون» has preceded in Āl ʿImrān.
His saying: {وَعْداً}: accusative as a reinforcing maṣdar of the content of the clause, because the meaning of «اشترى» is that He promised them that, so it is the counterpart of «هذا ابني حقاً» ("this is my son, truly"). It may also be a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl, and in it is weakness. «حقاً» is its adjective, and «عليه» is a ḥāl from «حقاً», because in origin it is an adjective of it, had it been postponed.
His saying: {فِي التوراة}: two possibilities. One: that it is attached to «اشترى», and on this every community was commanded to fight and promised Paradise for it. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of the promise, that is: "a promise mentioned and found in the Torah", and on this the promise of Paradise for this community is mentioned in the revealed Books of Allah. al-Zamakhsharī said in the course of his words: «لا يجوز عليه قبيحٌ قط» ("nothing ugly is ever permissible for Him"). The Shaykh said: "He used «قط» in other than its placement; because he brought it with His saying «لا يجوز عليه», and «قط» is a ẓarf of past time, so only a past governs it." I say: a specific time is not meant here.
His saying: {فاستبشروا}: there is an iltifāt from the third person to the address, since in addressing them with that there is honour for them. «استفعل» here is not for request but in the sense of «أفعل», like «استوقد» and «أوقد». His saying {الذي بَايَعْتُمْ بِهِ} is an emphasis, like His saying {الذي بَنَوْاْ} [al-Tawba: 110], to specify for them this very transaction.

semin-durr:112-112.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {التائبون}: there are five possibilities in it. One: that they are a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «العابدون», with what follows being adjectives or multiple khabars according to whoever allows that. The second: that the khabar is His saying «الآمرون». The third: that the khabar is omitted, that is: "the repentant who are described with these attributes are among the people of Paradise", and His saying «وبَشِّر المؤمنين» supports it. This is according to whoever holds that this verse is cut off from what precedes and is not a condition in fighting. As for whoever claimed that it is a condition in fighting, like al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others, the iʿrāb of «التائبين» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: «هم التائبون»; this is of the type of qaṭʿ al-nuʿūt (cutting off the adjectives from the noun), because these attributes, according to those who say so, are among the attributes of the believers in His saying, the Exalted, {[اشترى] مِنَ المؤمنين أَنفُسَهُمْ} [al-Tawba: 111]. The reading of Ubayy, Ibn Masʿūd and al-Aʿmash «التائبين» with the yāʾ supports that. This reading may also be on the cutting-off, in which case it is accusative by an implied verb. al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya stated explicitly that «التائبين» in this reading is an adjective. The fifth: that «التائبون» is a badal from the attached pronoun in «يقاتلون». [Translator's note: the source's numbering jumps from the third possibility to the fifth; the fourth is presumably the cutting-off view discussed within the third.]
No attachment is mentioned for these attributes; He did not say "the repentant from such-and-such", nor "the worshippers of Allah", because that is understood, except in the forms of command and prohibition, for emphasis in that. He did not bring a conjunction between these attributes because of their fittingness to each other, except in the forms of command and prohibition because of the difference between them, for command is a demand for an action and prohibition is a demand for abandonment or restraint; and likewise «الحافظون», whose conjunction He included and whose attachment He mentioned. He brought the order of these attributes in mention in the finest arrangement, which is apparent upon reflection, for He put repentance first and then followed it with worship, to the end. It was also said: the wāw was only entered because it is the wāw of eight, as in {وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ} [al-Kahf: 22] and {وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا} [al-Zumar: 71]; when Paradise has eight gates, the wāw was brought with it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The wāw was only entered in the eighth attribute to signal that seven is, in their view, a complete number, which is why they say «سبع في ثمانية», that is, seven cubits in eight spans; and the wāw indicates that because the wāw signals that what follows it differs from what precedes it, which is why it enters in the chapter of coordinating conjunction." I say: this is a very weak statement with no verification.

semin-durr:113-113.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَوْ كانوا أُوْلِي قربى}: like his saying «أَعْطوا السائلَ ولو على فرس» ("Give the beggar, even if he is on a horse"). What is in that has already preceded, and that it is a ḥāl conjoined to an implied ḥāl.

semin-durr:114-114.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ}: there was disagreement over the nominative and the detached accusative pronouns. It was said, and this is the apparent sense: the nominative refers to Ibrāhīm and the accusative to his father, meaning that Ibrāhīm had promised his father that he would seek forgiveness for him. The reading of al-Ḥasan, Ḥammād al-Rāwiya, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ, Abū Nahīk and Muʿādh al-Qāriʾ «وعدها أباه» with the single-dotted bāʾ supports this. It was also said: the nominative is for the father of Ibrāhīm and the accusative for Ibrāhīm; and in the exegesis it is that he had promised Ibrāhīm that he would believe, and thereby he hoped for his faith.
«الأَوَّاه» is the one who often sighs (taʾawwuh), the one who says «أَوَّاه»; it was also said: the one who says «أوَّه», which is more fitting because «أَوَّهَ» is in the sense of "I feel pain", so «الأَوَّاه» is faʿʿāl, a pattern of intensification from that; and by analogy its verb ought to be triliteral, because patterns of intensification are regular only from the triliteral. Quṭrub reported its verb as triliteral, saying: one says آهَ يَؤُوه like قام يقوم, أَوْهاً. The grammarians rejected this statement of Quṭrub, saying that no triliteral verb is said from «أَوَّه» in the sense of pain; one says only أوَّه تأَوْيهاً and تَأَوَّه تَأَوُّهاً. The rajaz poet said:
2547 - فأَوَّه الراعي وضوضى أَكْلبُه
(The shepherd sighed and his dogs howled.)
and al-Muthaqqib al-ʿAbdī said:
2548 - إذا ما قُمْتُ أرْحَلُها بليلٍ ... تأوَّهُ آهَةَ الرجلِ الحزينِ
(Whenever I rise at night to saddle her, she groans the groan of a sorrowful man.)
al-Zamakhsharī said: «أَوَّاه» is faʿʿāl from «أَوَّه», like «لأَّل» from «اللؤلؤ», and it is the one who sighs often. The Shaykh said: "His likening «أوَّاه» from «أوَّه» to «لأَّل» from «اللؤلؤ» is not good, because the root of «أوَّه» is present in the form of «أواه», whereas the root of «لؤلؤ» is missing in «لأل» because of the difference in composition, since «لأل» is triliteral and «لؤلؤ» is quadriliteral, and the condition of derivation is agreement in the radical letters." I say: «لاَّل» and «لؤلؤ» are both from the repeated quadriliteral, that is: the root is lām and hamza, and then we repeated; the utmost in the matter is that two hamzas were joined in «لآَّل» so the first was assimilated into the other, and they were distinguished in «لؤلؤ».

semin-durr:117-117.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {اتبعوه}: two possibilities. One: that it is a real following, he, peace be upon him, having gone out first and his companions following him; and the other that it is figurative, that is: "they followed his command and prohibition". "The hour of hardship" is an expression for the time of going out to the expedition, and the real hour is not meant, but like their sayings "the day of al-Kulāb" and "the evening we fought Judhām"; so «الساعة» was borrowed for that, as «الغداة» and «العشية» were borrowed in his saying:
2549 - غَدَاةَ طَفَتْ عَلْماءِ بكرُ بنُ وائلٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The morning Bakr ibn Wāʾil rose over ʿAlmāʾ…)
[and his saying]:
2550 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... عشية قارَعْنا جُذَام وحميرا
(…the evening we fought Judhām and Ḥimyar.)
[and his saying]:
2551 - إذا جاء يوماً وارثي يبتغي الغنى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If my heir comes one day seeking wealth…)
His saying: {كَادَ يَزِيغُ}: Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read «يزيغ» with the yāʾ (below), and the rest with the tāʾ (above). The first reading admits that the subject of «كاد» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), with «قلوب» nominative by «يزيغ», and the clause in the position of the accusative as its khabar; or that its subject is the pronoun of the people, or the group which the mention of the Emigrants and Helpers indicates, and therefore Abū l-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya estimated: «من بعد كاد القوم». The Shaykh said of this reading: "It is necessary that «كاد» contain the pronoun of the matter and that «قلوب» be nominative by «يزيغ», because it is impossible for «قلوب» to be the subject of «كاد» and «يزيغ» to be in the place of the khabar, since the intention for it is postponement, and it is not permissible: «مِن بعد كاد قلوب يزيغ» with the yāʾ." I say: what he mentioned is not necessary in this reading, for what has preceded: that the subject of «كاد» may be a pronoun referring to the group or the people, with the verbal clause as its khabar, and there is no objection preventing that. His statement "because it is impossible for «قلوب» to be the subject of «كاد»" means that if we made «قلوب» the subject of «كاد», «يزيغ» would necessarily be a fronted khabar and so would necessarily govern a pronoun referring to «قلوب», and were that so the verb would necessarily be feminine, because it would then be predicated of a pronoun of a figurative feminine, as the broken plural is treated as feminine figuratively.
As for the reading with the tāʾ (above), it admits that «كاد» contains the pronoun of the matter, as before, with «قلوب» nominative by «تزيغ», feminine because of the feminine plural; and that «قلوب» is its subject and «تزيغ» a fronted khabar, with no objection in that, since the verb has been made feminine. The Shaykh said: "On each of these three parsings there is a difficulty, according to what is established in the science of grammar, that the khabar of the verbs of approximation can only be an imperfect verb governing a pronoun of its subject; some stated this absolutely, and some restricted it to those other than «عسى» among the verbs of approximation; and it is not to be indirect (sababī), unlike «كان», whose khabar may govern the pronoun and the indirect element of the subject of «كان». So when we estimate the pronoun of the matter in it, the clause is in the position of the accusative as khabar, and the nominative is not a pronoun referring to the subject of «كاد», nor even indirect to it.
"This also applies in the tāʾ reading. As for the medial placement of the khabar, it is built on the permissibility of such a construction as «كان يقوم زيد», and there is disagreement in it, and the sound view is prohibition. As for the last possibility, it is very weak in that a pronoun is implied in «كاد» which has no referent except in imagination, and in that the khabar of «كاد» would govern an indirect element."
I say: how can he say "the sound view is prohibition" when this construction is present in the Qur'an, as in His saying, the Exalted, {مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 137] and {كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنَا} [al-Jinn: 4], and in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
2552 - وإن تَكُ قد ساءَتْكِ مني خَليقةٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If some trait of mine has displeased you…)
This construction undoubtedly occurs; they only differed in its estimate: whether it is of the type of fronting the khabar or not. Whoever prevented it did so because it is like the chapter of mubtadaʾ and khabar, and a plain khabar, whenever it is so, cannot be fronted before the mubtadaʾ lest it be confused with the chapter of the agent, and so likewise after it is abrogated. Whoever allowed it did so for the safety from confusion.
Then the Shaykh said: "What rescues from these difficulties is believing that «كاد» is redundant, its meaning being intended, with no governing then of a subject or khabar, so it is like «كان» when added, its meaning intended and without governing. The reading of Ibn Masʿūd «من بعد ما زاغَتْ», omitting «كاد», supports this interpretation. The Kufans held its redundancy in His saying, the Exalted, {لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا} [al-Nūr: 40], despite its being affected by a governor and governing what follows; so it is more fitting to claim its redundancy when it is neither governing nor governed." I say: the majority rejected its redundancy, and among the Basrans al-Akhfash held it, and made from it {أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا} [Ṭā Hā: 15]. The discussion of that has preceded at the beginning of this book.
al-Aʿmash and al-Jaḥdarī read «تُزيغ» with a ḍamma on the tāʾ, as if he made «أزاغ» and «زاغ» the same in meaning. Ubayy read «كادَتْ» with the feminine tāʾ.

semin-durr:118-118.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَعَلَى الثلاثة}: it may be conjoined to «النبيّ», that is: "He turned in mercy to the Prophet and to the three"; and it may be conjoined to the pronoun in «عليهم», that is: "then He turned to them and to the three", and therefore the preposition is repeated.
The majority of people read «خُلِّفوا», passive, doubled, from «خلَّفه يُخَلِّفه». Abū Mālik read likewise except that he lightened the lām. ʿIkrima, Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd, ʿIkrima ibn Hārūn al-Makhzūmī and Muʿādh al-Qāriʾ read «خَلَفوا», active, light, from «خَلَفَه», the meaning being "those who became corrupt", from «خُلوف فم الصائم». The meaning may be that they stayed behind the fighters in Medina. Abū l-ʿĀliya and Abū l-Jawzāʾ read likewise except that they doubled the lām. Abū Razīn, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and his two sons Zayd and Muḥammad al-Bāqir and his son Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq read «خالفوا», with an alif, that is: they did not go along with the fighters in going out. al-Bāqir said: "Had they been left behind, it would not have been theirs." «الظن» here is in the sense of knowledge, as in the saying:
2553 - فقلتُ لهم ظُنُّوا بأَلْفَي مُدَجَّجٍ ... سَرَاتُهمُ كالفارِسي المُسَرَّدِ
(So I said to them: think of two thousand armoured men, whose leaders are like the Persian mail-coat strung together.)
It was also said: it is in its basic sense.
His saying: {أَن لاَّ مَلْجَأَ}: «أنْ» is the lightened one, standing in place of the two objects, «لا» and what is in its scope is the khabar, and «من الله» is its khabar. It cannot be attached to «مَلْجَأ» with «إلا إليه» as the khabar, because then it would have to be declined (given tanwīn), since it would be an extended noun. Some said it is permissible to liken the extended noun to the muḍāf, so that its tanwīn and nūn are removed, as in the saying:
2554 - أراني ولا كفرانَ لله أيَّةً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I see myself, and there is no ingratitude to Allah, a sign…)
and the saying «لا صَمْتَ يومٌ إلى الليل» with «يوم» nominative; the discussion of that has preceded. His saying «إلا إليه» is an exception from that omitted general term, that is: "there is no refuge to anyone except to Him", like «لا إله إلا الله».

semin-durr:120-120.t:
«الظَّمأُ» is thirst. One says: ظَمِىء يَظْمَأُ ظَمَأً, so he is ظمآنُ and she is ظمأى. It has two forms: the short and the lengthened; ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read with the lengthened form, like سَفِه سَفاهاً. «الظِّمْءُ» is the interval between two drinkings.
«مَوْطِئاً» is mafʿil from «وَطِىءَ». It may be a maṣdar in the sense of «الوَطْء», or a place. The first is clearer, because the agent of «يغيظ» refers to it without interpretation, unlike its being a place, in which case it refers to the maṣdar, which is «الوَطْءُ» indicated by «المَوْطِىءُ».
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُغيظ» with a ḍamma on the yāʾ; they are two forms: غاظَه and أغاظه.
«النَّيْلُ» is a maṣdar; it may be in its basic sense, and may stand in the place of the direct object. Its yāʾ is not a substitute for a wāw as some claimed, but «ناله ينولُه» is another root and another meaning, which is handing over (munāwala); one says نِلْتُه أَنُوْله, that is, "I took it in hand" (تناولته); and نِلْتُه أنيله, that is, "I attained it".

semin-durr:121-121.t:
«الوادي»: al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الوادي» is every opening between mountains and hillocks that serves as a channel for the torrent; in origin it is fāʿil from «ودى» when it flows, and from it «الوَدِيّ»; it became widespread in the usage of the Arabs in the sense of land." It is pluralised as «أودية», which is not by analogy; its analogy would be «الأَوادي», like «أَواصل» as the plural of «واصل», the original being «وَوَاصِل», the first wāw being changed to hamza. al-Naḥḥās said: "I know no fāʿil and afʿila other than it." This was supplemented against him, and they added «نادٍ» and «أندية», reciting:
2555 - وفيهم مقاماتٌ حِسانٌ وجوهُهمْ ... وأنديةٌ ينتابها القولُ والفعلُ
(Among them are assemblies with handsome faces, and gathering-places frequented by word and deed.)
«النادي» is the assembly. al-Farrāʾ said that it is pluralised as «أَوْداء», like «صاحب» and «أصحاب», and recited for Jarīr:
2556 - عَرَفْتُ ببُرْقَةِ الأَوْداءِ رَسْماً ... مُحيلاً طال عهدُكَ مِنْ رسومِ
(At the stony ground of the valleys I recognised a trace, effaced, long since you knew such traces.)
I say: al-Rāghib added to fāʿil and afʿila: «ناجٍ» and «أنْجِيَة», so three words are complete in fāʿil and afʿila. One says «وَدَاه», that is, "he destroyed him", as if they conceived of it as making blood flow; and «الدِّيَة» (blood money) was called diya because it is in return for the flowing of blood; and from it «الوَدْيُ», which is the male's fluid during play and the water that comes out with urine; and «الوَدِيُّ» with a kasra on the dāl and shadda on the yāʾ is the young palm trees.
His saying: {ذلك بِأَنَّهُمْ} [al-Tawba: 120]: mubtadaʾ and khabar; the reference by it is to what is contained in the negation of staying behind, namely the obligation to go out with him.
His saying: {إِلاَّ كُتِبَ}: this clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from «ظَمَأ» and what is conjoined to it, that is: "no thirst befalls them without being written". The pronoun in «به» is singular although things precede it, treating it like a demonstrative, that is: "a righteous deed was written for them thereby". The pronoun may refer back to the preceding righteous deed, and it may refer to one of the two maṣdars understood from «ينفقون» and «يقطعون», that is: "without being written for them through spending or through crossing".
His saying: {لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ}: attached to «كُتِب». In this clause there is eloquence and rhetorical beauty not hidden from whoever reflects on it, especially one trained by what has preceded in this work.

semin-durr:122-122.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَوْلاَ نَفَرَ مِن كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ}: «لولا» is of urging (taḥḍīḍ), and what is meant is the command. «منهم» may be an adjective of «فرقة» and may be a ḥāl from «طائفة», because in origin it is an adjective of it; on both estimates it is attached to an omitted element. What ought to be said is that «من كل فرقة» is a ḥāl from «طائفة», and «منهم» is an adjective of «فرقة»; and «من كل» may be attached to «نَفَرَ».
His saying: {لِّيَتَفَقَّهُواْ}: there are two views regarding this pronoun. One: that it is for the group that goes out, on the basis that what is meant by going out is going out to seek knowledge, which is the apparent sense. It was also said: the pronoun in «ليتفَّقهوا» refers to the group that stays, and that in «رَجَعوا» to the group that goes out, what is meant by going out being going out to jihad; the meaning is that when those who go out to fight depart, their brothers remain learning jurisprudence from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when the fighters return, the teachers warn them, that is, teach them jurisprudence and the law.

semin-durr:123-123.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلِيَجِدُواْ}: it is of the type of «لا أُرَيَنَّك ههنا» ("let me not see you here"), and its explanation has preceded.
His saying: {غِلْظَةً}: the majority read it with a kasra, which is the stronger dialect. al-Aʿmash, Abān ibn Taghlib and al-Mufaḍḍal, both from ʿĀṣim, read «غَلْظة» with a fatḥa, which is the dialect of the Hijaz. Abū Ḥaywa, al-Sulamī, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and al-Mufaḍḍal and Abān in a report from them, read «غُلظة» with a ḍamma, which is the dialect of Tamīm. Abū ʿAmr reported the three dialects. «الغِلظة» in origin applies to bodies, and was borrowed here for severity, endurance and fortitude.

semin-durr:124-124.t: His saying, the Exalted: {زَادَتْهُ}: the majority have «أيُكم» nominative as a mubtadaʾ with what follows as khabar. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read it accusative by ishtighāl, but the verb is estimated postponed after it because it has the heading of the speech; and accusative, according to al-Akhfash, in this type is better than nominative, because he treats the interrogative noun like nouns preceded by an interrogative particle such as «أزيداً ضربته» in preferring the implied verb.

semin-durr:126-126.t: His saying, the Exalted: {أَوَلاَ يَرَوْنَ}: Ḥamza read «ترون» with the tāʾ of address, which is an address to those who believed, and the rest with the yāʾ of the third person, referring back to {الذين فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ}. The seeing here may be of the heart or of the eye.

semin-durr:127-127.t: His saying, the Exalted: {هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ}: in the position of the accusative by an implied saying, that is: «يقولون: هل يراكم». The clause of the saying is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and «مِنْ أحد» is the agent.

semin-durr:128-128.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ}: an adjective of «رسول», that is: from the purest of the Arabs. Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū l-ʿĀliya, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Maḥbūb from Abū ʿAmr, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qusayṭ al-Makkī, and Yaʿqūb in some of his chains read — and it is the reading of the Messenger of Allah, Fāṭima and ʿĀʾisha — with a fatḥa on the fāʾ, that is: "from the most noble of you", from «النَّفاسة» (preciousness).
His saying: {عَزِيزٌ}: there are several possibilities in it. One: that «عزيز» is an adjective of «رسول»; against which it is that something other than a plain adjective is placed before the plain adjective, and it may be answered that «من أنفسكم» is attached to «جاء», and «ما» may be a maṣdar-forming particle or in the sense of «الذي»; on both estimates it is the agent of «عزيز», that is: "your distress is grievous to him" or "that which you suffer is grievous to him", that is, their distress pains him, so the ʿāʾid is omitted by gradation; this is like the saying:
2557 - يَسُرُّ المرءَ ما ذهب الليالي ... وكان ذهابُهنَّ له ذهاباً
(A man is pleased by the passing of the nights, though their passing is a passing for him.)
that is, "the passing of the nights pleases him". «عزيز» may also be a fronted khabar, with «ما عَنِتُّم» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause an adjective of «رسول». al-Ḥawfī allowed that «عزيز» be a mubtadaʾ with «ما عنتُّم» as its khabar, and in it is beginning with an indefinite noun because of its governing the prepositional phrase after it. The meaning of «العنت» has preceded. The more probable is that «عزيز» is an adjective of «رسول»; because of His saying after it «حريصٌ», so it is not made a khabar for anything else, and the claim that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is «هو حريصٌ», has no need.
«بالمؤمنين» is attached to «رؤوف». It is not permissible for the matter to be one of tanāzuʿ (competition of governors), because one of its conditions is that the governed term come after the two governors, even though some have differed and allowed «زيداً ضربتُ وشتمته» on the basis of tanāzuʿ; and if we build on this weaker view, it would be a case of the second governor acting, not the first, as is known: whenever the first acts, a pronoun is implied in the second without omission.

semin-durr:129-129.t: The majority have a kasra on the mīm of «العظيم», as an adjective of «العرش». Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with a ḍamma, making it an adjective of «الرب», and this was also reported as a reading from Ibn Kathīr. Abū Bakr al-Aṣamm said: "This reading is more pleasing to me, because making «العظيم» an attribute of Allah, the Exalted, is better than making it an attribute of the Throne."

semin-durr:1-1.t:
The majority read «براءة» in the nominative, with two views. The first is that it is nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is His saying «إلى الذين». The mubtadaʾ may be an indefinite because it has been specified by the description of the preposition and its genitive noun after it. The second is that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "these verses are a repudiation (barāʾa)." «من الله» may be attached to «براءة» itself, because it is a maṣdar, and this root takes «مِنْ»: you say baritʾtu min fulān abraʾu barāʾatan, that is: the tie between us was cut. On this basis, this may be the justification for the indefinite as mubtadaʾ in the first view. «إلى الذين» is attached to an omitted word on the first view, since it falls as the khabar, and to «براءة» itself on the second. One says baritʾtu and baraʾtu min al-dayn, with kasra and fatḥa. Al-Wāḥidī said: "There is in it only one dialect: kasra on the ʿayn in the past and fatḥa in the future," but it is not so; the lexicographers reported both.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «براءةً» in the accusative by an implied verb, that is: "hear a repudiation." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "That is: hold fast to a repudiation, and it has the sense of incitement (ighrāʾ)."
«مِنِ الله» was also read, with kasra on the nūn of «مِنْ», either on the basis of the original meeting of two sākins, or by following the mīm of «مِنْ»; it is a minor dialect, for the more frequent is fatḥa with the lām of definiteness and kasra with others, as in «مِنِ ابنك», and the matter is sometimes reversed in both. Abū ʿAmr reported from the people of Najrān that they read so, with kasra on the nūn before the lām of definiteness.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَسِيحُواْ}: This is on an implied saying, that is: "it was said: travel freely." It is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to address. One says sāḥa yasīḥu siyāḥatan, suyūḥan and sayaḥānan, that is: it flowed, like the flow of water in level places. Ṭarafa said:
2447 - لو خِفْتُ هذا منك ما نِلْتَني ... حتى ترى خيلاً أمامي تَسِيحْ
(Had I feared this from you, you would not have reached me until you saw horses streaming before me.)
«أربعةَ أشهرٍ» is an adverbial of «سِيْحوا». {غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِي الله} was also read with the divine Name in the accusative, on the basis that the nūn was omitted for lightness. Its treatment has already been given.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَذَانٌ}: nominative as mubtadaʾ; «مِن الله» is either its adjective or attached to it, and «إلى الناس» is the khabar. It may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "and this is an announcement," the two prepositional phrases being attached to it, as given earlier in «براءة». The Shaykh said: "There is no ground for the saying of whoever said that it is conjoined to «براءة», just as one does not say «عمرو» is conjoined to «زيد» in «زيد قائم وعمرو قاعد»." [Translator's note: the source has «وهو [كما قال]، وهذه عبارة [الزمخشري بعينها]» with bracketed words, apparently editorial insertions, meaning "and it is as he said, and this is al-Zamakhsharī's very wording."] Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿIkrima and Abū l-Mutawakkil read «وإذْن» with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the dhāl. The majority read «أنَّ الله» with fatḥa on the hamza, in one of two ways: either it is the khabar of «أذان», that is: "the announcement from Allah is His repudiation of the polytheists" — the Shaykh weakened this view but did not state his weakening — or it is on the omission of the preposition, that is: «بأن الله». This preposition and its genitive noun is attached either to the maṣdar itself or to an omitted word as its adjective. «يومَ» is accusative by what the preposition and its genitive noun in «إلى الناس» are attached to. Some claimed that it is accusative by «أذانٌ», but this is invalid for two reasons: one, describing the maṣdar before it has acted; the other, separating it from what it governs by an outsider, which is the khabar.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj read with kasra on the hamza, which admits the two well-known schools: the school of the Basrans is the implication of a saying, and the school of the Kufans is treating the announcement (adhān) as the equivalent of a saying.
His saying: {مِّنَ المشركين} is attached to «بريء» itself, as one says "I am free of him" (bariʾtu minhu), unlike {بَرَآءَةٌ مِّنَ الله} [al-Tawba: 1], where it admits this and also admits being an adjective of «براءة».
His saying: {وَرَسُولِهِ}: The majority read it in the nominative, with three views. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, that is: "and His Messenger is free of them," omitted because it is indicated. The second: that it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in the khabar, and this is allowed because of the separation that justifies conjunction, so its nominative is as agent on this view. The third: that it is conjoined to the position of the ism of «أنَّ», according to those who allow that with the fatḥa form by analogy with the kasra form. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The school of the Ustadh, meaning Ibn al-Bādhish, in accord with Sībawayh's words, is that what «أنَّ» enters upon has no position, since it is declined and the effect of the governor has appeared in it, and that there is no difference between «أَنَّ» and «ليت», and the consensus is that what these enter upon has no position." The Shaykh said: "There is a rejoinder to it, because the reason for «أنَّ» having no position for what it enters upon is not the appearance of the governor's effect, as shown by «ليس زيد بقائم» and «ما في الدار مِنْ رجل», in which the effect of the governor appears and both have a position; and his saying 'by consensus', meaning that there is no position for what «ليت» enters upon by consensus, is not so, because al-Farrāʾ disagreed and made the ruling for «ليت» and all its sisters the ruling of kasra «إنَّ»."
I say: his statement "as shown by «ليس زيدٌ بقائم»" and so on — the difference between them may be apparent, for this governor, although its effect appears, is in the ruling of the non-existent, since it is redundant; that is why we take the position into account with it, unlike «أنَّ» with fatḥa, which is a non-redundant governor. His statement "there is no difference between «أنَّ» and «ليت»" should have been rebutted, for the difference stands: the ruling of the mubtadaʾ has been abrogated with «ليت», «لعل» and «كأن», in form and meaning, unlike with «إنَّ» and «أنَّ», with which its meaning remains.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «ورسولَه» in the accusative, with two views, the more apparent being that it is conjoined to the divine Name; the second, that it is mafʿūl maʿahu, as al-Zamakhsharī said. Al-Ḥasan read «ورسولِه» in the genitive, with two views: one, that it is an oath-object, that is: "by His Messenger, the matter is so," its answer being omitted for the meaning to be understood; the second, that it is by adjacency (jiwār), as they made adjectives and emphatics follow by adjacency, whose treatment has already been given. This reading is unlikely to be sound from al-Ḥasan, because of the ambiguity, so that it is reported that a Bedouin heard a man read «ورسولِه» in the genitive. The Bedouin said: "If Allah has disowned His Messenger, then I disown him," and the reciter seized him and took him to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him; the Bedouin related the incident, and then ʿUmar ordered that Arabic be taught. This is also reported of the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī and of Abū l-Aswad al-Duʾalī. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It cannot be conjoined to «المشركين», because that would lead to disbelief." This is among the obvious points.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ الذين}: There are three views. The first is that it is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). The implied form is: "but those with whom you made a covenant, fulfil their covenant to them." Al-Zamakhsharī took this course, saying: "If you ask: from what is His saying {إِلاَّ الذين عَاهَدتُّم} excepted? I say: its aspect is that it is excepted from His saying {فَسِيحُواْ فِي الأرض}, since the speech is addressed to the Muslims, and its meaning is: a repudiation from Allah and His Messenger to those polytheists with whom you made a covenant, so say to them: travel freely, except those of them with whom you made a covenant and who then did not diminish you, so fulfil their covenant to them. The exception has the meaning of rectification (istidrāk), as if it were said, after they were commanded about the covenant-breakers: but those who did not break, fulfil their covenant to them and do not treat them as the others."
The second: that it is a continuous exception (muttaṣil), preceded by an omitted sentence whose implied form is: "kill the polytheists who have covenants, except those with whom you made a covenant." There is weakness in it.
The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is His saying «فأتمُّوا إليهم»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. There is something to consider in it, because the fāʾ is added where it does not belong, since the mubtadaʾ does not resemble a condition, for it refers to specific people; it can proceed only on the view of al-Akhfash, who allows its addition without restriction. The preferable view is that it is discontinuous, for if we made it continuous, excepted from the polytheists at the beginning of the sūra, it would lead to separation between the excepted and that from which it is excepted by many sentences.
His saying: {ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنقُصُوكُمْ شَيْئاً}: The majority read «يَنْقُصوكم» with the undotted ṣād, which takes one object or two. Both are possible here: «كُمْ» is an object and «شيئاً» is either a second object or a maṣdar, that is: "anything of diminution," or "neither little nor much of diminution." ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib al-Kūfī, ʿIkrima, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Abū Zayd read «يَنْقُضوكم» with the dotted ḍād, which is on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: "break your covenant," the muḍāf being omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. Al-Kirmānī said: "It fits the mention of the covenant," that is: breaking matches the covenant. It is close to the reading of the majority, for whoever breaks the covenant has diminished the term; but the reading of the majority is more apt because of its contrast with completion.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الأشهر}: The alif-lām may be one of reference (ʿahd), the months meant being those mentioned earlier in His saying {فَسِيحُواْ فِي الأرض أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ}. When the Arabs mention an indefinite and then wish to mention it a second time, they bring its pronoun or its word defined by «أل», and it is not permissible then to describe it by a description suggesting difference. If it were said «رأيت رجلاً فأكرَمْتُ الرجلَ الطويل» ("I saw a man and honoured the tall man"), you would not mean by the second the first; but if you describe it with what does not imply difference, it is allowed, as in your saying «فأكرمت الرجل المذكور» ("I honoured the man mentioned"). This verse is of that kind, for «الأشهر» has been described as sacred (ḥurum), which is a description understood from the drift of the speech, so it does not imply difference. It may also be that something other than the months mentioned earlier is meant, in which case «أل» is not for reference; both views are reported in the exegesis.
The "stripping off" (insilākh) here is among the finest metaphors, and Abū l-Haytham explained it, saying: "One says «أَهْلَلْنا شهرَ كذا», that is: we entered it; each night of it, until half of it has passed, we increase in garment, then we strip it off ourselves piece by piece until it ends and is stripped away." And he recited:
2448 - إذا ما سَلَخْتُ الشهرَ أَهْلَلْتُ مثلَه ... كفى قاتِلاً سَلْخي الشهورَ وإهلالي
(When I have stripped away a month I enter another like it; my stripping away months and entering them suffices as a killer.)
His saying: {كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ}: There are two views on its being accusative. The first is that it is accusative as an adverbial of place. Al-Zajjāj said: "like «ذهبت مذهباً»." Al-Fārisī rejected this view of his, because it is a specific adverbial of place, and a specific place is not reached by the verb directly but by means of «في», as in «صَلَّيْتُ في الطريق» and «في البيت»; it is reached directly only in a limited set of words, some of which are regular and some only heard. He made this a parallel to what Sībawayh did in the verse of Sāʿida:
2449 - لَدْنٌ بهَزِّ الكفِّ يَعْسِلُ مَتْنُهُ ... فيه كما عَسَل الطريقَ الثعلبُ
(Supple when the hand shakes it, its shaft quivering in it as the fox runs along the road.)
namely that he made it one from which the preposition was omitted by latitude, not an adverbial, because it is a specific adverbial of place.
The Shaykh said: "It is accusative as an adverbial, because the meaning of «واقعدوا» is not literally to sit, but rather: lie in wait for them. If so, the governing word and the adverbial agree in root, and whenever they agree in root, in form or meaning, the verb reaches it directly. You say «جلست مجلسَ القاضي» and «قعدت مجلسَ القاضي», and the verse is of that kind."
The second is that it is accusative by the omission of the preposition, which is «على», that is: «على كلِّ مَرْصَد». This is the view of al-Akhfash, who made it like the saying of the other:
2450 - تَحِنُّ فَتُبْدِي ما بها مِنْ صَبابةٍ ... وأُخْفي الذي لولا الأسى لقَضَاني
(She yearns and shows what she has of passion, and I conceal what, but for grief, would have killed me.)
This is not regular but limited to what has been heard, as in the saying of the Exalted: {لأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ}, that is: «على صراطك»; all agreed that it is on the supposition of «على». Some said it is on the supposition of the bāʾ, that is: «بكل مرصد»; Abū l-Baqāʾ reported it. In that case the bāʾ would have the meaning of «في», so «في» should be supplied, because the meaning rests on it; and he made it parallel to the poet's saying:
2451 - نُغالي اللحمَ للأضيافِ نَيْئاً ... ونَرْخُصُهُ إذا نَضِجَ القدورُ
(We prize the meat for the guests when raw, and sell it cheap once the pots have cooked.)
Al-marṣad is of the pattern mafʿal, from raṣadahu yarṣuduhu, that is: he watched him; it suits time, place and maṣdar. ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl said:
2452 - ولقد عَلِمْتَ وما إِخالك ناسِيا ... أنَّ المنيَّةَ للفتى بالمَرْصَدِ
(You know — and I do not think you forget — that death lies in wait for the young man.)
Al-mirṣād is the place specific to lying in wait. Al-marṣad applies to the one who watches, whether singular, dual or plural, and likewise to the one watched. His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً} [al-Jinn: 27] can bear all that; it is as if it were originally a maṣdar, hence the singular and masculine is kept in it.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ}: Like His saying {إِن امرؤ هَلَكَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 176], in that it belongs to the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation) according to the majority.
His saying: {حتى يَسْمَعَ}: «حتى» may here be for the limit (ghāya) or for causation (taʿlīl), and on both views it is attached to His saying «فَأَجِرْهُ». Can this issue be an instance of conflict of governors (tanāzuʿ) or not? There is obscurity in it: in meaning it is possible to attach «حتى» to His saying «استجارك» or to «فَأَجِرْهُ», since the implied form could be: "and if anyone seeks your protection until he hears the speech of Allah, protect him until he hears the speech of Allah." The answer is that it is not allowed according to the majority, for a verbal reason of the craft, not a reason of meaning: if we made it a case of tanāzuʿ and gave the operation to the first, say, the second would need it as a pronoun, as established; then it would follow that «حتى» governs the pronoun in the genitive, and «حتى» governs it only in poetic necessity, as in the saying:
2453 - فلا واللَّهِ لا يَلْقَى أُناسٌ ... فتى حَتَّاك يا ابنَ أبي يزيدِ
(No, by Allah, no people will find a youth up to you [ḥattāka], O son of Abū Yazīd.)
As for the one who allows it to govern a pronoun, it is not barred for him, and it would be the operation of the second, by omission of it, like your saying «فرحت ومررت بزيد», that is: «فرحت به»; had it been the operation of the first, you would not omit it from the second.
His saying {كَلاَمَ الله} is of the chapter of annexing the attribute to what it describes, not of annexing the created to the Creator. «مَأْمَنَه» may be a place, that is: the place of his safety, or a maṣdar, that is: "then convey him to his safety."

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَيْفَ يَكُونُ}: There are three views on the khabar of «يكون», the most apparent being that it is «كيف» and «عهدٌ» is its ism; the khabar here must be placed first because it contains what has the head of the sentence, namely the interrogative. On this view «للمشركين» is attached either to «يكون», according to those who allow «كان» to govern an adverbial and its like, or to an omitted word, because it was originally an adjective of «عهد», and when fronted it was made accusative as a ḥāl. «عند» may be attached to «يكون», or to an omitted word as an adjective of «عَهْد», or to «عهد» itself, since it is a maṣdar. The second: that the khabar is «للمشركين»; on this «عند» has the views given earlier. We add a fourth view, that it may be an adverbial of the being-established to which «للمشركين» is attached. The third: that the khabar is «عند الله»; on this «للمشركين» is either an explanation, or attached to «يكون» according to those who allow that as above, or a ḥāl from «عهد», or attached to the being-established to which the khabar is attached. No heed is paid to the fronting of the khabar's object before the ism since it is a preposition. «كيف» on the last two views resembles an adverbial or a ḥāl, as already treated at {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28].
They did not mention a fourth view here, which should have been the most apparent: that "being" is complete (tāmma), meaning: "how can a covenant exist for the polytheists with Allah?" The interrogative here has the meaning of negation, and for that reason the exception with «إلا» follows it. Also from its use in the sense of negation is his saying:
2454 - فهذي سيوفٌ يا صُدَيُّ بنَ مالكٍ ... كثيرٌ ولكن كيف بالسيفِ ضاربُ
(These are swords, O Ṣudayy ibn Mālik, many, but how [is there] one to strike with the sword?)
that is: there is no one striking with the sword.
His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين عَاهَدْتُمْ}: There are two views. The first is that it is a discontinuous exception, that is: "but those with whom you made a covenant, their ruling is thus and thus." The second is that it is continuous, and there are then two possibilities: one, that it is accusative on the basis of the exception from the polytheists; the other, that it is genitive as a badal from them, because the meaning of the preceding interrogative is negation, that is: "there is not for the polytheists a covenant except for those who did not break it." By analogy with Abū l-Baqāʾ's statement earlier, it would be nominative as mubtadaʾ, the sentence «فما استقاموا» being its khabar.
His saying: {فَمَا}: «ما» may be a maṣdar particle of time, in the position of accusative, that is: "so be upright to them for the duration of their uprightness to you." It may be conditional, and then there are two views on its position. One: that it is accusative as an adverbial of time, the implied form being: "at whatever time they are upright to you, be upright to them." Abū l-Baqāʾ compared it to the saying of the Exalted: {مَّا يَفْتَحِ الله لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحْمَةٍ فَلاَ مُمْسِكَ لَهَا} [Fāṭir: 2]. The second: that it is nominative as mubtadaʾ, with the well-known views on the khabar, and «فاستقيموا» is the apodosis. Al-Ḥūfī took this course, and it requires the omission of a returning pronoun, that is: "at whatever time they are upright to you in it, be upright to them." The Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik allowed that the maṣdar «ما» of time may be a conditional jussive-governing one, and recited on it:
2455 - فما تَحْيَ لا نسْأَمْ حياةً وإن تَمُتْ ... فلا خيرَ في الدنيا ولا العيشِ أجمعا
(As long as you live we will not tire of life; and if you die, there is no good in the world or in life at all.)
There is no proof in it, because the apparent sense is conditional without interpreting it as maṣdar and time. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It cannot be negative, for the meaning would be corrupted, since the meaning would become: 'be upright to them because they were not upright to you.'"

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَيْفَ وَإِن يَظْهَرُوا}: The thing asked about is omitted, as the meaning indicates it. Abū l-Baqāʾ supplied: "how can you feel secure," or "how can they have a covenant." Others supplied: "how do you not fight them." The second of Abū l-Baqāʾ's two suppositions is better, because it is of the kind of what came before, so the indication of it is stronger. Omission has often occurred in this construction, and there came earlier His saying, the Exalted: {فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 25] and {فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا} [al-Nisāʾ: 41]. The poet said:
2456 - وخبَّرْ تُماني أنَّما الموتُ بالقُرى ... فكيف وهاتا هَضْبةٌ وكَثِيبُ
(You two told me that death is in the villages; how then, when here are a hill and a dune?)
that is: "how did he die?" And al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
2457 - فكيف ولم أعلَمْهُمُ خَذَلُوكُمْ ... على مُعْظِمٍ ولا أَدِيْمَكُمُ قَدُّوا
(How [can you blame me], when I did not know them to have forsaken you in a grave matter, nor to have cut your hide?)
that is: "how do you blame me for praising them?" The Shaykh said: "Abū l-Baqāʾ supplied the verb after «كيف» as «كيف تطمئنون», and another supplied it as «كيف لا تقاتِلونهم»." I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ did not supply it with this alone, but with it and the preferred view, as I presented from him earlier.
His saying: {وَإِن يَظْهَرُوا}: This conditional sentence is in the position of accusative as ḥāl, that is: "how can they have a covenant when they are in a state contrary to that?" Its treatment was given at His saying {وَإِن يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِّثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 169]. «لا يرقُبوا» is the apodosis of the condition. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «وإن يُظْهَروا» in the passive, from aẓharahu ʿalayhi, that is: He made him prevail over him.
His saying: {إِلاًّ} is the direct object of «يرقُبوا», that is: "they do not observe." About «الإِلّ» the lexicographers have several views. The first: that the covenant is meant. Abū ʿUbayda, Ibn Zayd and al-Suddī said so, and from it comes the poet's saying:
2458 - لولا بنو مالكٍ والإِلُّ مَرْقَبَةٌ ... ومالكٌ فيهمُ الآلاءُ والشَّرَفُ
(Were it not for the sons of Mālik, and the covenant is a watchtower, and Mālik, in whom are the favours and the honour.)
that is: the alliance. Another said:
2459 - وجَدْناهُما كاذِباً إِلُّهُمْ ... وذو الإِلِّ والعهدِ لا يَكْذِبُ
(We found their covenant false, whereas a man of covenant and pledge does not lie.)
and another said:
2460 - أفسدَ الناسَ خُلوفٌ خَلَفُوا ... قطعُوا الإِلَّ وأعراقَ الرَّحِمْ
(The people were corrupted by successors who came after, who cut the covenant and the roots of kinship.)
In the ḥadīth of Umm Zarʿ: «بيت أبي زرع وَفِيُّ الإِلِّ، كريم الخِلّ، بَرودُ الظلّ» ("The house of Abū Zarʿ is faithful to the covenant, generous to the friend, cool in shade"), that is: faithful to the covenant.
The second: that kinship is meant, which is al-Farrāʾ's view, and he recited the verse of Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him:
2461 - لَعَمْرك إنَّ إِلَّكَ مِنْ قريشٍ ... كإِلِّ السَّقْبِ مِنْ رَأْلِ النَّعامِ
(By your life, your kinship to Quraysh is like the kinship of the camel-foal to the ostrich chick.)
Abū ʿUbayda recited on that the saying:
2462 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... قطعوا الإِلَّ وأعراق الرَّحِمْ
(... they cut kinship and the roots of the womb.)
The third: that Allah the Exalted is meant, that is: it is one of His names, and they cited as evidence the ḥadīth of Abū Bakr when the speech of Musaylima, may Allah curse him, was presented to him: «إنَّ هذا الكلام لم يَخْرج من إلّ» ("This speech did not come from an Ill"), that is, Allah, mighty and exalted. Al-Zajjāj did not accept this, saying: "Because His names, the Exalted, are known in the Book and the Sunna, and no one has been heard to say: 'O Ill, do such-and-such for me.'"
The fourth: that al-ill is the jūʾār, which is the raising of the voice at the making of a pact, because when they wiped hands and swore pacts they cried out loudly about it; from it is the saying of Abū Jahl:
2463 - لإِلٍّ علينا واجبٍ لا نُضِيعُه ... متينٍ قُواه غيرِ منتكثِ الحبلِ
(For a pledge incumbent upon us which we will not waste, its strands firm, its rope unbroken.)
The fifth: that it is from «ألَّ البرقُ», that is, it flashed. Al-Azharī said: "Al-alīl is the gleam; one says alla yaullu, that is: it was clear and shone." It was also said that al-ill is from sharpening, and from it comes al-alla, the spear, because of its sharpness.
