Some set between these meanings a common measure to which all I have mentioned to you returns. Al-Zajjāj said: "The reality of al-ill, in my view, as the language indicates, is the sharpening of a thing. From that: al-alla, the spear, and uzun muʾallala (a pointed ear); al-ill extends over everything explained of covenant, kinship and jūʾār from this, so if you say of a covenant «بينهما إلٌّ», its sense is that they have sharpened [their resolve] in taking covenants, and likewise for jūʾār and kinship." Al-Rāghib said: "Al-ill: every apparent state of covenant, alliance and kinship that gleams (taillu); alla al-faras: the horse sped; al-alla: the gleaming spear." Another recited on that the saying of Ḥimās ibn Qays on the day of the conquest of Mecca:
2464 - إن يُقْبلوا اليومَ فما لي عِلَّةْ ... هذا سلاحٌ كاملٌ وأَلَّةْ
وذو غِرارَيْنِ سَريعُ السَّلَّةُ
(If they come on today, I have no excuse: here is complete armour and a spear, and a double-edged sword quick to draw.)
He said: "It was said that al-ill and al-īl are two names of Allah the Exalted, but that is not correct; and the two alalān are the two sides of the knife." End of quotation. The plural of al-ill in the small number is allun, the original being aʾlul on the pattern afʿul (like aflus); the second hamza was replaced by alif because it is sākin after another with fatḥa, and the lām was assimilated into the lām. In the large number it is ilāl, like dhiʾb and dhiʾāb. Al-all with fatḥa was said to be extreme despair. Al-Harawī said, on the ḥadīth «عَجب ربكم مِنْ ألِّكم وقُنوطكم» ("Your Lord marvelled at your all and your despair"), Abū ʿUbayd said: "The ḥadīth scholars say it with kasra on the hamza, but what is preserved with us is the fatḥa, and it is more like the maṣdars, as if He meant 'at the intensity of your despair.' It may be from raising the voice; one says alla yaullu allan, alalan and alīlan, when he raised his voice in weeping, and from it one says: 'to him belong woe and alīl,' and from it is the saying of al-Kumayt:
2465 - وأنتَ ما أنت في غَبْراءَ مُظْلمةٍ ... إذا دَعَتْ أَلَلَيْها الكاعِبُ الفُضُلُ
(And you, what are you, in a dusty, dark [year], when the plump girl calls out her cries?)
End of quotation. A group read «ألاًّ» with fatḥa, and it is as he mentioned, a maṣdar of alla yaullu, when he made a covenant. ʿIkrima read «إيلاً» with kasra on the hamza followed by a sākin yāʾ, with three views. The first: that it is a name of Allah the Exalted; what was said earlier of Jibrīl and Isrāʾīl supports that, that the meaning is "servant of Allah." The second: that it may be derived from āla yaʾūlu when it came to the end of the matter, or from āla yaʾūlu when he managed, as Ibn Jinnī said, that is: "they do not observe in you management or conciliation." On both suppositions the wāw became sākin after a kasra and was turned into yāʾ, like rīḥ. The third: that it is the doubled al-ill, but the doubling was found heavy and one of the two was replaced by a weak letter, as they say amlaytu l-kitāb and amlaltuhu. The poet said:
2466 - يا ليتَما أمُّنا شالَتْ نَعَمَتُها ... أَيْما إلى جنةٍ أَيْما إلى نارِ
(Would that our mother had had her ostrich-hen lifted, either to a garden or to a fire.)
His saying: {وَلاَ ذِمَّةً}: Al-dhimma was said to be the covenant, so it is among the things repeated for difference of wording, if we say that al-ill is also the covenant; it is like His saying, the Exalted: {صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِم وَرَحْمَةٌ} [al-Baqara: 157], and his saying:
2467 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وألفى قولَها كَذِباً ومَيْنا
(... and he found her words a lie and falsehood.)
and his saying:
2468 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وهندٌ أتى مِنْ دونِها النَّأْيُ والبعدُ
(... and Hind, between whom and us came remoteness and distance.)
It was said: al-dhimma is guarantee (ḍamān); one says «هو في ذمَّتي» that is: in my guarantee, and from it the people of the dhimma (ahl al-dhimma) were named, for their entering into the guarantee of the Muslims; and one says «له عليَّ ذِمَّةٌ وذِمام ومَذَمَّة، وهي الذِّمُّ». Ibn ʿArafa said that and recited from Usāma ibn al-Ḥārith:
2469 - يُصَيِّح بالأَْسْحار في كل صَارَة ... كما ناشد الذِّمَّ الكفيلَ المعاهِدُ
(He cries out at the pre-dawn hours in every tract, as the covenanter adjures the guarantor by the dhimm.)
Al-Rāghib said: "Al-dhimām is that for the squandering of which a man is blamed (yudhammu), of covenant; likewise al-dhimma, al-madhamma and al-madhimma" — meaning with fatḥa and kasra — and it is said: «لي مَذَمَّةٌ فلا تَهْتكها». Another said: "It is called dhimma because every inviolability whose waste makes blame (dhamm) necessary for you is called dhimma," and it is pluralised as dhimm, as in his saying:
2470 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما ناشد الذِّمَّ. . . . . . . . . . .
(... as he adjured by the dhimm ...)
and as dhimam and dhimām. Abū Zayd said: "Madhimma with kasra is from al-dhimām and with fatḥa from al-dhamm." Al-Azharī said: "Al-dhimma: security (amān)," and in the ḥadīth: «ويَسْعى بذمَّتِهم أَدْناهم» ("The least of them strives on their behalf by their pledge"). Abū ʿUbayd said: "Al-dhimma here is security; he says: when the humblest of people gives security to a disbeliever, it takes effect upon them; for that reason ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, permitted the security of a slave on the entire army." Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "Al-dhimma: that which must be guarded and protected."
His saying: {يُرْضُونَكُم}: There are two views. One: that it is resumptive, which is the apparent view; He informed that their state is so. The second: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the subject of «لا يَرْقُبوا». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is nothing, because after their prevailing they do not please the believers."
His saying: {وتأبى}: One says abā yabā ibāʾan, that is: his refusal became intense; so every ibāʾ is refusal, but not the reverse. He said:
2471 - أبى الله إلا عَدْلَه ووفاءَه ... فلا النكرُ معروفٌ ولا العُرْفُ ضائعُ
(Allah refuses anything but His justice and His fidelity, so evil is not made good, nor is good wasted.)
and another said:
2472 - أبى الضيمَ والنعمانُ يَحْرقُ نابَه ... عليه فَأَفْضى والسيوفُ مَعَاقِلُهْ
(He refused humiliation while al-Nuʿmān gnashed his tooth against him; so he went out, his refuges being swords.)
So whoever explained it as mere refusal is not correct. The imperfect of it on yafʿal with fatḥa on the ʿayn is irregular, and likewise qalā yaqlā in one dialect.
